1.1.e: Now henceforth we shall declare the Pakayagnas.

1.1.s: abhisamāvartsyamāno yatra antyām samidham abhyādadhyāt tam agnim indhīta |
1.1.d: अभिसमावर्त्स्यमानो यत्र अन्त्याम् समिधम् अभ्यादध्यात् तम् अग्निम् इन्धीत ।
1.1.e: When (a pupil) is going to return (from his teacher), let him keep that fire (as his domestic fire) on which he has put the last piece of wood (as required by the regulations for a student),
Or (he should keep) his nuptial fire.
Some declare (that the domestic fire should be kindled) at the time of the division of the inheritance.
Or that after the death of the householder the eldest one himself (should kindle it).
(It should be kindled) on the day of the new moon of the month of Vaisakha or on another (new moon day).
Some say (that the fire should be kindled) according to the (sacrificer's) wishes under the (corresponding) constellation.

1.1.s: puru paśu viṭ kula ambarīṣa bahu yājinām anyatamasmād agnim indīta |
1.1.d: पुरु पशु विट् कुल अम्बरीष बहु याजिनाम् अन्यतमस्माद् अग्निम् इन्दीत ।
1.1.e: He should light his fire at one of the following places, viz. in the house of a Vaisya who is rich in cattle, at a frying-pan, or (at the fire of) one who offers many sacrifices.
Some say that (the fire should be fetched from one of the above-mentioned places) in the evening and in the morning.

1.1.s: sāyam āhuti saṃskāro adhvaryu pratyaya iti ācāryāḥ |
1.1.d: सायम् आहुति संस्कारो अध्वर्यु प्रत्यय इति आचार्याः ।
1.1.e: The inauguration (of the fire) by an evening offering should be learnt from the Adhvaryus, according to (my) teacher.

1.1.s: prātaḥ pūrṇa āhutim juhuyād vaiṣṇavyā ṛcā tūṣṇīm vā |
1.1.d: प्रातः पूर्ण आहुतिम् जुहुयाद् वैष्णव्या ऋचा तूष्णीम् वा ।
1.1.e: In the morning he shall offer a full oblation with a verse sacred to Vishnu, or silently.

1.1.s: tasya prāduṣ karaṇa havana kālāv agni hotreṇa vyākyātau |
1.1.d: तस्य प्रादुष् करण हवन कालाव् अग्नि होत्रेण व्याक्यातौ ।
1.1.e: The time for setting it (i.e. the domestic fire) in a blaze and for sacrificing on it has been explained by (the rules given with regard to) the Agnihotra.

1.1.s: yajña upavītī ity ādi ca sambhavat sarvam kalpa ekatvāt |
1.1.d: यज्ञ उपवीती इत्य् आदि च सम्भवत् सर्वम् कल्प एकत्वात् ।
1.1.e: And 'invested with the sacrificial cord,' &c., all these rules, as far as they are applicable, should be applied (here also) in consequence of the unity of the ritual.
With regard to this they quote also (the following Sloka):

1.1.s: pāka saṃsthā haviḥ saṃsthāḥ soma saṃsthās tathā aparāḥ | ekaviṃśatir ity etā yajña saṃsthāḥ prakīrtitāḥ |
1.1.d: पाक संस्था हविः संस्थाः सोम संस्थास् तथा अपराः । एकविंशतिर् इत्य् एता यज्ञ संस्थाः प्रकीर्तिताः ।
1.1.e: 'The kinds of Pakayagnas, the kinds of Haviryagnas, and again the kinds of Soma sacrifices, 'Twenty-one by number, these are proclaimed to be the kinds of sacrifice.'

1.2.e: At the end of the sacrificial acts (follows) the distribution of food to Brahmanas.

1.2.s: vāg rūpa vayaḥ śruta śīla vṛttāni guṇāḥ |
1.2.d: वाग् रूप वयः श्रुत शील वृत्तानि गुणाः ।
1.2.e: Voice, (pleasantness of) form, age, learning, moral character, (right) conduct are the qualities (required in the Brahmanas who are to be invited thereto).
A learned one should not be passed over.

1.2.s: adhidaivam atha adhyātmam adhiyajñam iti trayam | mantreṣu brāhmaṇe caiva śrutam ity abhidhīyate |
1.2.d: अधिदैवम् अथ अध्यात्मम् अधियज्ञम् इति त्रयम् । मन्त्रेषु ब्राह्मणे चैव श्रुतम् इत्य् अभिधीयते ।
1.2.e: 'The threefold (knowledge, viz. that) which refers to the deities, that which refers to the Atman, and that which refers to sacrifice, '(Handed down) in the Mantras and in the Brahmana: this is called learning.

1.2.s: kriyāvantam adhīyānam śruta vṛddham tapasvinam | bhojayet tam sasṛd yas tu na tam bhūyaḥ kṣud aśnute |
1.2.d: क्रियावन्तम् अधीयानम् श्रुत वृद्धम् तपस्विनम् । भोजयेत् तम् ससृद् यस् तु न तम् भूयः क्षुद् अश्नुते ।
1.2.e: 'A performer of the sacred rights, a man who has studied (the Veda), who is old in learning and devoted to austerities: 'He who gives food (even) once to such (a Brahmana), hunger will not befall that man any more.

1.2.s: yām titarpayiṣet kāṃcid devatām sarva karmasu | tasyā uddiśya manasā dadyād evam vidhāya vai |
1.2.d: याम् तितर्पयिषेत् कांचिद् देवताम् सर्व कर्मसु । तस्या उद्दिश्य मनसा दद्याद् एवम् विधाय वै ।
1.2.e: 'Whatsoever deity he may wish to satiate at any sacrifice, 'Destining it to that (deity) in his mind, he shall give (the food) to a person like that.

1.2.s: na evam vidhe havir nyastam na gacched devatām kvacit | nidhir eṣa manuṣyāṇām devānām pātram ucyate |
1.2.d: न एवम् विधे हविर् न्यस्तम् न गच्छेद् देवताम् क्वचित् । निधिर् एष मनुष्याणाम् देवानाम् पात्रम् उच्यते ।
1.2.e: 'An oblation deposited in a person like that will never miss its way to the deity; 'Treasure of men, vessel of gods (in which they receive what is given to them) he is called.'

1.3.e: Now (follow) the ceremonies of the days of the new and full moon. He fasts.

1.3.s: prātar yatra etan mahā vṛkṣa agrāṇi sūrya ātapati sa homa kālaḥ svastyayanatamaḥ sarvāsām āvṛtām anyatra nirdeśāt |
1.3.d: प्रातर् यत्र एतन् महा वृक्ष अग्राणि सूर्य आतपति स होम कालः स्वस्त्ययनतमः सर्वासाम् आवृताम् अन्यत्र निर्देशात् ।
1.3.e: In the morning, when the sun shines on the top of the great trees, that is the most auspicious time for all kinds of sacrifices, unless there be a special rule.

1.3.s: sumanāḥ śuciḥ śucau varūthya deśe pūrṇa vidhanam carum śrapayitvā darśa pūrṇa māsa devatābhyo yathā vibhāgam sthālī pākasya juhoti |
1.3.d: सुमनाः शुचिः शुचौ वरूथ्य देशे पूर्ण विधनम् चरुम् श्रपयित्वा दर्श पूर्ण मास देवताभ्यो यथा विभागम् स्थाली पाकस्य जुहोति ।
1.3.e: With a genial mind, clean, on a pure, protected spot, having cooked a full, thin mess of rice, he offers that cooked oblation to the deities of the festivals of the new and full moon, distributing it in the due way.

1.3.s: sthālī pākeṣu ca grahaṇa āsādana prokṣaṇāni mantra devatābhyaḥ |
1.3.d: स्थाली पाकेषु च ग्रहण आसादन प्रोक्षणानि मन्त्र देवताभ्यः ।
1.3.e: In the oblations of cooked food the acts of taking (the intended oblation), of putting it down (near the fire), and of sprinkling it (with water) are performed with regard to the deities of the (respective) Mantras.
And the rules about the portions to be cut off (from the sacrificial food, are valid).

1.3.s: pūrvam tu darśa pūrṇa māsābhyām anvārambhaṇīya devatābhyo juhuyāt |
1.3.d: पूर्वम् तु दर्श पूर्ण मासाभ्याम् अन्वारम्भणीय देवताभ्यो जुहुयात् ।
1.3.e: But before the sacrifices of the new and full moon one should make offerings to the deities of the Anvarambhaniya ceremony.

1.3.s: ā paurṇamāsād darśasya anatītaḥ kālaḥ ā darśāt paurṇamāsasya |
1.3.d: आ पौर्णमासाद् दर्शस्य अनतीतः कालः आ दर्शात् पौर्णमासस्य ।
1.3.e: The time for the new moon sacrifice is not elapsed until the full moon, nor that for the full moon sacrifice until the new moon.

1.3.s: prātar āhutim ca eke sāyam āhuti kāle atyayān manyante |
1.3.d: प्रातर् आहुतिम् च एके सायम् आहुति काले अत्ययान् मन्यन्ते ।
1.3.e: And some say that the morning oblation may be made at the time of the evening oblation, in the case of danger.

1.3.s: niyatas tv eva kālo agni hotre prāyaś citta darśanād bhinna kālasya |
1.3.d: नियतस् त्व् एव कालो अग्नि होत्रे प्रायश् चित्त दर्शनाद् भिन्न कालस्य ।
1.3.e: But the time is fixed, as at the Agnihotra an expiation has been prescribed for him who has neglected the time.

1.3.s: nitya āhutyor vrīhi yava taṇḍulānām anyatamadd haviḥ kurvīta |
1.3.d: नित्य आहुत्योर् व्रीहि यव तण्डुलानाम् अन्यतमद्द् हविः कुर्वीत ।
1.3.e: At the two daily oblations one should use as sacrificial food either rice or barley or grains.
In case these are not at hand, other (sorts of sacrificial food are) not prohibited.
Some say that if he uses grains, he should wash them.
With the other (kinds of food) no such preparation takes place.
In the evening (he makes the oblation) to Agni, in the morning to Surya,
And after both silently to Pragapati.
Some (say that) before the first oblation a piece of wood (is to be put on the fire).
The sprinkling with water as indicated (in the Srauta-sutra).

1.4.s: utthāya prātar ācamya ahar ahaḥ svādhyāyam adhīyīta |
1.4.d: उत्थाय प्रातर् आचम्य अहर् अहः स्वाध्यायम् अधीयीत ।
1.4.e: When he has risen in the morning and has sipped water, let him daily repeat his recital.

1.4.s: adyā no deva savitar dve apehi manasas pata iti sūktam ṛtam ca satyam ca iti sūktam ādityā ava hi khyata iti sūkta śeṣaḥ indra śreṣṭhāni iti ekā haṃsaḥ śuciṣad iti ekā namo mahadbhya iti ekā yata indra bhayāmaha iti ekā adha svapnasya iti ekā yo me rājann iti ekā mama agne varca iti sūktam svasti no mimītām iti ca pañca |
1.4.d: अद्या नो देव सवितर् द्वे अपेहि मनसस् पत इति सूक्तम् ऋतम् च सत्यम् च इति सूक्तम् आदित्या अव हि ख्यत इति सूक्त शेषः इन्द्र श्रेष्ठानि इति एका हंसः शुचिषद् इति एका नमो महद्भ्य इति एका यत इन्द्र भयामह इति एका अध स्वप्नस्य इति एका यो मे राजन्न् इति एका मम अग्ने वर्च इति सूक्तम् स्वस्ति नो मिमीताम् इति च पञ्च ।
1.4.e: (This consists of, or is accompanied by, the following texts:) the two verses, 'To-day, god Savitar' (Rig-veda V, 82, 4-5); the hymn, 'Go away, Manasaspati' (X, 164); the hymn, 'Right and truth' (X, 190); the verses, 'Look down, ye Adityas,' to the end of the hymn (VIII, 47, 11-18); the verse, 'O Indra, the best treasures' (II, 21, 6); the verse, 'The swan dwelling in purity' (IV, 40, 5); the verse, 'Adoration to the great ones' (I, 27, 13); the verse, 'What we fear, Indra' (VIII, 50, 13); the verse, 'And of the sleep' (I, 120, 12); the verse, 'He who says to me, O king' (II, 28, 10); the hymn, 'Let glory be mine, Agni' (X, 128); and the five verses,' Bliss may create for us' (V, 51, 11 seq.).

1.5.s: catvāraḥ pāka yajñā huto ahutaḥ prahutaḥ prāśita iti |
1.5.d: चत्वारः पाक यज्ञा हुतो अहुतः प्रहुतः प्राशित इति ।
1.5.e: There are four kinds of Pakayagnas, viz. the HUTA, the AHUTA, the PRAHUTA, and the PRASITA.

1.5.s: pañcasu bahiḥ śālāyām vivāhe cūḍā karaṇa upanayane keśa ante sīmanta unnayana iti |
1.5.d: पञ्चसु बहिः शालायाम् विवाहे चूडा करण उपनयने केश अन्ते सीमन्त उन्नयन इति ।
1.5.e: On the following five occasions, viz. the wedding, the tonsure (of the child's head), the initiation (of the Brahmakarin), the cutting of the beard, and the parting of the hair, (on these occasions) in the outer hall--
To a place that has been smeared (with cow-dung), which is elevated, and which has been sprinkled (with water), he carries forward the fire,
Having kindled it by rubbing, according to some teachers, at his marriage.

1.5.s: udag ayana āpūrya māṇa pakṣe puṇya ahe kumāryai pāṇim gṛhṇīyāt |
1.5.d: उदग् अयन आपूर्य माण पक्षे पुण्य अहे कुमार्यै पाणिम् गृह्णीयात् ।
1.5.e: During the northern course of the sun, in the time of the increasing moon, on an auspicious day he shall seize the hand of a girl,

1.5.s: āvartāv api yasyai syātām pradakṣiṇau grīvāyām |
1.5.d: आवर्ताव् अपि यस्यै स्याताम् प्रदक्षिणौ ग्रीवायाम् ।
1.5.e: Who should also have at her neck two curls turned to the right.
(Of such a girl) he shall know that she will give birth to six men.

1.6.s: jāyām upagrahīṣyamāṇo anṛkṣarā iti varakān gacchato anumantrayate |
1.6.d: जायाम् उपग्रहीष्यमाणो अनृक्षरा इति वरकान् गच्छतो अनुमन्त्रयते ।
1.6.e: If he will acquire a wife, let him recite over the wooers (whom he sends to the girl's father) when they go away, the verse, 'Thornless' (Rig-veda X, 85, 23).

1.6.s: abhigamane puṣpa phala yavān ādāya uda kumbhaś ca |
1.6.d: अभिगमने पुष्प फल यवान् आदाय उद कुम्भश् च ।
1.6.e: When they arrive, they take flowers, fruits, barley, and a pot of water.

1.6.s: ayam aham bho iti triḥ procya |
1.6.d: अयम् अहम् भो इति त्रिः प्रोच्य ।
1.6.e: They say thrice, 'Here I am, sir!'

1.6.s: udite prān mukhā gṛhyāḥ pratyan mukhā āvahamānā gotra nāmāny anukīrtayantaḥ kanyām varayanti |
1.6.d: उदिते प्रान् मुखा गृह्याः प्रत्यन् मुखा आवहमाना गोत्र नामान्य् अनुकीर्तयन्तः कन्याम् वरयन्ति ।
1.6.e: When these words have been uttered, they ask the girl in marriage, reciting the clan names, the dwellers turning their faces to the east, the visitors to the west.

1.6.s: ubhayato rucite pūrṇa pātrīm abhimṛśanti puṣpa akṣata yava hiraṇya miśrām anādhṛṣṭam asya anādhṛṣṭyam devānām ojo anabhiśasty abhiśastipā anabhiśaste anyam añjasā satyam upa geṣam suvite mā dhā iti |
1.6.d: उभयतो रुचिते पूर्ण पात्रीम् अभिमृशन्ति पुष्प अक्षत यव हिरण्य मिश्राम् अनाधृष्टम् अस्य अनाधृष्ट्यम् देवानाम् ओजो अनभिशस्त्य् अभिशस्तिपा अनभिशस्ते अन्यम् अञ्जसा सत्यम् उप गेषम् सुविते मा धा इति ।
1.6.e: When the matter pleases both sides, let them touch a full vessel into which have been put flowers, fried grain, fruits, barley, and gold, and let them recite (the formula), 'Undisturbed art thou, the undisturbable vigour of the gods, not cursed, protecting against a curse, unexposed to a curse. Might I straightway attain to truth. Put me into prosperity.'

1.6.s: ā naḥ prajām iti tvayi kanyāyā ācārya utthāya mūrdhani karoti prajām tvayi dadhāmi paśūṃs tvayi dadhāmi tejo brahma varcasam tvayi dadhāmi iti |
1.6.d: आ नः प्रजाम् इति त्वयि कन्याया आचार्य उत्थाय मूर्धनि करोति प्रजाम् त्वयि दधामि पशूंस् त्वयि दधामि तेजो ब्रह्म वर्चसम् त्वयि दधामि इति ।
1.6.e: With the verse, 'Offspring may produce us' (Rig-veda X, 85, 43), the Akarya of the girl's (family), standing up, places (the vessel) on her head (saying), 'Offspring I put into thee, cattle I put into thee, splendour and holy lustre I put into thee.'

1.7.e: The northern one, if the rites belong to the gods,
Or rather the east (itself) according to some (teachers).
He draws in the middle (of the sacrificial ground) a line from south to north,

1.7.s: tasyai dakṣiṇata upariṣṭād ūrdhvām ekām madhya ekām uttarata ekām |
1.7.d: तस्यै दक्षिणत उपरिष्टाद् ऊर्ध्वाम् एकाम् मध्य एकाम् उत्तरत एकाम् ।
1.7.e: Upwards from this, turned upwards, to the south one line, in the middle one, to the north one.

1.7.s: agnim pra ṇayāmi manasā śivena ayam astu saṃgamano vasūnām | mā no hiṃsīḥ sthaviram mā kumāram śam no bhava dvipade śam catuṣpade ity agnim praṇīya |
1.7.d: अग्निम् प्र णयामि मनसा शिवेन अयम् अस्तु संगमनो वसूनाम् । मा नो हिंसीः स्थविरम् मा कुमारम् शम् नो भव द्विपदे शम् चतुष्पदे इत्य् अग्निम् प्रणीय ।
1.7.e: Carries forward the fire with the verse, 'I carry forward Agni with genial mind; may he be the assembler of goods. Do no harm to us, to the old nor to the young; be a saviour to us, to men and animals,'

1.7.s: pradakṣimam agneḥ samantāt pāṇinā sa udakena triḥ pramārṣṭi tat samūhanam ity ācakṣate |
1.7.d: प्रदक्षिमम् अग्नेः समन्तात् पाणिना स उदकेन त्रिः प्रमार्ष्टि तत् समूहनम् इत्य् आचक्षते ।
1.7.e: Then he wipes with his wet hand three times around the fire, turning his right side to it. This they call SAMUHANA (sweeping together).
Once, turning his left side to it, in the rites belonging to the Manes.

1.8.e: Now (follows) the strewing (of grass) around (the fire).

1.8.s: prāg agraiḥ kuśaiḥ paristṛṇāti trivṛt pañcavṛd vā |
1.8.d: प्राग् अग्रैः कुशैः परिस्तृणाति त्रिवृत् पञ्चवृद् वा ।
1.8.e: He strews eastward-pointed Kusa grass around it, in three layers or in five layers,

1.8.s: purastāt prathamam atha paścād atha paścāt |
1.8.d: पुरस्तात् प्रथमम् अथ पश्चाद् अथ पश्चात् ।
1.8.e: Beginning on the east side, then to the west, then to the west.
He covers the roots (of the grass-blades) with the points.

1.8.s: sarvāś ca āvṛto dakṣiṇataḥ pravṛttaya udak saṃsthā bhavanti |
1.8.d: सर्वाश् च आवृतो दक्षिणतः प्रवृत्तय उदक् संस्था भवन्ति ।
1.8.e: And all kinds of rites are to be performed beginning south, ending north.

1.8.s: dakṣiṇato brahmāṇam pratiṣṭhāpya bhūr bhuvaḥ svar iti |
1.8.d: दक्षिणतो ब्रह्माणम् प्रतिष्ठाप्य भूर् भुवः स्वर् इति ।
1.8.e: He places the Brahman south with the words, BHUR BHUVAH SVAH,
Adorns him with flowers,

1.8.s: uttarataḥ praṇītāḥ praṇīya ko vaḥ praṇayati iti |
1.8.d: उत्तरतः प्रणीताः प्रणीय को वः प्रणयति इति ।
1.8.e: Carries forward on the north side the Pranita waters with the words, 'Who carries ye forward?'--
Takes up with the left hand the Kusa blades, and arranges them (on the ground) with the right hand,
Bending his right knee,
The left when worshipping the Manes.
The strewing around (of the grass) is not necessary in the Agya offerings,
Nor in the standing offerings, according to Mandukeya.

1.8.s: kuśa taruṇe aviṣame avicchinna agre ananvar garbhe prādeśena māpayitvā kuśena chinatti pavitre stha iti |
1.8.d: कुश तरुणे अविषमे अविच्छिन्न अग्रे अनन्वर् गर्भे प्रादेशेन मापयित्वा कुशेन छिनत्ति पवित्रे स्थ इति ।
1.8.e: He now measures off with the span (of his hand) two Kusa blades, which are not unequal, with unbroken points, bearing no young shoots in them, and severs them (from their roots) with a Kusa blade, saying, 'Purifiers are ye.'
There are two or three (of these Kusa strainers).

1.8.s: prāg agre dhārayan vaiṣṇavyāv iti abhyukṣya |
1.8.d: प्राग् अग्रे धारयन् वैष्णव्याव् इति अभ्युक्ष्य ।
1.8.e: He holds them with their points to the east and sprinkles them (with water, saying), 'Belonging to Vishnu.'

1.8.s: kuśa taruṇābhyām pradakṣiṇam agnim triḥ paryukṣya |
1.8.d: कुश तरुणाभ्याम् प्रदक्षिणम् अग्निम् त्रिः पर्युक्ष्य ।
1.8.e: With the two Kusa blades he sprinkles (water) around the fire three times, keeping his right side turned towards it,

1.8.s: mahīnām payo asi iti ājya sthālīm ādāya |
1.8.d: महीनाम् पयो असि इति आज्य स्थालीम् आदाय ।
1.8.e: Takes up the Agya pot with the words, 'Milk of the cows art thou;'
Puts it on the fire with the words, 'For sap thee;'
Takes it from the fire towards the north with the words, 'For juice thee;'

1.8.s: udag agre pavitre dhārayann aṅguṣṭhābhyām ca upakaniṣṭhikābhyām ca ubhayataḥ pratigṛhya ūrdhva agre prahve kṛtvā ājye pratyasyati | savituṣ ṭvā prasava utpunāmy acchidreṇa pavitreṇa vasoḥ sūryasya raśmibhir iti |
1.8.d: उदग् अग्रे पवित्रे धारयन्न् अङ्गुष्ठाभ्याम् च उपकनिष्ठिकाभ्याम् च उभयतः प्रतिगृह्य ऊर्ध्व अग्रे प्रह्वे कृत्वा आज्ये प्रत्यस्यति । सवितुष् ट्वा प्रसव उत्पुनाम्य् अच्छिद्रेण पवित्रेण वसोः सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिर् इति ।
1.8.e: And holding the two (Kusa) strainers with their points to the north, seizing them on both sides with his two thumbs and fourth fingers, he bends them down, the points upwards, and dips them into the Agya with the words, 'By the impulse of Savitar I purify thee with this uninjured purifier, with the rays of the good sun.'
(This) preparation of the Agya (takes place) each time.
Let him not offer (Agya) which has not been (thus) prepared.

1.8.s: sruve ca apaḥ savitur va iti |
1.8.d: स्रुवे च अपः सवितुर् व इति ।
1.8.e: Also the waters in the Sruva spoon (he purifies) with the words, '(By the impulse) of Savitar (I purify) you.'
This (is called) the PRANITA and the PROKSHANI water.

1.9.e: The Sruva spoon (serves as) a vessel.
According to the purpose the properties (of the different things to be used at each oblation) should be chosen.

1.9.s: savyena kuśān ādāya dakṣiṇena mūle sruvam viṣṇor hasto asi iti |
1.9.d: सव्येन कुशान् आदाय दक्षिणेन मूले स्रुवम् विष्णोर् हस्तो असि इति ।
1.9.e: Taking up Kusa blades with the left, and the [paragraph continues] Sruva at its bottom with the right hand, with the words, 'The hand of Vishnu art thou'--
He offers with the Sruva the Agya oblations.

1.9.s: uttara paśca ardhād agner ārabhya avicchinnam dakṣiṇato juhoti tvam agne pramatir iti |
1.9.d: उत्तर पश्च अर्धाद् अग्नेर् आरभ्य अविच्छिन्नम् दक्षिणतो जुहोति त्वम् अग्ने प्रमतिर् इति ।
1.9.e: Beginning from the north-west side of the fire he offers (the Agya) unintermittingly on the south side (of the fire) with (the verse), 'Thou Agni art full of foresight' (Rig-veda I, 31, 10).

1.9.s: dakṣiṇa paśca ardhād agner ārabhya avicchinnam uttarato juhoti yasya ime himavanta iti |
1.9.d: दक्षिण पश्च अर्धाद् अग्नेर् आरभ्य अविच्छिन्नम् उत्तरतो जुहोति यस्य इमे हिमवन्त इति ।
1.9.e: Beginning from the south-west side of the fire he unintermittingly offers on the north side with (the verse), 'To whom these snowy mountains' (Rig-veda X, 121, 4).

1.9.s: āgneyam uttaram ājya bhāgam saumyam dakṣiṇam |
1.9.d: आग्नेयम् उत्तरम् आज्य भागम् सौम्यम् दक्षिणम् ।
1.9.e: To Agni belongs the northern Agya portion, to Soma the southern.
In the middle (are made) the other oblations,

1.9.s: agnir janitā sa me amūm jāyām dadātu svāhā | somo janimānt sa mā amuyā janimantam karotu svāhā | pūṣā jñātimānt sa mā amuṣyai pitrā mātrā bhrātṛbhir jñātimantam karotu svāhā iti |
1.9.d: अग्निर् जनिता स मे अमूम् जायाम् ददातु स्वाहा । सोमो जनिमान्त् स मा अमुया जनिमन्तम् करोतु स्वाहा । पूषा ज्ञातिमान्त् स मा अमुष्यै पित्रा मात्रा भ्रातृभिर् ज्ञातिमन्तम् करोतु स्वाहा इति ।
1.9.e: (With the words,) 'Agni is the begetter; may he give to me N.N. as my wife; svaha! 'Soma is rich in wives; may he make me rich in wives by N.N.; svaha! 'Pushan is rich in kindred; may he make me rich in kindred by the father, the mother, the brothers of N.N.; svaha!'

1.9.s: na ājya āhutiṣu nityāv ājya bhāgau sviṣṭakṛc ca |
1.9.d: न आज्य आहुतिषु नित्याव् आज्य भागौ स्विष्टकृच् च ।
1.9.e: At the Agya oblations the offering of the two Agya portions and of the Svishtakrit oblation is not standing,
Nor in the standing oblations, according to Mandukeya.

1.9.s: mahā vyāhṛti sarva prāyaś citta prājāpatya antaram etad āvāpa sthānam |
1.9.d: महा व्याहृति सर्व प्रायश् चित्त प्राजापत्य अन्तरम् एतद् आवाप स्थानम् ।
1.9.e: The place for the insertion is the interval between the Mahavyahritis, the general expiation, and the oblation to Pragapati.

1.9.s: ājye haviṣi savye pāṇau ye kuśās tān dakṣiṇena agre saṃgṛhya mūle savyena teṣām agram sruve samanakti madhyam ājya sthālyām mule ca |
1.9.d: आज्ये हविषि सव्ये पाणौ ये कुशास् तान् दक्षिणेन अग्रे संगृह्य मूले सव्येन तेषाम् अग्रम् स्रुवे समनक्ति मध्यम् आज्य स्थाल्याम् मुले च ।
1.9.e: If the oblation consists in Agya, let him seize the Kusa blades in his left hand with his right hand at their points and with the left at their roots, and let him wet their points (with Agya) in the Sruva, the middle and the roots in the Agya pot;

1.9.s: atha cet sthālī pāleṣu srucy agram madhyam sruve mūlam ājya sthālyām |
1.9.d: अथ चेत् स्थाली पालेषु स्रुच्य् अग्रम् मध्यम् स्रुवे मूलम् आज्य स्थाल्याम् ।
1.9.e: In the oblations of cooked food, however, the points in the Sruk, the middle in the Sruva, the roots in the Agya pot.

1.9.s: tān anuprahṛtya agner vāso asi iti |
1.9.d: तान् अनुप्रहृत्य अग्नेर् वासो असि इति ।
1.9.e: When he then has thrown them (into the fire) with the words, 'Agni's garment art thou,'
And has put on (the fire) three pieces of wood,
(Water) is sprinkled round (the fire) as stated above.

1.9.s: anāmnāta mantrāsv ādiṣṭa devatāsu amuṣyai svāhā amuṣyai svāhā iti juhuyāt svāhā kāreṇa śuddhena |
1.9.d: अनाम्नात मन्त्रास्व् आदिष्ट देवतासु अमुष्यै स्वाहा अमुष्यै स्वाहा इति जुहुयात् स्वाहा कारेण शुद्धेन ।
1.9.e: Oblations for which only the deities are indicated, but no texts prescribed, are to be made merely with the word SVAHA, 'To such and such a deity svaha! To such and such a deity svaha!'
The ritual (here) declared of the sacrifice (to be performed) when (the father's) assent (to give away his daughter) has been declared--

1.10.e: Forms the standard for all sacrifices that procure happiness,
For the sacrifice of animals which are tied to a branch,
And for the offerings of boiled (rice) grains and of cooked food.

1.10.s: ta ete aprayājā ananuyājā aniḍā anigadā asāmidhenīkāś ca sarve pāka yajñā bhavanti |
1.10.d: त एते अप्रयाजा अननुयाजा अनिडा अनिगदा असामिधेनीकाश् च सर्वे पाक यज्ञा भवन्ति ।
1.10.e: These are performed, all the offerings of cooked food, without PRAYAGA and ANUYAGA oblations, without (the invocation of) the ILA, without NIGADA recitation, and without SAMIDHENI verses.
There are also the following Slokas:

1.10.s: huto agni hotra homena ahuto brāhmaṇe hutaḥ | prahutaḥ pitṛ karmaṇā prāśito brāhmaṇe hutaḥ |
1.10.d: हुतो अग्नि होत्र होमेन अहुतो ब्राह्मणे हुतः । प्रहुतः पितृ कर्मणा प्राशितो ब्राह्मणे हुतः ।
1.10.e: '(An oblation is called) HUTA, (if made) by the performing of the Agnihotra; AHUTA (i.e. unsacrificed, if) by the Bali offering; PRAHUTA (i.e. sacrificed up, if) by a sacrifice to the Manes; PRASITA (i.e. tasted, if) deposited as an offering in a Brahmana.

1.10.s: anūrdhvajñur vyūḍa jānur juhuyāt sarvadā haviḥ | na hi bāhya hutam devāḥ pratigṛhṇanti karhicit |
1.10.d: अनूर्ध्वज्ञुर् व्यूड जानुर् जुहुयात् सर्वदा हविः । न हि बाह्य हुतम् देवाः प्रतिगृह्णन्ति कर्हिचित् ।
1.10.e: 'Without raising his knees, with spread knees let him always offer his oblation; for the gods never accept an offering (that has been made holding the hand) not between (the knees).

1.10.s: raudram tu rākṣasam pitryam āsuram ca abhicārikam | uktvā mantra spṛśed apa ālabhya ātmānam eva ca |
1.10.d: रौद्रम् तु राक्षसम् पित्र्यम् आसुरम् च अभिचारिकम् । उक्त्वा मन्त्र स्पृशेद् अप आलभ्य आत्मानम् एव च ।
1.10.e: 'But when he has repeated a text sacred to Rudra, to the Rakshas, to the Manes, to the Asuras, or that contains an imprecation, let him touch water, and so also when he has touched his own body.'

1.11.s: atha etām rātrīm śvas tṛtīyām vā kanyām vakṣyanti iti |
1.11.d: अथ एताम् रात्रीम् श्वस् तृतीयाम् वा कन्याम् वक्ष्यन्ति इति ।
1.11.e: Now when the bride is to be carried away (to the bridegroom's house) that night, or on the next, or on the third night,

1.11.s: tasyām rātryām atīte niśā kāle sarva oṣadhi phala uttamaiḥ surabhi miśraiḥ saśiraskām kanyām āplāvya |
1.11.d: तस्याम् रात्र्याम् अतीते निशा काले सर्व ओषधि फल उत्तमैः सुरभि मिश्रैः सशिरस्काम् कन्याम् आप्लाव्य ।
1.11.e: On that night, when (the darkness of) night is gone, they wash the girl up to her head with (water that has been made fragrant by) all sorts of herbs and the choicest fruits together with scents;
They put on her a newly-dyed garment or (a new one) which has not yet been washed;

1.11.s: paścād agneḥ kanyām upaveśya anvārabdhāyām mahā vyāhṛtibhir hutvā ājya āhutīr juhoti agraye somāya prajāpataye mitrāya varuṇāya indrāya indrāṇyai gandharvāya bhagāya pūṣṇe tvaṣṭre bṛhaspataye rājñe pratyānīkāya iti |
1.11.d: पश्चाद् अग्नेः कन्याम् उपवेश्य अन्वारब्धायाम् महा व्याहृतिभिर् हुत्वा आज्य आहुतीर् जुहोति अग्रये सोमाय प्रजापतये मित्राय वरुणाय इन्द्राय इन्द्राण्यै गन्धर्वाय भगाय पूष्णे त्वष्ट्रे बृहस्पतये राज्ञे प्रत्यानीकाय इति ।
1.11.e: Then (the Akarya of the bride's family) makes the girl sit down behind the fire, and while she takes hold of him he sacrifices with the Mahavyahritis, and then he makes Agya oblations to Agni, to Soma, to Pragapati, to Mitra, to Varuna, to Indra, to Indrani, to the Gandharva, to Bhaga, to Pushan, to Tvashtar, to Brihaspati, to the king Pratyanika.

1.11.s: catasro aṣṭau vā avidhavāḥ śāka piṇḍībhir surayā annena ca tarpayitvā catur ānartanam kuryuḥ |
1.11.d: चतस्रो अष्टौ वा अविधवाः शाक पिण्डीभिर् सुरया अन्नेन च तर्पयित्वा चतुर् आनर्तनम् कुर्युः ।
1.11.e: After they have regaled four or eight women, who are not widows, with lumps of vegetables, Sura, and food, these should perform a dance four times.
The same deities (they worship also) on behalf of the man,
Then follows the distribution of food to Brahmanas.

1.12.s: snātam kṛta maṅgalam varam avidhavāḥ subhagā yuvatyaḥ kumāryai veśma prapādayanti |
1.12.d: स्नातम् कृत मङ्गलम् वरम् अविधवाः सुभगा युवत्यः कुमार्यै वेश्म प्रपादयन्ति ।
1.12.e: The bridegroom, who has bathed and for whom auspicious ceremonies have been performed, is escorted by happy young women, who are not widows, to the girl's house.

1.12.s: tāsām apratikūlaḥ syād anyatra abhakṣya pātakebhyaḥ |
1.12.d: तासाम् अप्रतिकूलः स्याद् अन्यत्र अभक्ष्य पातकेभ्यः ।
1.12.e: To these he shall not behave unobsequiously, except where forbidden food or a transgression is concerned.

1.12.s: tābhir anujñāto atha asyai vāsaḥ prayacchati raibhy āsīd iti |
1.12.d: ताभिर् अनुज्ञातो अथ अस्यै वासः प्रयच्छति रैभ्य् आसीद् इति ।
1.12.e: Having obtained their permission, he then gives her the garment with (the verse), 'The Raibhi was' (Rig-veda X, 85, 6).

1.12.s: cittir ā upabarhaṇam iti āñjana kośam ādatte |
1.12.d: चित्तिर् आ उपबर्हणम् इति आञ्जन कोशम् आदत्ते ।
1.12.e: With (the verse), 'Mind was the cushion' (ibid. 7) he takes up the salve-box.
The verse for the Anointing is, 'May the Visve devas anoint (or, unite),' (ibid. 47.)

1.12.s: yathā iyam śacīm vāvātām suputrām ca yathā aditim | avidhavām ca apālām evam tvām iha rakṣatād imam iti dakṣiṇe pāṇau śalalīm tṛvṛtam dadāti |
1.12.d: यथा इयम् शचीम् वावाताम् सुपुत्राम् च यथा अदितिम् । अविधवाम् च अपालाम् एवम् त्वाम् इह रक्षताद् इमम् इति दक्षिणे पाणौ शललीम् तृवृतम् ददाति ।
1.12.e: 'As this (has protected) Saki the beloved one, and Aditi the mother of noble sons, and Apala who was free from widowhood, nay it thus here protect thee, N.N.!'--with these words (the. bridegroom) gives her into her right hand the quill of a porcupine (and) a string of three twisted threads,
With the verse, 'Shape by shape' (Rig-veda VI, 47, 18) a mirror into the left.

1.12.s: rakta kṛṣṇam āvikam kṣaumam vā trimaṇim pratisaram jñātayo asyā badhnanti nīla lohitam iti |
1.12.d: रक्त कृष्णम् आविकम् क्षौमम् वा त्रिमणिम् प्रतिसरम् ज्ञातयो अस्या बध्नन्ति नील लोहितम् इति ।
1.12.e: Her relations tie (to her body) a red and black, woollen or linen cord with three (amulet) gems, with the verse, 'Dark-blue and red' (Rig. veda X, 85, 28).
With the verse, 'Full of honey the herbs' (Rig-veda IV, 57, 3), (the bridegroom) ties (to her body) Madhuka flowers.

1.12.s: vivāhe gām arhayitvā gṛheṣu gām te mādhuparkikyau |
1.12.d: विवाहे गाम् अर्हयित्वा गृहेषु गाम् ते माधुपर्किक्यौ ।
1.12.e: At the wedding one cow, when the Argha ceremony has been performed; in the house one cow: these are the two Madhuparka cows.

1.12.s: paścād agneḥ kanyām upaveśya anvāarabdhāyām mahā vyāhṛtibhis tisro juhoti |
1.12.d: पश्चाद् अग्नेः कन्याम् उपवेश्य अन्वाअरब्धायाम् महा व्याहृतिभिस् तिस्रो जुहोति ।
1.12.e: (The bridegroom) makes the girl sit down behind the fire, and while she takes hold of him he makes three oblations with the Mahavyahritis.
A fourth (oblation) with (the three Mahavyahritis) together is to be understood from this rule.

1.12.s: evam anādeśe sarveṣu bhūti karmasu purastāc ca upariṣṭāc ca etābhir eva juhuyāt |
1.12.d: एवम् अनादेशे सर्वेषु भूति कर्मसु पुरस्ताच् च उपरिष्टाच् च एताभिर् एव जुहुयात् ।
1.12.e: In this way, where no express rule is stated, in all sacrifices that procure happiness, one is to sacrifice before and afterwards with these same (Mahavyahritis).

1.13.s: saṃrājñī śvaśure bhava iti pitā bhrātā vā asy agreṇa mūrdhani juhoti sruveṇa vā tiṣṭhann āsīnāyāḥ prān mukhyāḥ pratyan mukhaḥ |
1.13.d: संराज्ञी श्वशुरे भव इति पिता भ्राता वा अस्य् अग्रेण मूर्धनि जुहोति स्रुवेण वा तिष्ठन्न् आसीनायाः प्रान् मुख्याः प्रत्यन् मुखः ।
1.13.e: 'Be queen with thy father-in-law,' with this verse (Rig-veda X, 85, 46) her father or brother sacrifices with a sword's point on her head, or with the Sruva, standing while she is sitting, with his face turned to the west, while her face is turned to the east.

1.13.s: gṛbhṇāmi te saubhagatvāya hastam iti dakṣiṇena pāṇinā dakṣiṇam pāṇim gṛhṇāti sāṅguṣṭham uttānena uttānam tiṣṭhann āsīnāyāḥ prān mukhyāḥ pratyan mukhaḥ |
1.13.d: गृभ्णामि ते सौभगत्वाय हस्तम् इति दक्षिणेन पाणिना दक्षिणम् पाणिम् गृह्णाति साङ्गुष्ठम् उत्तानेन उत्तानम् तिष्ठन्न् आसीनायाः प्रान् मुख्याः प्रत्यन् मुखः ।
1.13.e: 'I seize thy hand for the sake of happiness' (Rig-veda X, 85, 36), with these words (the bridegroom) seizes with his right hand her right hand with the thumb, both hands being turned with the palms upwards, he standing while she is sitting, with his face turned to the west, while her face is turned to the east.
And when he has murmured the following five verses,

1.13.s: amo aham asmi sā tvam sā tvam asy amo aham dyaur aham pṛthivī tvam ṛk tvam asi sāma aham sā mām anuvratā bhava | tāv eha vi vahāvahai prajām pra janayāvahai putrān vindāvahai bahūn te santu jarad aṣṭaya iti |
1.13.d: अमो अहम् अस्मि सा त्वम् सा त्वम् अस्य् अमो अहम् द्यौर् अहम् पृथिवी त्वम् ऋक् त्वम् असि साम अहम् सा माम् अनुव्रता भव । ताव् एह वि वहावहै प्रजाम् प्र जनयावहै पुत्रान् विन्दावहै बहून् ते सन्तु जरद् अष्टय इति ।
1.13.e: (He continues thus,) 'This am I, that art thou; that art thou, this am I; the heaven I, the earth thou; the Rik art thou, the Saman I. So be thou devoted to me. 'Well! Let us here marry. Let us beget offspring. Let us acquire many sons who may reach old age.'

1.13.s: uda kumbham navam bhūr bhuvaḥ svar iti pūrayitvā |
1.13.d: उद कुम्भम् नवम् भूर् भुवः स्वर् इति पूरयित्वा ।
1.13.e: (The Akarya) fills, with the words bhur bhuvah svah, a new water-pot,

1.13.s: pum nāmno vṛkṣasya sakṣīrānt sapalāśānt sakuśān opya |
1.13.d: पुम् नाम्नो वृक्षस्य सक्षीरान्त् सपलाशान्त् सकुशान् ओप्य ।
1.13.e: Throws into it (branches) with milky sap and leaves, of a tree the name of which is masculine, together with Kusa grass,

1.13.s: tam brahma cāriṇe vāg yatāya pradāya |
1.13.d: तम् ब्रह्म चारिणे वाग् यताय प्रदाय ।
1.13.e: And hands it over to a student who observes silence.

1.13.s: prāg udīcyām diśi tāḥ stheyāḥ pradakṣiṇā bhavanti |
1.13.d: प्राग् उदीच्याम् दिशि ताः स्थेयाः प्रदक्षिणा भवन्ति ।
1.13.e: They should walk round this Stheya water, (placed) to the north-east, so that they turn their right sides . towards it.
And after (the Akarya) has placed a stone towards the northern direction,
(The bridegroom) makes her rise with the words, 'Come, thou joyful one,'

1.13.s: ehy aśmānam ā tiṣṭha aśmā iva tvam sthirā bhava | abhitiṣṭha pṛtanyataḥ sahasva pṛtanāyata iti dakṣiṇena prapadena aśmānam ākramayya |
1.13.d: एह्य् अश्मानम् आ तिष्ठ अश्मा इव त्वम् स्थिरा भव । अभितिष्ठ पृतन्यतः सहस्व पृतनायत इति दक्षिणेन प्रपदेन अश्मानम् आक्रमय्य ।
1.13.e: And makes her tread with the tip of her right foot on the stone, with the words, 'Come, tread on the stone; like a stone be firm. Tread the foes down; overcome the enemies.'
He then leads her round the fire so that their right sides are turned to it,

1.13.s: tena eva mantreṇa dvitīyam vasanam pradāya |
1.13.d: तेन एव मन्त्रेण द्वितीयम् वसनम् प्रदाय ।
1.13.e: And gives her a second garment with the same text (chap. 12, section 3).

1.13.s: lājān śamī palāśa miśrān pitā bhrātā vā syād añjalāv āvapati |
1.13.d: लाजान् शमी पलाश मिश्रान् पिता भ्राता वा स्याद् अञ्जलाव् आवपति ।
1.13.e: Her father or brother pours out of a basket fried grain mixed with Sami leaves into her joined hands.
The spreading under, the sprinkling over, and the second sprinkling over (are done) with Agya.

1.14.s: iyam nāry upabrūte lājān āvapantikā | śivā jñātihbyo bhūyāṃsam ciram jīvatu me patiḥ svāhā iti tiṣṭhantī juhoti patir mantram japati |
1.14.d: इयम् नार्य् उपब्रूते लाजान् आवपन्तिका । शिवा ज्ञातिह्ब्यो भूयांसम् चिरम् जीवतु मे पतिः स्वाहा इति तिष्ठन्ती जुहोति पतिर् मन्त्रम् जपति ।
1.14.e: 'This woman, strewing grains, prays thus, "May I bring bliss to my relations; may my husband live long. Svaha!"'--while the husband murmurs (this) text, she sacrifices standing.
(All the ceremonies,) beginning from the treading upon the stone, (are repeated) in the same way for a second time,
And in the same way a third time.
Silently, if they like, a fourth time.

1.14.s: prāg udīcyām diśi sapta padāni prakramayati |
1.14.d: प्राग् उदीच्याम् दिशि सप्त पदानि प्रक्रमयति ।
1.14.e: (The Akarya?) makes (them) step forward in a north-eastern direction seven steps (with the words),

1.14.s: iṣa eka padī ūrje dvipadīṇrāyas poṣāya tripadī āyo bhavyāya catuṣpadī paśubhyaḥ pañcapadī ṛtubhyaḥ ṣaṭpadī sakhā sapta padī bhava iti |
1.14.d: इष एक पदी ऊर्जे द्विपदीण्रायस् पोषाय त्रिपदी आयो भव्याय चतुष्पदी पशुभ्यः पञ्चपदी ऋतुभ्यः षट्पदी सखा सप्त पदी भव इति ।
1.14.e: 'For sap with one step, for juice with two steps, for the prospering of wealth with three steps, for comfort with four steps, for cattle with five steps, for the seasons with six steps. Friend be with seven steps.'
With the three Apohishthiya verses (Rig-veda X, 9, 1-3) he wipes (them) with the Stheya water,
And sprinkles it on their heads.
(The bridegroom then) says, 'I give you a cow.'

1.14.s: brāhmaṇebhyaḥ kiṃcid dadyāt sarvatra sthālī pāla ādiṣu karmasu |
1.14.d: ब्राह्मणेभ्यः किंचिद् दद्यात् सर्वत्र स्थाली पाल आदिषु कर्मसु ।
1.14.e: Let him give something to the Brahmanas each time at the Sthalipakas and other rites;
To him who knows the Surya hymn the bride's shift.
A cow is the optional gift to be given by a Brahmana,
A hundred (cows) with a chariot (he gives to a father) who has only daughters.
To those versed in the sacrificial rites he gives a horse.

1.15.s: pra tvā muñcāmi iti tṛcam gṛhāt pratiṣṭhamānāyām |
1.15.d: प्र त्वा मुञ्चामि इति तृचम् गृहात् प्रतिष्ठमानायाम् ।
1.15.e: The three verses, 'I loosen thee' (Rig-veda X, 85, 24), when she departs from the house.
'The living one they bewail' (Rig-veda X, 40, 10), if she begins to cry.

1.15.s: atha ratha akṣasya upāñjanam patnī kurute akṣann amīmadanta iti etayā sarpiṣā |
1.15.d: अथ रथ अक्षस्य उपाञ्जनम् पत्नी कुरुते अक्षन्न् अमीमदन्त इति एतया सर्पिषा ।
1.15.e: The wife then smears the axle of the chariot with clarified butter with this (verse), 'They feasted, they got drunk' (Rig-veda I, 82, 2),

1.15.s: śucī te cakre dve te cakre iti ca etābhyām cakrayoḥ pūrvayā pūrvam uttarayā uttaram |
1.15.d: शुची ते चक्रे द्वे ते चक्रे इति च एताभ्याम् चक्रयोः पूर्वया पूर्वम् उत्तरया उत्तरम् ।
1.15.e: And with the two (verses), 'Pure are thy wheels,' 'Thy two wheels' (Rig-veda X, 85, 12. 16), of the two wheels the first with the first (verse) and the second with the second (verse),

1.15.s: khe rathasya etayā phalavato vṛkṣasya śamyā garteṣv eka ekām vayān nikhāya |
1.15.d: खे रथस्य एतया फलवतो वृक्षस्य शम्या गर्तेष्व् एक एकाम् वयान् निखाय ।
1.15.e: After (the wife?) has put, with this (verse), 'In the box of the wheel' (Rig-veda VIII, 80, 7), a branch of a fruit-bearing tree into each of the holes destined for the pins,
Or, if (such branches) are (already) fixed, has recited (that verse) over them,

1.15.s: atha usrau yuñjanti yuktas te astu dakṣiṇa iti dvābhyām śukrāv anaḍvāhāv iti etena ardharceṇa yuktāv abhimantrya |
1.15.d: अथ उस्रौ युञ्जन्ति युक्तस् ते अस्तु दक्षिण इति द्वाभ्याम् शुक्राव् अनड्वाहाव् इति एतेन अर्धर्चेण युक्ताव् अभिमन्त्र्य ।
1.15.e: They then harness the two bulls with the two (verses), 'Harnessed be thy right one' (Rig-veda I, 82, 5-6), (the bridegroom) reciting the half-verse, 'White the two bulls' (Rig-veda X, 85, 10), over them when they have been harnessed.

1.15.s: atha yadi ratha aṅgam viśīryeta chidyeta vā āhita agneḥ gṛhān kanyām prapādya |
1.15.d: अथ यदि रथ अङ्गम् विशीर्येत छिद्येत वा आहित अग्नेः गृहान् कन्याम् प्रपाद्य ।
1.15.e: Now should any part of the chariot break or burst, let him take the girl to the house of one who keeps the sacred fires,

1.15.s: abhi vyayasva khadirasya iti etayā pratidadhyāt |
1.15.d: अभि व्ययस्व खदिरस्य इति एतया प्रतिदध्यात् ।
1.15.e: And repair (the damage) with the verse, 'Cover thyself with the Khadiras' (Rig-veda III, 53, 19).
A knot with the verse, 'Him like a horse' (Rig-veda X, 143, 2).

1.15.s: svasti no mimītām iti pañcarcam japati |
1.15.d: स्वस्ति नो मिमीताम् इति पञ्चर्चम् जपति ।
1.15.e: He then murmurs the five verses, 'May prosperity give us' (Rig-veda V, 51, 11-15).
'Adorned with Kimsuka flowers' (Rig-veda X, 85, 20), when she mounts the chariot;
'May no waylayers meet us' (ibid. 32), at a cross-way;

1.15.s: vanaspate śata valśa iti vanaspatāv ardharcam japati |
1.15.d: वनस्पते शत वल्श इति वनस्पताव् अर्धर्चम् जपति ।
1.15.e: The half-verse, 'O tree with thy hundred branches' (Rig-veda III, 8, 11), he mutters near a big tree;
'The good protectress' (Rig-Veda X, 63, 10), when she ascends a ship;
'Carrying stones' (Rig-veda X, 53, 8), when she crosses a river;

1.15.s: iha priyam iti sapta gṛhān prāptāyāḥ kṛtāḥ parihāpya |
1.15.d: इह प्रियम् इति सप्त गृहान् प्राप्तायाः कृताः परिहाप्य ।
1.15.e: The seven verses, 'Here may delight' (Rig-veda X, 85, 27 seq.), when she has reached the house, omitting the verses already employed.

1.16.s: tasminn upaveśya anvārabdhāyām patiś catasro juhoti |
1.16.d: तस्मिन्न् उपवेश्य अन्वारब्धायाम् पतिश् चतस्रो जुहोति ।
1.16.e: On that hide the husband makes her sit down and sacrifices, while she takes hold of him, four oblations (with the following formulas),

1.16.s: agninā devena pṛthivī lokena lokānām ṛgvedena vedānām tena tvā śamayāmy asau svāhā | vayaunā devena antarikṣa lokena lokānām yajur vedena vedānām tena tvā śamayāmy asau svāhā | sūryeṇa devena dyaur lokena lokānām sāmavedena vedānām tena tvā śamayāmy asau svāhā | candreṇa devena diśām lokena lokānām brahma vedena vedānām tena tvā śamayāmy asau svāhā |
1.16.d: अग्निना देवेन पृथिवी लोकेन लोकानाम् ऋग्वेदेन वेदानाम् तेन त्वा शमयाम्य् असौ स्वाहा । वयौना देवेन अन्तरिक्ष लोकेन लोकानाम् यजुर् वेदेन वेदानाम् तेन त्वा शमयाम्य् असौ स्वाहा । सूर्येण देवेन द्यौर् लोकेन लोकानाम् सामवेदेन वेदानाम् तेन त्वा शमयाम्य् असौ स्वाहा । चन्द्रेण देवेन दिशाम् लोकेन लोकानाम् ब्रह्म वेदेन वेदानाम् तेन त्वा शमयाम्य् असौ स्वाहा ।
1.16.e: 'With god Agni, with the earth-world of the worlds, and the Rig-veda of the Vedas: therewith I appease thee, N.N., svaha! 'With god Vayu, with the air-world of the worlds, with the Yagur-veda of the Vedas: therewith I appease thee, N.N., svaha! 'With god Surya, with the heaven-world of the worlds, with the Sama-veda of the Vedas: therewith I appease thee, N.N., svaha! 'With god Kandra, with the world of the quarters (of the horizon) of the worlds, with the Brahma-veda of the Vedas: therewith I appease thee, N.N., svaha!'

1.16.s: bhūr yā te patidhnya lakṣmī devaraghnī jāraghnī tām karomy asau svāhā iti vā prathamayā mahā vyāhṛtyā prathama upahitā dvitīyayā dvitīyā tṛtīyayā tṛtīyā samastābhiś caturthī |
1.16.d: भूर् या ते पतिध्न्य लक्ष्मी देवरघ्नी जारघ्नी ताम् करोम्य् असौ स्वाहा इति वा प्रथमया महा व्याहृत्या प्रथम उपहिता द्वितीयया द्वितीया तृतीयया तृतीया समस्ताभिश् चतुर्थी ।

1.16.s: aghora cakṣur iti ājya lepena cakṣuṣī vimṛjīta |
1.16.d: अघोर चक्षुर् इति आज्य लेपेन चक्षुषी विमृजीत ।

1.16.s: uta tyā daivyā bhijasā iti catasro anudrutya ante svāhā kāreṇa mūrdhani saṃsrāvam |
1.16.d: उत त्या दैव्या भिजसा इति चतस्रो अनुद्रुत्य अन्ते स्वाहा कारेण मूर्धनि संस्रावम् ।
1.16.e: And having quickly recited the four verses, 'And those divine medicines' (Rig-veda VIII, 18, 8), at the end (of that text) with the word svaha (pours out) the remainder on (her) head.

1.16.s: atra ha eke kumāram utsaṅgam ānayanty ubhayataḥ sujātam ā te yonim iti etayā |
1.16.d: अत्र ह एके कुमारम् उत्सङ्गम् आनयन्त्य् उभयतः सुजातम् आ ते योनिम् इति एतया ।
1.16.e: Here some place a boy of good birth on both sides, in her lap, with this (verse), 'Into thy womb' (see below, chap. 19, 6),

1.16.s: tasya añjalau phalāni dattvā puṇya aham vācayati |
1.16.d: तस्य अञ्जलौ फलानि दत्त्वा पुण्य अहम् वाचयति ।
1.16.e: Into this (boy's) joined hands (the bridegroom) gives fruits and causes (the Brahmanas) to wish an auspicious day.
Thus she becomes the mother of male children.

1.16.s: iha eva stam iti sūkta śeṣeṇa gṛhān prapādayanti |
1.16.d: इह एव स्तम् इति सूक्त शेषेण गृहान् प्रपादयन्ति ।
1.16.e: With the rest of the hymn, 'Stay ye here both' (Rig-veda X, 85, 42 seq.), they make them enter the house.

1.17.e: With the verse, 'I praised Dadhikravan' (Rig-veda IV, 39, 6), let them drink together curds.

1.17.s: vāg yatāv āsīyātām ā dhruva darśanāt |
1.17.d: वाग् यताव् आसीयाताम् आ ध्रुव दर्शनात् ।
1.17.e: Let them sit silent, when the sun has set, until the polar-star appears.

1.17.s: astamite dhruvam darśayati dhruvā edhi poṣyā mayi iti |
1.17.d: अस्तमिते ध्रुवम् दर्शयति ध्रुवा एधि पोष्या मयि इति ।
1.17.e: He shows her the polar-star with the words, 'Firm be thou, thriving with me!'

1.17.s: dhruvam paśyāmi prajām vindaya iti brūyāt |
1.17.d: ध्रुवम् पश्यामि प्रजाम् विन्दय इति ब्रूयात् ।
1.17.e: Let her say, 'I see the polar-star; may I obtain offspring.'
Through a period of three nights let them refrain from conjugal intercourse.
Let them sleep on the ground.

1.17.s: dadhy odanam sambhuñjīyātām pibatam ca tṛpṇutam ca iti tṛcena |
1.17.d: दध्य् ओदनम् सम्भुञ्जीयाताम् पिबतम् च तृप्णुतम् च इति तृचेन ।
1.17.e: Let them eat together boiled rice with curds, with the three verses, 'Drink and satiate yourselves' (Rig-veda VIII, 35, 10).

1.17.s: sāyam prātar vaivāhyam agnim paricareyātām agnaye svāhā anagnaye sviṣṭakṛte svāhā iti |
1.17.d: सायम् प्रातर् वैवाह्यम् अग्निम् परिचरेयाताम् अग्नये स्वाहा अनग्नये स्विष्टकृते स्वाहा इति ।
1.17.e: Let them serve the nuptial fire in the evening and in the morning with the words, 'To Agni svaha! To Agni Svishtakrit svaha!'

1.17.s: pumāṃsau mitā varuṇau pumāṃsāv aśvināv ubhau | pumān indraś ca agniś ca pumāṃsam vardhatām mayi svāhā iti pūrvā garbha kāmā |
1.17.d: पुमांसौ मिता वरुणौ पुमांसाव् अश्विनाव् उभौ । पुमान् इन्द्रश् च अग्निश् च पुमांसम् वर्धताम् मयि स्वाहा इति पूर्वा गर्भ कामा ।
1.17.e: 'Let the two men Mitra and Varuna, let the two men, the Asvins both, let the man Indra and also Agni make a man grow in me. Svaha!'--with [paragraph continues] (these words she offers) the first oblation if she is desirous of pregnancy.
For ten days they are not to set out (from home).

1.18.e: Now the rites of the fourth day.
When the three nights have elapsed, he makes offerings of cooked food (with the texts),

1.18.s: agne prāyaś cittir asi tvam devānām prāyaś cittir asi | yā asyāḥ patighnī tanūs tām asyā apa jahi | vāyo prāyaś cittir asi tvam devānām prāyaś cittir asi | yā asyā aputrayā tanūs tām asyā apa jahi | sūrya prāyaś cittir asi tvam devānām prāyaś cittir asi | yā asyā apaśavyā tanūs tām asyā apa jahi | aryamaṇam nu devam kanyā agnim ayakṣata | sā imām devo aryamā preto muñcātu mā amutaḥ | varuṇam nu devam kanyā agnim ayakṣata | sā imām devo varuṇa reto muñcātu mā amutaḥ | pūṣaṇam tu devam kanyā agnim ayakṣata | sā imām devaḥ pūṣā preto muñcātu mā amutaḥ |
1.18.d: अग्ने प्रायश् चित्तिर् असि त्वम् देवानाम् प्रायश् चित्तिर् असि । या अस्याः पतिघ्नी तनूस् ताम् अस्या अप जहि । वायो प्रायश् चित्तिर् असि त्वम् देवानाम् प्रायश् चित्तिर् असि । या अस्या अपुत्रया तनूस् ताम् अस्या अप जहि । सूर्य प्रायश् चित्तिर् असि त्वम् देवानाम् प्रायश् चित्तिर् असि । या अस्या अपशव्या तनूस् ताम् अस्या अप जहि । अर्यमणम् नु देवम् कन्या अग्निम् अयक्षत । सा इमाम् देवो अर्यमा प्रेतो मुञ्चातु मा अमुतः । वरुणम् नु देवम् कन्या अग्निम् अयक्षत । सा इमाम् देवो वरुण रेतो मुञ्चातु मा अमुतः । पूषणम् तु देवम् कन्या अग्निम् अयक्षत । सा इमाम् देवः पूषा प्रेतो मुञ्चातु मा अमुतः ।
1.18.e: 'Agni! Thou art expiation; thou art the expiation of the gods. What substance dwells in her that brings death to her husband, that drive away from her. 'Vayu! Thou art expiation; thou art the expiation of the gods. What substance dwells in her that brings sonlessness, that drive away from her. 'Surya! Thou art expiation; thou art the expiation of the gods. What substance dwells in her that brings destruction to the cattle, that drive away from her. 'To god Aryaman the girls have made sacrifice, to Agni; may he, god Aryaman, loosen her from this, and not from that place. 'To god Varuna the girls have made sacrifice, to Agni; may he, god Varuna, &c. 'To god Pushan the girls have made sacrifice, to Agni; may he, god Pushan, &c.'
The seventh oblation with the verse, 'Pragapati' (Rig-veda X, 121, 10).

1.19.s: adhyāṇḍā mūlam peṣayitvā ṛtu velāyām ud īrṣvātaḥ pativatī iti dvābhyām ante svāhā kārābhyām nasto dakṣiṇato niṣiñcet |
1.19.d: अध्याण्डा मूलम् पेषयित्वा ऋतु वेलायाम् उद् ईर्ष्वातः पतिवती इति द्वाभ्याम् अन्ते स्वाहा काराभ्याम् नस्तो दक्षिणतो निषिञ्चेत् ।
1.19.e: Let him pound the root of the Adhyanda plant and sprinkle it at the time of her monthly period with the two (verses), 'Speed away from here; a husband has she' (Rig-veda X, 85, 21. 22), with svaha at the end of each, into her right nostril.

1.19.s: gandharvasya viśvāvasor mukham asi iti upastham prajanayiṣyamāṇo abhimṛśet |
1.19.d: गन्धर्वस्य विश्वावसोर् मुखम् असि इति उपस्थम् प्रजनयिष्यमाणो अभिमृशेत् ।
1.19.e: 'The mouth of the Gandharva Visvavasu art thou'--with these words let him touch her, when he is about to cohabit with her.
When he has finished, let him murmur,

1.19.s: prāṇe te reto dadhāmy asāv iti anuprāṇyāt |
1.19.d: प्राणे ते रेतो दधाम्य् असाव् इति अनुप्राण्यात् ।
1.19.e: 'Into thy breath I put the sperm, N.N.!'

1.19.s: yathā bhūmir agni garbhā yathā dyaur indreṇa garbhiṇī | vāyur yathā diśām garbham evam garbham dadhāmi te asāv iti vā |
1.19.d: यथा भूमिर् अग्नि गर्भा यथा द्यौर् इन्द्रेण गर्भिणी । वायुर् यथा दिशाम् गर्भम् एवम् गर्भम् दधामि ते असाव् इति वा ।

1.19.s: ā te yonim garbha etu pumān bāṇa iva iṣudhim | ā te vīro atra jāyatām putras te daśa māsyaḥ |
1.19.d: आ ते योनिम् गर्भ एतु पुमान् बाण इव इषुधिम् । आ ते वीरो अत्र जायताम् पुत्रस् ते दश मास्यः ।

1.19.s: pumāṃsam putram janaya tam pumān anu jāyatām | teṣām mātā bhaviṣyasi jātānām janayāṃsi ca |
1.19.d: पुमांसम् पुत्रम् जनय तम् पुमान् अनु जायताम् । तेषाम् माता भविष्यसि जातानाम् जनयांसि च ।

1.19.s: puṃsi vai puruṣe retas tat striyām anu ṣiñcati | tathā tad abravīd dhātā tat prajāpatir abravīt |
1.19.d: पुंसि वै पुरुषे रेतस् तत् स्त्रियाम् अनु षिञ्चति । तथा तद् अब्रवीद् धाता तत् प्रजापतिर् अब्रवीत् ।

1.19.s: prajāpatir vyadadhāt savitā vyakalpayata | strīṣūyam anyāt svād adhat pumāṃsam ādadhād iha |
1.19.d: प्रजापतिर् व्यदधात् सविता व्यकल्पयत । स्त्रीषूयम् अन्यात् स्वाद् अधत् पुमांसम् आदधाद् इह ।

1.19.s: yāni bhadrāṇi bījāni puruṣā janayanti naḥ | tebhiṣ ṭvam putram janaya suprasūr dhenukā bhava |
1.19.d: यानि भद्राणि बीजानि पुरुषा जनयन्ति नः । तेभिष् ट्वम् पुत्रम् जनय सुप्रसूर् धेनुका भव ।

1.19.s: abhi kranda vīḍayasva garbham ā dhehi sādhaya | vṛṣāṇam vṛṣann ā dhehi prajāyai tvā havāmahe |
1.19.d: अभि क्रन्द वीडयस्व गर्भम् आ धेहि साधय । वृषाणम् वृषन्न् आ धेहि प्रजायै त्वा हवामहे ।

1.19.s: yasya yonim pati reto gṛbhāya pumān putro dhīyatām garbhe antaḥ | tam pipṛhi daśa māsyo antar udare sa jāyatām śraiṣṭhyatamaḥ svānām iti vā |
1.19.d: यस्य योनिम् पति रेतो गृभाय पुमान् पुत्रो धीयताम् गर्भे अन्तः । तम् पिपृहि दश मास्यो अन्तर् उदरे स जायताम् श्रैष्ठ्यतमः स्वानाम् इति वा ।

1.20.e: In the third month the Pumsavana (i.e. the ceremony to secure the birth of a male child),

1.20.s: soma aṃśum peṣayitvā kuśa kaṇṭakam vā nyagrodhasya vā skandhasya antyām śuṅgām yūpasya vā aṅgiṣṭhām |
1.20.d: सोम अंशुम् पेषयित्वा कुश कण्टकम् वा न्यग्रोधस्य वा स्कन्धस्य अन्त्याम् शुङ्गाम् यूपस्य वा अङ्गिष्ठाम् ।
1.20.e: Having pounded a Soma stalk, or a Kusa needle, or the last shoot of a Nyagrodha trunk, or the part of a sacrificial post which is exposed to the fire,
Or (having taken) after the completion of a sacrifice the remnants from the Guhu ladle,

1.20.s: agninā rayim tan nas turīpam samiddha agnir vanavat piśaṅga rūpa iti catasṛbhir ante svāhā kārābhir nasto dakṣiṇato niṣiñcet |
1.20.d: अग्निना रयिम् तन् नस् तुरीपम् समिद्ध अग्निर् वनवत् पिशङ्ग रूप इति चतसृभिर् अन्ते स्वाहा काराभिर् नस्तो दक्षिणतो निषिञ्चेत् ।
1.20.e: Let him sprinkle it into her right nostril with the four verses, 'By Agni may good' (Rig-veda I, 1, 3), 'That sperm to us' (III, 4, 9), 'May he succeed who lights fire' (V, 37, 2), 'Of tawny shape' (II, 3, 9), with Svaha at the end (of each verse).

1.21.e: In the fourth month the Garbharakshana (i.e. the ceremony for the protection of the embryo),

1.21.s: brahmaṇā agniḥ saṃvidāna iti ṣaṭ sthālī pākasya hutvā |
1.21.d: ब्रह्मणा अग्निः संविदान इति षट् स्थाली पाकस्य हुत्वा ।
1.21.e: Sacrificing six oblations from a mess of cooked food with (the six verses of the hymn), 'Agni, joined with the prayer' (Rig-veda X, 162),

1.21.s: akṣībhyām te nāsikābhyām iti pratyṛcam ājya lepena aṅgāny anuvimṛjya |
1.21.d: अक्षीभ्याम् ते नासिकाभ्याम् इति प्रत्यृचम् आज्य लेपेन अङ्गान्य् अनुविमृज्य ।
1.21.e: With (the verses), 'From thy eyes, thy nose' (Rig-veda X, 163), verse by verse besmearing her limbs with Agya salve.

1.22.s: saptame māsi prathama garbhe sīmanta unnayanam |
1.22.d: सप्तमे मासि प्रथम गर्भे सीमन्त उन्नयनम् ।
1.22.e: In the seventh month, at her first pregnancy, the Simantonnayana (or parting of the hair).

1.22.s: snātām ahata vāsasam paścād agneu upaveśya |
1.22.d: स्नाताम् अहत वाससम् पश्चाद् अग्नेउ उपवेश्य ।
1.22.e: He causes her, after she has bathed and put on a (new) garment which has not yet been washed, to sit down behind the fire.
He sacrifices, while she takes hold of him, with the Mahavyahritis.
He cooks a mess of food,
According to some (teachers) boiled rice with Mudga beans.
The implements used and the Nakshatra should be of male gender.

1.22.s: dhātā dadātu dāśuṣe prācīm jīvātum akṣitim | vayam devasya dhīmahi sumatim satya dharmaṇaḥ | dhātā prajāyā uta rāya īśe dhātā idam viśvam bhuvanam jajāna | dhātā putram yajamānāya dātā tasmā u havyam ghṛtavaj johota iti | nejameṣa parā pata iti tisraḥ prajāpata iti ṣaṣṭhī |
1.22.d: धाता ददातु दाशुषे प्राचीम् जीवातुम् अक्षितिम् । वयम् देवस्य धीमहि सुमतिम् सत्य धर्मणः । धाता प्रजाया उत राय ईशे धाता इदम् विश्वम् भुवनम् जजान । धाता पुत्रम् यजमानाय दाता तस्मा उ हव्यम् घृतवज् जोहोत इति । नेजमेष परा पत इति तिस्रः प्रजापत इति षष्ठी ।
1.22.e: (He then sacrifices with the following texts,) 'May Dhatar give to his worshipper further life and safety; may we obtain the favour of the god whose laws are truthful. 'Dhatar disposes of offspring and wealth; Dhatar has created this whole world; Dhatar will give a son to the sacrificer: to him you shall sacrifice, an offering rich in ghee.' (Besides) with the three verses, 'Negamesha, fly away' (Rig-veda Khailika sukta, after X, 184, vol. vi, p. 31), and in the sixth place the verse, 'Pragapati' (Rig-veda X, 121, 10).

1.22.s: triḥ śvetayā śalalyā darbha sūcyā vā udumbara śalāṭubhiḥ saha madhyād ūrdhvam sīmantam unnayati bhūr bhuvaḥ svar iti |
1.22.d: त्रिः श्वेतया शलल्या दर्भ सूच्या वा उदुम्बर शलाटुभिः सह मध्याद् ऊर्ध्वम् सीमन्तम् उन्नयति भूर् भुवः स्वर् इति ।
1.22.e: (The husband then) parts her hair, upwards, beginning from the middle, with a porcupine's quill that has three white spots, or with a Darbha needle together with unripe Udumbara fruits, with the words, 'Bhur bhuvah svah.'
He lays down (the thing he has used) in her lap,

1.22.s: trivṛti pratimucya kaṇṭhe badhnāti ayam ūrjāvato vṛkṣa ūrjī iva phalinī bhava iti |
1.22.d: त्रिवृति प्रतिमुच्य कण्ठे बध्नाति अयम् ऊर्जावतो वृक्ष ऊर्जी इव फलिनी भव इति ।
1.22.e: Ties (the fruits) to a string of three twisted threads and fastens them to her neck with the words, 'Rich in sap is this tree; like the sappy one be thou fruitful.'

1.22.s: atha āha vīṇā gāthinaḥ rājānam saṃgāyata iti yo vā apy anyo vīratara iti |
1.22.d: अथ आह वीणा गाथिनः राजानम् संगायत इति यो वा अप्य् अन्यो वीरतर इति ।

1.22.s: uda pātre akṣatān avaninīya viṣṇur yonim kalpayatu rākām aham iti |
1.22.d: उद पात्रे अक्षतान् अवनिनीय विष्णुर् योनिम् कल्पयतु राकाम् अहम् इति ।

1.22.e: Let him then touch her (with the words),

1.22.s: suparṇo asi garutmāṃs trivṛt te śiro gāyatram cakṣuḥ | chandāṃsy aṅgāni yajūṃṣi nāma sāma te tanūḥ |
1.22.d: सुपर्णो असि गरुत्मांस् त्रिवृत् ते शिरो गायत्रम् चक्षुः । छन्दांस्य् अङ्गानि यजूंषि नाम साम ते तनूः ।
1.22.e: 'The winged one art thou, the Garutmat; the Trivrit (stoma) is thy head, the Gayatra thy eye, the metres thy limbs, the Yagus thy name, the Saman thy body.'
Let him cause her to sing merrily,
Wearing, if she likes, many gold ornaments.
A bull is the fee for the sacrifice.

1.23.s: kākātanyā macakacātanyāḥ kośātakhyā bṛhatyāḥ kālaklītakasya iti mūlāni peṣayitvā upalepayed deśam yasmin prajāyeta rakṣasām apahatyai |
1.23.d: काकातन्या मचकचातन्याः कोशातख्या बृहत्याः कालक्लीतकस्य इति मूलानि पेषयित्वा उपलेपयेद् देशम् यस्मिन् प्रजायेत रक्षसाम् अपहत्यै ।
1.23.e: Let him pound the roots of the plants kakatani, makakakatani, kosataki, of the egg-plant, and of the indigo plant, and besmear (therewith) the place in which she is going to be confined, in order to drive away the Rakshas.

1.24.e: Now the Gatakarman (i.e. ceremony for the new-born child).

1.24.s: jātam kumāram trir abhyavānya anuprāṇyāt ṛcā prāaṇihi yajuṣā samanihi sāmnā udanihi iti |
1.24.d: जातम् कुमारम् त्रिर् अभ्यवान्य अनुप्राण्यात् ऋचा प्राअणिहि यजुषा समनिहि साम्ना उदनिहि इति ।
1.24.e: Let (the father) breathe three times on the new-born child and then draw in his breath with the words, 'Draw in your breath with the Rik, breathe within with the Yagus, breathe forth with the Saman.'

1.24.s: sarpir madhunī dadhy udake ca samninīya brīhi yavau vā samnighṛṣya triḥ prāśayej jāta rūpeṇa |
1.24.d: सर्पिर् मधुनी दध्य् उदके च सम्निनीय ब्रीहि यवौ वा सम्निघृष्य त्रिः प्राशयेज् जात रूपेण ।
1.24.e: Let him mix together butter and honey, milk curds and water, or grind together rice and barley, and give it to eat (to the child) thrice from gold (i.e. from a golden vessel or with a golden spoon),

1.24.s: pra te yacchāmi madhuman makhāya veda prasūtam savitrā maghonā | āyuṣmān gupito devatābhiḥ śatam jīva śarado loke asminn iti | asāv iti nāma asya dadhāti ghoṣavad ādy antar antastham dvy akṣaram catur akṣaram vā api vā ṣaḍ akṣaram kṛtam kuryān na taddhitam |
1.24.d: प्र ते यच्छामि मधुमन् मखाय वेद प्रसूतम् सवित्रा मघोना । आयुष्मान् गुपितो देवताभिः शतम् जीव शरदो लोके अस्मिन्न् इति । असाव् इति नाम अस्य दधाति घोषवद् आद्य् अन्तर् अन्तस्थम् द्व्य् अक्षरम् चतुर् अक्षरम् वा अपि वा षड् अक्षरम् कृतम् कुर्यान् न तद्धितम् ।
1.24.e: With (the verse), 'I administer to thee honey food for the festival, the wisdom ("veda") raised by Savitar the bountiful; long-living, protected by the gods, live a hundred autumns in this world, N.N.!'(with these words) he gives him a name beginning with a sonant, with a semivowel in it, consisting of two syllables, or of four syllables, or also of six syllables; he should take a krit (suffix), not a taddhita.

1.24.s: tad asya pitā mātā ca vidyātām |
1.24.d: तद् अस्य पिता माता च विद्याताम् ।
1.24.e: That (name only) his father and his mother should know.
On the tenth day a name for common use, which is pleasing to the Brahmanas.

1.24.s: goḥ kṛṣṇasya śukla kṛṣṇāni lohitāni ca romāṇi maṣam kārayitvā etasminn eva catuṣṭaye samninīya catuḥ prāśayed iti māṇḍūkeyaḥ |
1.24.d: गोः कृष्णस्य शुक्ल कृष्णानि लोहितानि च रोमाणि मषम् कारयित्वा एतस्मिन्न् एव चतुष्टये सम्निनीय चतुः प्राशयेद् इति माण्डूकेयः ।
1.24.e: Let him pulverise black and white and red hairs of a black ox, intermix (that powder) with those four substances (see Sutra 3), and give it to eat (to the child) four times: such (is the opinion of) Mandukeya.

1.24.s: bhūr ṛgvedam tvayi dadhāmy asau svāhā bhūr bhuvaḥ svar vāko vākyam itihāsa purāṇam om sarvān vedāṃs tvayi dadhāmy asau svāhā iti vā |
1.24.d: भूर् ऋग्वेदम् त्वयि दधाम्य् असौ स्वाहा भूर् भुवः स्वर् वाको वाक्यम् इतिहास पुराणम् ओम् सर्वान् वेदांस् त्वयि दधाम्य् असौ स्वाहा इति वा ।
1.24.e: If he likes (let him do so) with the words, 'Bhuh! The Rig-veda I lay into thee, N.N., svaha! 'Bhuvah! The Yagur-veda I lay into thee, N.N., svaha! 'Svah! The Sama-veda I lay into thee, N.N., svaha! 'Bhur bhuvah svah! Vakovakya (colloquies), Itihasa, and Purana--Om! All the Vedas I lay into thee, N.N., svaha!'

1.24.s: medhā jananam dakṣiṇe karṇe vāg iti triḥ |
1.24.d: मेधा जननम् दक्षिणे कर्णे वाग् इति त्रिः ।
1.24.e: The production of intelligence (is performed) by thrice saying in his right ear, 'Speech!'

1.24.s: vāg devī manasā saṃvidānā prāṇena vatsena saha indra proktā | juṣatama tvā saumanasāya devī mahī mandrā vāṇī vāṇīcī salilā svayambhūr iti | ca anumantrayet |
1.24.d: वाग् देवी मनसा संविदाना प्राणेन वत्सेन सह इन्द्र प्रोक्ता । जुषतम त्वा सौमनसाय देवी मही मन्द्रा वाणी वाणीची सलिला स्वयम्भूर् इति । च अनुमन्त्रयेत् ।
1.24.e: And let him recite over (the child the following text), 'Speech, the goddess, united with mind, together with breath, the child, uttered by Indra--may she rejoice in thee, the goddess, for the sake of joy, the great one, the sweet sounding, the music, full of music, the flowing, self-produced.'
Let him tie a piece of gold to a hempen string,
And bind it to (the child's) right hand until (the mother) gets up (from childbed).
After the tenth day let him give it to the Brahmanas,

1.25.e: After ten days the getting up (of the mother from childbed).

1.25.s: mātā pitarau śiraḥ snātāv ahata vāsasau |
1.25.d: माता पितरौ शिरः स्नाताव् अहत वाससौ ।
1.25.e: Father and mother with washed heads, wearing (new) clothes which have not yet been washed;

1.25.s: etasminn eva sūtikā agnau sthālī pākam śrapayitvā |
1.25.d: एतस्मिन्न् एव सूतिका अग्नौ स्थाली पाकम् श्रपयित्वा ।
1.25.e: Let (the father) cook a mess of food in that same fire that has been kept from her confinement,

1.25.s: janma tithim hutvā trīṇi ca bhāni sadaivatāni |
1.25.d: जन्म तिथिम् हुत्वा त्रीणि च भानि सदैवतानि ।
1.25.e: And let him make oblations to the Tithi of (the child's) birth and to three constellations with their (presiding) deities.

1.25.s: tan madhye juhuyād yasmin jātaḥ syāt pūrvma tu daivatam sarvatra |
1.25.d: तन् मध्ये जुहुयाद् यस्मिन् जातः स्यात् पूर्व्म तु दैवतम् सर्वत्र ।
1.25.e: Let him place in the middle the oblation to that constellation under which (the child) is born; the deity, however, is constantly to precede (the corresponding Nakshatra).

1.25.s: āyuṣ te adya gīrbhir ayam agnir vareṇyaḥ | āyur no dehi jīvase āyurdā agne haviṣā vṛdhāno | ghṛta pratīko ghṛta yonir edhi ghṛtam pītvā madhu cāru gavyam | tvam soma mahe bhagam iti | cd pitā iva putram iha rakṣatād imam iti | daśamī sthālī pākasya |
1.25.d: आयुष् ते अद्य गीर्भिर् अयम् अग्निर् वरेण्यः । आयुर् नो देहि जीवसे आयुर्दा अग्ने हविषा वृधानो । घृत प्रतीको घृत योनिर् एधि घृतम् पीत्वा मधु चारु गव्यम् । त्वम् सोम महे भगम् इति । च्द् पिता इव पुत्रम् इह रक्षताद् इमम् इति । दशमी स्थाली पाकस्य ।
1.25.e: (He then makes two other oblations with the verses,) '(May) this Agni, the excellent one, (give) thee to-day life for (our) prayers; give us life that we may live long,'--(and,) 'Life-giving, Agni, be strong by Havis; may thy face and thy seat be full of ghee; drinking ghee, the sweet honey of the cow, protect, as a father (protects) his son, here N.N.' The tenth oblation of the mess of cooked food with the verse, 'Thou, Soma, givest bliss to the old one' (Rig-veda I, 91, 7).
And caused the Brahmanas to say auspicious words,

1.25.s: evam eva māsi māsi janma tithim hutvā |
1.25.d: एवम् एव मासि मासि जन्म तिथिम् हुत्वा ।
1.25.e: And having sacrificed in the same way every month to the Tithi of (the child's) birth,
He sacrifices, when one year has expired, on the (ordinary) domestic fire.

1.26.e: To Aditi, to the two Punarvasus.
To the Serpents, to the Asleshas.
To the Manes, to the Maghas.
To Bhaga, to the two Phalgunis.
To Aryaman, to the two Phalgunis.
To Indra and Agni, to the two Visakhas.
To the Waters, to the Ashadhas.
To the Visve devas, to the Ashadhas.
To the Vasus, to the Dhanishthas.
To Aga ekapad, to the Proshthapadas.
To Ahi budhnya, to the Proshthapadas.
To the two Asvins, to the two Asvinis.

1.27.e: In the sixth month the Annaprasana (i.e. the first feeding with solid food).
Goat's flesh, if he is desirous of nourishment,
Flesh of partridge, if desirous of holy lustre,
Boiled rice with ghee, if desirous of splendour--

1.27.s: dadhi madhu ghṛta miśram annam prāśayet |
1.27.d: दधि मधु घृत मिश्रम् अन्नम् प्राशयेत् ।
1.27.e: (Such) food, prepared with milk curds, honey, and ghee, he should give (to the child) to eat.

1.27.s: anna pate annasya no dehy amīvasya śuṣṇmiṇaḥ | pra pra dātāram tāriṣa ūrjan no dhehi dvipade ca | yac cidd hi mahaścit | imam agna āyuṣe varcase tigmam ojo varuṇa soma rājan | mātā iva asmā aditiḥ śarma yaṃsad viśve devā jarad aṣṭir yathā asad iti hutvā |
1.27.d: अन्न पते अन्नस्य नो देह्य् अमीवस्य शुष्ण्मिणः । प्र प्र दातारम् तारिष ऊर्जन् नो धेहि द्विपदे च । यच् चिद्द् हि महश्चित् । इमम् अग्न आयुषे वर्चसे तिग्मम् ओजो वरुण सोम राजन् । माता इव अस्मा अदितिः शर्म यंसद् विश्वे देवा जरद् अष्टिर् यथा असद् इति हुत्वा ।
1.27.e: After he has made oblations with (the verses), 'Lord of food, give us food, painless and strong; bring forward the giver; bestow power on us, on men and animals;' 'Whatsoever' (Rig-veda IV, 12, 4); 'Even of great' (ibid. 5), 'Him, Agni, (lead) to long life and splendour; sharp strength (mayst thou), Varuna, king Soma, protection may Aditi, like a mother, afford to him, and all the gods that he may reach old age'--
And has recited over (the child) the verse, 'Powers of life, Agni' (Rig-veda IX, 66, 19),

1.27.s: udag agreṣu kuśeṣu syonā pṛthivi bhava iti upaveśya |
1.27.d: उदग् अग्रेषु कुशेषु स्योना पृथिवि भव इति उपवेश्य ।
1.27.e: And has set him down on northward pointed Kusa grass with (the verse), 'Be soft, O earth' (Rig-veda I, 22, 15)--
The act of feeding is performed with the Mahavyahritis.
Let the mother eat the remnant.

1.28.s: saṃvatsare cūḍā karma |
1.28.d: संवत्सरे चूडा कर्म ।
1.28.e: After one year the Kudakarman (i.e. the tonsure of the child's head);

1.28.s: tṛtīye vā varṣe |
1.28.d: तृतीये वा वर्षे ।
1.28.e: Or in the third year;

1.28.s: pañcame kṣatriyasya |
1.28.d: पञ्चमे क्षत्रियस्य ।
1.28.e: In the fifth for a Kshatriya;

1.28.s: saptame vaiśyasya |
1.28.d: सप्तमे वैश्यस्य ।
1.28.e: In the seventh for a Vaisya.

1.28.s: agnim upasamādhāya |
1.28.d: अग्निम् उपसमाधाय ।
1.28.e: Having placed the fire (in the outer hall; see chap. 5, 2)--

1.28.s: vrīhi yavānām tila māṣāṇām iti pātrāṇi ca pūrayitvā |
1.28.d: व्रीहि यवानाम् तिल माषाणाम् इति पात्राणि च पूरयित्वा ।
1.28.e: And having filled vessels with rice and barley, sesamum seeds and beans,

1.28.s: ānaḍuham ca gomayam kuśa bhittam ca keśa pratigrahaṇāya ādarśan nava nītam loha kṣuram ca uttarata upasthāpya |
1.28.d: आनडुहम् च गोमयम् कुश भित्तम् च केश प्रतिग्रहणाय आदर्शन् नव नीतम् लोह क्षुरम् च उत्तरत उपस्थाप्य ।
1.28.e: And having put down northwards bull-dung and a layer of Kusa grass for receiving the hair, a mirror, fresh butter, and a razor of copper,

1.28.s: sampṛcyadhvam ṛtāvarīr ūrmiṇā madhumattamāḥ | pṛñcatīr madhunā payo mandrā dhanasya sātaya iti | uṣṇāsv apsu śītā āsiñcati |
1.28.d: सम्पृच्यध्वम् ऋतावरीर् ऊर्मिणा मधुमत्तमाः । पृञ्चतीर् मधुना पयो मन्द्रा धनस्य सातय इति । उष्णास्व् अप्सु शीता आसिञ्चति ।
1.28.e: He pours cold water into warm with (the verse), 'Mix yourselves, ye holy ones, with your waves, ye honied ones, mixing milk with honey, ye lovely ones, for the obtaining of wealth.'

1.28.s: āpa undantu jīvase dīrgha āyutvāya varcase | tryāyuṣam jamadagneḥ paśyapasya tryāyuṣam | agastyasya tryāyuṣam yad devānām tryāyuṣam | tat te karomi tryāyuṣam iti | asāv iti śīṭa uṣṇābhir adbhir dakṣiṇam keśa pakṣam trir abhyanakti |
1.28.d: आप उन्दन्तु जीवसे दीर्घ आयुत्वाय वर्चसे । त्र्यायुषम् जमदग्नेः पश्यपस्य त्र्यायुषम् । अगस्त्यस्य त्र्यायुषम् यद् देवानाम् त्र्यायुषम् । तत् ते करोमि त्र्यायुषम् इति । असाव् इति शीट उष्णाभिर् अद्भिर् दक्षिणम् केश पक्षम् त्रिर् अभ्यनक्ति ।
1.28.e: 'May the waters moisten thee for life, for old age and splendour. The threefold age of Gamadagni, Kasyapa's threefold age, the threefold age of [paragraph continues] Agastya, the threefold age that belongs to the gods, that threefold age I produce for thee! N.N.!'--with these words he sprinkles the right part of his hair three times with lukewarm water.

1.28.s: śalalyā eke vijaṭān kṛtvā |
1.28.d: शलल्या एके विजटान् कृत्वा ।
1.28.e: Having loosened the tangled locks, according to some (teachers), with a porcupine's quill,

1.28.s: nava nītena abhyajya |
1.28.d: नव नीतेन अभ्यज्य ।
1.28.e: And having anointed (his hair)with fresh butter,

1.28.s: oṣadhe trāyasva enam iti kuśa taruṇam antar dadhāti |
1.28.d: ओषधे त्रायस्व एनम् इति कुश तरुणम् अन्तर् दधाति ।
1.28.e: He puts a young Kusa shoot among (the hairs) with the words, 'Herb, protect him!'

1.28.s: keśān kuśa taruṇam ca ādarśena saṃspṛśya |
1.28.d: केशान् कुश तरुणम् च आदर्शेन संस्पृश्य ।
1.28.e: Having touched the hair and the Kusa shoot with the mirror,

1.28.s: tejo asi svadhitiṣ ṭe pitā mā enam hiṃsīr iti loha kṣuram ādatte |
1.28.d: तेजो असि स्वधितिष् टे पिता मा एनम् हिंसीर् इति लोह क्षुरम् आदत्ते ।
1.28.e: He takes up the copper razor with the words, Sharpness art thou; the axe is thy father. Do no harm to him!'

1.28.s: yena āvapat savitā śmaśrv agre kṣureṇa rājño varuṇasya vidvān yena dhātā bṛhaspatir indrasya ca āvapat śiraḥ | tena brahmāṇo vapata idam adya āyuṣmān dīrgha āyur ayam astu vīro asāv iti keśa agrāṇi chinatti kuśa taruṇam ca |
1.28.d: येन आवपत् सविता श्मश्र्व् अग्रे क्षुरेण राज्ञो वरुणस्य विद्वान् येन धाता बृहस्पतिर् इन्द्रस्य च आवपत् शिरः । तेन ब्रह्माणो वपत इदम् अद्य आयुष्मान् दीर्घ आयुर् अयम् अस्तु वीरो असाव् इति केश अग्राणि छिनत्ति कुश तरुणम् च ।
1.28.e: With (the words), 'The razor with which in the beginning Savitar, the knowing one, has shaven the beard of king Varuna, and with which Dhatar Brihaspati has shaven Indra's head, with that, ye Brahmanas, shave this (head) to-day; blessed with long life, with old age be this man N.N.!' he cuts the tips of the hairs and the Kusa shoot.

1.28.s: evam dvitīyam evam tṛtīyam |
1.28.d: एवम् द्वितीयम् एवम् तृतीयम् ।
1.28.e: In the same way a second time; in the same way a third time.

1.28.s: evma dvir uttarataḥ |
1.28.d: एव्म द्विर् उत्तरतः ।
1.28.e: In the same way twice on the left side.

1.28.s: nikakṣayoḥ ṣaṣṭha saptame go dāna karmaṇi |
1.28.d: निकक्षयोः षष्ठ सप्तमे गो दान कर्मणि ।
1.28.e: Under the armpits a sixth and a seventh time at the Godanakarman (ceremony of shaving the beard).

1.28.s: etad ea go dāna karma yac cūḍā karma |
1.28.d: एतद् एअ गो दान कर्म यच् चूडा कर्म ।
1.28.e: The Godanakarman is identical with the Kudakarman,

1.28.s: ṣoḍaśe varṣe aṣṭādaśe vā |
1.28.d: षोडशे वर्षे अष्टादशे वा ।
1.28.e: (It is to be performed) in the sixteenth or in the eighteenth year.

1.28.s: tṛtīye tu pravapane gām dadāty ahatam ca vāsaḥ |
1.28.d: तृतीये तु प्रवपने गाम् ददात्य् अहतम् च वासः ।
1.28.e: At the third turn of shaving, however, he gives a cow and a garment that has not yet been washed.

1.28.s: tūṣṇīm āvṛtaḥ kanyānām |
1.28.d: तूष्णीम् आवृतः कन्यानाम् ।
1.28.e: Silently the rites (are performed) for girls.

1.28.s: prāg udīcyām diśi bahv aoṣadhike deśe apām vā samīpe keśān nikhananti |
1.28.d: प्राग् उदीच्याम् दिशि बह्व् अओषधिके देशे अपाम् वा समीपे केशान् निखनन्ति ।
1.28.e: To the north-east, in a place covered with herbs, or in the neighbourhood of water they bury the hairs in the earth.

1.28.s: nāpitāya dhānya pātrāṇi nāpitāya dhānya pātrāṇi |
1.28.d: नापिताय धान्य पात्राणि नापिताय धान्य पात्राणि ।
1.28.e: To the barber the vessels of grain. To the barber the vessels of grain.

2.1.e: In the eighth year after the conception let him initiate a Brahmana,
With an antelope-skin,
Or in the tenth year after the conception.
In the eleventh year after the conception a Kshatriya with the skin of a spotted deer,
In the twelfth year after the conception a Vaisya with a cow-hide.

2.1.s: ā ṣoḍaśād varṣād brāhmaṇasya anatītaḥ kālaḥ |
2.1.d: आ षोडशाद् वर्षाद् ब्राह्मणस्य अनतीतः कालः ।
2.1.e: Until the sixteenth year the time has not passed for a Brahmana,
Until the twenty-second for a Kshatriya,
Until the twenty-fourth for a Vaisya.
After that (time has passed), they become patitasavitrika (men who have lost their right of learning the Savitri).
Let them not initiate such men,
Nor teach them,
Nor perform sacrifices for them,
Nor have intercourse with them.
Or (let them initiate students of) all (castes) wearing a (new) garment that has not yet been washed. And wearing a girdle.
The girdle of a Brahmana (shall be) made of Munga grass,
That of a Kshatriya (shall be) a bowstring,
That of a Vaisya a woollen thread.
The staff of a Brahmana (shall be) made of Palasa or of Bilva wood,
That of a Kshatriya of Nyagrodha wood,
That of a Vaisya of Udumbara wood.
That of the Brahmana shall reach the tip of the nose,
That of the Kshatriya the forehead,
That of the Vaisya the hair.
Or all (sorts of staffs are to be used) by (men of) all (castes).

2.1.s: yena abaddhena upanayeta ācārya adhīnam tat |
2.1.d: येन अबद्धेन उपनयेत आचार्य अधीनम् तत् ।
2.1.e: Whatsoever (the student) wears at his initiation, is at the disposal of the teacher.
Having had him shaved all round (his head) he should initiate him.
After (the student) has washed and adorned himself,

2.1.s: hutvā jaghanena agnim tiṣṭhataḥ prān mukha ācāryaḥ pratyan mukha itaraḥ |
2.1.d: हुत्वा जघनेन अग्निम् तिष्ठतः प्रान् मुख आचार्यः प्रत्यन् मुख इतरः ।
2.1.e: (And) after (the teacher) has sacrificed, both station themselves behind the fire, the teacher with his face turned to the east, the other with his face to the west.
Let him initiate him standing while (the other also) stands.

2.1.s: mitrasya cakṣur dharuṇam balīyas tejo yaśasvi sthaviram samṛddham | anāhanasyam vasanam cariṣṇu pari idam vājy ajinam dadhe aham |
2.1.d: मित्रस्य चक्षुर् धरुणम् बलीयस् तेजो यशस्वि स्थविरम् समृद्धम् । अनाहनस्यम् वसनम् चरिष्णु परि इदम् वाज्य् अजिनम् दधे अहम् ।
2.1.e: ['The firm, powerful eye of Mitra, glorious splendour, strong and prosperous, a chaste, flowing vesture, this skin I put on, a valiant (man).']

2.2.s: iyam duruktāt paribādhamānā varṇam pavitram punatī na āgāt | prāṇa apānābhyām balam āviśantī sakhā devī subhagā mekhalā iyam iti | trir mekhalām pradakṣiṇam triḥ pariveṣṭya
2.2.d: इयम् दुरुक्तात् परिबाधमाना वर्णम् पवित्रम् पुनती न आगात् । प्राण अपानाभ्याम् बलम् आविशन्ती सखा देवी सुभगा मेखला इयम् इति । त्रिर् मेखलाम् प्रदक्षिणम् त्रिः परिवेष्ट्य
2.2.e: 'Here has come to us, protecting (us) from evil words, purifying our kin as a purifier, clothing herself, by (the power of) inhalation and exhalation, with strength, this friendly goddess, this blessed girdle'--with these words, three times repeated, he ties the girdle from left to right thrice round.

2.2.s: granthir ekas trayo api vā api vā pañca |
2.2.d: ग्रन्थिर् एकस् त्रयो अपि वा अपि वा पञ्च ।
2.2.e: (There should be) one knot, or also three, or also five.

2.2.s: yajña upavītam kṛtvā yajña upavītam asi yajñasya tvā upavītena upa nahyāmi iti |
2.2.d: यज्ञ उपवीतम् कृत्वा यज्ञ उपवीतम् असि यज्ञस्य त्वा उपवीतेन उप नह्यामि इति ।
2.2.e: He adjusts the sacrificial cord with (the words), 'The sacrificial cord art thou. With the cord of the sacrifice I invest thee.'

2.2.s: añjalī pūrayitvā atha enam āha ko nāma asi iti |
2.2.d: अञ्जली पूरयित्वा अथ एनम् आह को नाम असि इति ।
2.2.e: He fills the two hollows of (his own and the student's) joined hands (with water), and then says to him: 'What is thy name?'
'I am N.N., sir,' says the other.
'Descending from the same Rishis?' says the teacher.

2.2.s: samāna ārṣeyo aham bho iti itaraḥ |
2.2.d: समान आर्षेयो अहम् भो इति इतरः ।
2.2.e: 'Descending from the same Rishis, sir,' says the other.

2.2.s: brahma cāry aham bho iti itaraḥ |
2.2.d: ब्रह्म चार्य् अहम् भो इति इतरः ।
2.2.e: 'I am a student, sir,' says the other.

2.2.s: bhūr bhuvaḥ svar iti asyā añjalāv añjalīṃs trīn āsicya |
2.2.d: भूर् भुवः स्वर् इति अस्या अञ्जलाव् अञ्जलींस् त्रीन् आसिच्य ।
2.2.e: With the words, 'Bhur bhuvah svah' (the teacher) sprinkles thrice with his joined hands (water) on the joined hands (of the student),

2.2.s: dakṣiṇa uttarābhyām pāṇibhyām pāṇī saṃgṛhya japati |
2.2.d: दक्षिण उत्तराभ्याम् पाणिभ्याम् पाणी संगृह्य जपति ।
2.2.e: And seizing (the student's) hands with (his own) hands, holding the right uppermost, he murmurs,

2.2.s: devasya tvā savituḥ prasave aśvinor bāhubhyām pūṣṇo hastābhyām upanayāmy asāv iti |
2.2.d: देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे अश्विनोर् बाहुभ्याम् पूष्णो हस्ताभ्याम् उपनयाम्य् असाव् इति ।
2.2.e: 'By the impulse of the god Savitar, with the arms of the two Asvins, with Pushan's hands I initiate thee, N.N.'
Those who are desirous of a host (of adherents, he should initiate) with (the verse), 'Thee, (the lord) of hosts' (Rig-veda II, 23, 1).

2.2.s: gā gantā mā riṣaṇyata iti yodhān |
2.2.d: गा गन्ता मा रिषण्यत इति योधान् ।
2.2.e: Warriors with (the verse), 'Come here, do not come to harm' (Rig-veda VIII, 20, 1).

2.3.s: bhagas te hastam agrabhīt savitā hastam agrabhīt | pūṣā te hastam agrabhīd aryamā hastam agrabhīt | mitras tvam asi dharmaṇā agnir ācāryas tava | asāv aham ca ubhau agna etam te brahma cāriṇam pari dadāmi indra etam te brahma cāriṇam pari dadāmi āditya etam te brahma cāriṇam pari dadāmi viśve devā etam vo brahma cāriṇam pari dadāmi dīrgha āyutvāya suprajāstvāya suvīryāya rāyas poṣāya sarveṣām vedānām ādhipatyāya suślokyāya svastaye |
2.3.d: भगस् ते हस्तम् अग्रभीत् सविता हस्तम् अग्रभीत् । पूषा ते हस्तम् अग्रभीद् अर्यमा हस्तम् अग्रभीत् । मित्रस् त्वम् असि धर्मणा अग्निर् आचार्यस् तव । असाव् अहम् च उभौ अग्न एतम् ते ब्रह्म चारिणम् परि ददामि इन्द्र एतम् ते ब्रह्म चारिणम् परि ददामि आदित्य एतम् ते ब्रह्म चारिणम् परि ददामि विश्वे देवा एतम् वो ब्रह्म चारिणम् परि ददामि दीर्घ आयुत्वाय सुप्रजास्त्वाय सुवीर्याय रायस् पोषाय सर्वेषाम् वेदानाम् आधिपत्याय सुश्लोक्याय स्वस्तये ।
2.3.e: 'Bhaga has seized thy hand, Savitar has seized thy hand, Pushan has seized thy hand, Aryaman has seized thy hand. Mitra art thou by right, Agni is thy teacher, and I, N.N., both of us. Agni, I give this student in charge to thee. Indra, I give this student in charge to thee. Sun, I give this student in charge to thee. Visve devas, I give this student in charge to you, for the sake of long life, of blessed offspring and strength, of increase of wealth, of mastership of all Vedas, of renown, of bliss.'

2.3.s: aindrīm āvṛtam āvarta ādityasya āvṛtam anvāvarta iti dakṣiṇam bāhum anvāvṛtya |
2.3.d: ऐन्द्रीम् आवृतम् आवर्त आदित्यस्य आवृतम् अन्वावर्त इति दक्षिणम् बाहुम् अन्वावृत्य ।
2.3.e: 'In Indra's course I move; in the sun's course I move after him'--with these words he turns round from left to right,

2.3.s: dakṣiṇena prādeśena dakṣiṇam aṃsam anvavahṛtya ariṣyatas te hṛdayasya priyo bhūyāsam iti hṛdaya deśam abhimṛśati |
2.3.d: दक्षिणेन प्रादेशेन दक्षिणम् अंसम् अन्ववहृत्य अरिष्यतस् ते हृदयस्य प्रियो भूयासम् इति हृदय देशम् अभिमृशति ।
2.3.e: And grasping down with the span of his right hand over (the student's) right shoulder he touches the place of his heart with the words, 'May I be dear to thy inviolate heart.'
Having silently turned round from right to left,

2.3.s: atha asya ūrdhva aṅgulim pāṇim hṛdaye nidhāya japati |
2.3.d: अथ अस्य ऊर्ध्व अङ्गुलिम् पाणिम् हृदये निधाय जपति ।
2.3.e: And then laying his hand with the fingers upwards on his (i.e. the student's) heart, he murmurs:

2.4.s: mama vrate hṛdayam te dadhāmi mama cittam anu cittam te astu | mama vācam eka manā juṣasva bṛhaspatiṣṭ tvā niyunaktu mahyām ati |
2.4.d: मम व्रते हृदयम् ते दधामि मम चित्तम् अनु चित्तम् ते अस्तु । मम वाचम् एक मना जुषस्व बृहस्पतिष्ट् त्वा नियुनक्तु मह्याम् अति ।
2.4.e: 'Under my will I take thy heart; my mind shall thy mind follow; in my word thou shalt rejoice with all thy heart; may Brihaspati join thee to me.'
'Thou art the Brahmakarin of Kama, N.N.!'

2.4.s: tena eva mantreṇa tathā eva paryāvṛtya |
2.4.d: तेन एव मन्त्रेण तथा एव पर्यावृत्य ।
2.4.e: With the same text (see chap. 3, 2) he turns round as before,

2.4.s: dakṣiṇena prādeśena dakṣiṇam aṃsam anvārabhya japati |
2.4.d: दक्षिणेन प्रादेशेन दक्षिणम् अंसम् अन्वारभ्य जपति ।
2.4.e: And touching with the span of his right hand (the student's) right shoulder, he murmurs:

2.4.s: brahma cāry asi samidham ā dhehi apo aśāna karma kuru mā divā suṣupthāḥ vācam yaccha ā samid ādhānāt |
2.4.d: ब्रह्म चार्य् असि समिधम् आ धेहि अपो अशान कर्म कुरु मा दिवा सुषुप्थाः वाचम् यच्छ आ समिद् आधानात् ।
2.4.e: 'A student art thou. Put on fuel. Eat water. Do the service. Do not sleep in the day-time. Keep silence till the putting on of fuel.'

2.4.s: eṣā te agne samid iti abhyādadhāti samidham tūṣṇīm vā |
2.4.d: एषा ते अग्ने समिद् इति अभ्यादधाति समिधम् तूष्णीम् वा ।
2.4.e: With (the words), 'Thine, Agni, is this piece of wood,' he puts the fuel on (the fire), or silently.

2.5.e: After one year (the teacher) recites the Savitri (to the student),
Let him recite a Gayatri to a Brahmana,
But let it be anyhow a verse sacred to Savitar.
They seat themselves to the north of the fire,

2.5.s: prān mukha ācāryaḥ pratyan mukha itaraḥ |
2.5.d: प्रान् मुख आचार्यः प्रत्यन् मुख इतरः ।
2.5.e: The teacher with his face turned eastward, the other westward.

2.5.s: ācārya om kāram prayujya atha itaram vācayati sāvitrī bho anubrūhi iti |
2.5.d: आचार्य ओम् कारम् प्रयुज्य अथ इतरम् वाचयति सावित्री भो अनुब्रूहि इति ।
2.5.e: The teacher, having pronounced the word OM, then causes the other one to say, 'Recite the Savitri, sir!'

2.5.s: atha asmai sāvitrīm anvāha tat savitur vareṇyam iti etām pacco ardharcaśo anavānam |
