2.5.d: अथ अस्मै सावित्रीम् अन्वाह तत् सवितुर् वरेण्यम् इति एताम् पच्चो अर्धर्चशो अनवानम् ।
2.5.e: He then recites the Savitri to him, the verse 'That glorious (splendour) of Savitar' (Rig-Veda III, 62, 10); (firstly) pada by pada, (then) hemistich by hemistich, (and finally) without a stop.

2.6.s: āpo nāma stha śivā nāma stha | ūrjā nāma stha ajarā nāma stha | abhayā nāma stha amṛtā nāma stha | tāsām vo aśīya sumatau mā dhatta iti evam trir apa ācāmayya |
2.6.d: आपो नाम स्थ शिवा नाम स्थ । ऊर्जा नाम स्थ अजरा नाम स्थ । अभया नाम स्थ अमृता नाम स्थ । तासाम् वो अशीय सुमतौ मा धत्त इति एवम् त्रिर् अप आचामय्य ।
2.6.e: 'Waters are ye by name; happy ones are ye by name; sappy ones are ye by name; undecaying ones are ye by name; fearless ones are ye by name; immortal ones are ye by name. Of you, being such, may I partake; receive me into your favour'--with these words (the teacher) makes the student sip water three times,

2.6.s: svasti no mimītām iti pañcarcena daṇḍam prayacchati |
2.6.d: स्वस्ति नो मिमीताम् इति पञ्चर्चेन दण्डम् प्रयच्छति ।
2.6.e: And hands over to him the staff with the five verses, 'Blessing may give us' (Rig-veda V, 51, 11-15).
An optional gift is the fee for the sacrifice.
After (the teacher) has led him round the fire, turning his right side towards it, (the student) goes through the village to beg food.
(Let him beg,) however, of his mother first,
Or of a woman who will not refuse.

2.6.s: ācāryāya bhaikṣyam nivedayitvā anujñāto guruṇā bhuñjīta |
2.6.d: आचार्याय भैक्ष्यम् निवेदयित्वा अनुज्ञातो गुरुणा भुञ्जीत ।
2.6.e: Having announced the alms to his teacher, he may eat (the food himself) with the master's permission.

2.6.s: ahar ahaḥ samid ādhānam bhikṣā caraṇam adhaḥ śayyā guru śuśrūṣā iti brahma cāriṇo nityāni |
2.6.d: अहर् अहः समिद् आधानम् भिक्षा चरणम् अधः शय्या गुरु शुश्रूषा इति ब्रह्म चारिणो नित्यानि ।
2.6.e: The daily putting on of fuel, the going for alms, the sleeping on the ground, and obedience to the teacher: these are the standing duties of a student.

2.7.s: atha anuvācanasya |
2.7.d: अथ अनुवाचनस्य ।
2.7.e: Now (follows the exposition) of the study of the Veda.

2.7.s: agner uttarata upaviśataḥ |
2.7.d: अग्नेर् उत्तरत उपविशतः ।
2.7.e: Both sit down to the north of the fire,

2.7.s: prān mukha ācāryaḥ pratyan mukha itaraḥ |
2.7.d: प्रान् मुख आचार्यः प्रत्यन् मुख इतरः ।
2.7.e: The teacher with his face to the east, the other one to the west.

2.7.s: abhivādya pādāv ācāryasya pāṇī prakṣālya |
2.7.d: अभिवाद्य पादाव् आचार्यस्य पाणी प्रक्षाल्य ।
2.7.e: After (the student) has reverentially saluted the teacher's feet and has sprinkled his (own) hands (with water),

2.7.s: dakṣiṇena jānunā ākramya mūle kuśa truṇān |
2.7.d: दक्षिणेन जानुना आक्रम्य मूले कुश त्रुणान् ।
2.7.e: And has kneeled down with his right knee on young Kusa shoots at their roots,

2.7.s: dakṣiṇa uttarābhyām pāṇibhyām madhye parigṛhya |
2.7.d: दक्षिण उत्तराभ्याम् पाणिभ्याम् मध्ये परिगृह्य ।
2.7.e: And has grasped round (those Kusa shoots) in 'heir middle with his hands, holding the right uppermost,

2.7.s: tānt savyena ācāryo agre saṃgṛhya dakṣiṇena adbhiḥ pariṣiñcann atha itaram vācayati |
2.7.d: तान्त् सव्येन आचार्यो अग्रे संगृह्य दक्षिणेन अद्भिः परिषिञ्चन्न् अथ इतरम् वाचयति ।
2.7.e: The teacher, having seized them at their tops with his left hand, and with his right hand sprinkling them with water, then makes the other say:

2.7.s: sāvitrīm bho anubrūni iti itaraḥ |
2.7.d: सावित्रीम् भो अनुब्रूनि इति इतरः ।
2.7.e: 'Recite the Savitri, sir!' says the other.

2.7.s: sāvitrīm te anubravīmi iti ācāryaḥ |
2.7.d: सावित्रीम् ते अनुब्रवीमि इति आचार्यः ।
2.7.e: 'I recite the Savitri to thee!' says the teacher.

2.7.s: gāyatrīm bho anubrūhi iti itaraḥ gāyatrīm te anubravīmi iti ācāryaḥ |
2.7.d: गायत्रीम् भो अनुब्रूहि इति इतरः गायत्रीम् ते अनुब्रवीमि इति आचार्यः ।
2.7.e: 'Recite the Gayatri, sir!' says the other. 'I recite the Gayatri to thee!' says the teacher.

2.7.s: vaiśvāmitrīm bho anubrūhi iti itaraḥ vaiśvāmitrīm te anubravīmi iti ācāryaḥ |
2.7.d: वैश्वामित्रीम् भो अनुब्रूहि इति इतरः वैश्वामित्रीम् ते अनुब्रवीमि इति आचार्यः ।
2.7.e: 'Recite the verse of Visvamitra, sir!' says the other. 'I recite the verse of Visvamitra to thee!' says the teacher.

2.7.s: ṛṣīn bho anubrūhi iti itaraḥ devatās te anubravīmi iti ācāryaḥ |
2.7.d: ऋषीन् भो अनुब्रूहि इति इतरः देवतास् ते अनुब्रवीमि इति आचार्यः ।
2.7.e: 'Recite the Rishis, sir!' says the other. I recite the Rishis to thee!' says the teacher.

2.7.s: devatā bho anubrūhi iti itaraḥ devatās te anubravīmi iti ācāryaḥ |
2.7.d: देवता भो अनुब्रूहि इति इतरः देवतास् ते अनुब्रवीमि इति आचार्यः ।
2.7.e: 'Recite the deities, sir!' says the other. 'I recite the deities to thee!' says the teacher.

2.7.s: chandāṃsi bho anubrūhi iti itaraḥ chandāṃsi te anubravīmi iti ācāryaḥ |
2.7.d: छन्दांसि भो अनुब्रूहि इति इतरः छन्दांसि ते अनुब्रवीमि इति आचार्यः ।
2.7.e: 'Recite the metres, sir!' says the other. 'I recite the metres to thee!' says the teacher.

2.7.s: śrutim bho anubrūhi iti itaraḥ śrutim te anubravīmi iti ācāryaḥ |
2.7.d: श्रुतिम् भो अनुब्रूहि इति इतरः श्रुतिम् ते अनुब्रवीमि इति आचार्यः ।
2.7.e: 'Recite the Sruti, sir!' says the other. 'I recite the Sruti to thee!' says the teacher.

2.7.s: smṛtim bho anubrūhi iti itaraḥ smṛtim e anubravīmi iti ācāryaḥ |
2.7.d: स्मृतिम् भो अनुब्रूहि इति इतरः स्मृतिम् ए अनुब्रवीमि इति आचार्यः ।
2.7.e: 'Recite the Smriti, sir!' says the other. 'I recite the Smriti to thee!' says the teacher.

2.7.s: śraddhā medhe bho anubrūhi iti itaraḥ śraddhā medhe anubravīmi iti ācāryaḥ |
2.7.d: श्रद्धा मेधे भो अनुब्रूहि इति इतरः श्रद्धा मेधे अनुब्रवीमि इति आचार्यः ।
2.7.e: 'Recite faith and insight, sir!' says the other. 'I recite faith and insight to thee!' says the teacher.

2.7.s: evam evam ṛṣer yasya yasya yo yo mantro yad devatyo yac chandāś ca tathā tathā tam tam mantram anubrūyāt |
2.7.d: एवम् एवम् ऋषेर् यस्य यस्य यो यो मन्त्रो यद् देवत्यो यच् छन्दाश् च तथा तथा तम् तम् मन्त्रम् अनुब्रूयात् ।
2.7.e: In that way, according to what Rishi each hymn belongs to and what its deity and its metre is, thus (with the corresponding indications of Rishi, &c.) let him recite each hymn;

2.7.s: api vā avindann ṛṣi daivata chandāṃsi tat savitur vareṇyam iti etām paccho ardharcaśo anavānam ity eṣā iti samāpta āha ācāryaḥ |
2.7.d: अपि वा अविन्दन्न् ऋषि दैवत छन्दांसि तत् सवितुर् वरेण्यम् इति एताम् पच्छो अर्धर्चशो अनवानम् इत्य् एषा इति समाप्त आह आचार्यः ।
2.7.e: Or also, if he does not know the Rishis, deities, and metres, the teacher recites this verse, 'That glorious (splendour) of Savitar' (Rig-veda III, 62, 10), pada by pada, hemistich by hemistich, (and finally) without a stop, and says, when he has finished, 'This (verse belongs to Savitar; it is a Gayatri; Visvamitra is its Rishi).'

2.7.s: evam eka ekam ṛṣim anuvākam vā anubrūyāt |
2.7.d: एवम् एक एकम् ऋषिम् अनुवाकम् वा अनुब्रूयात् ।
2.7.e: Let him thus recite (the hymns belonging to) each Rishi, or (each) Anuvaka;

2.7.s: kṣudra sūkteṣv anuvākam |
2.7.d: क्षुद्र सूक्तेष्व् अनुवाकम् ।
2.7.e: Of the short hymns (in the tenth Mandala) an Anuvaka,

2.7.s: yāvad vā gurur manyeta |
2.7.d: यावद् वा गुरुर् मन्येत ।
2.7.e: Or as much as the master may think fit.

2.7.s: ādya uttame kāmam sūkte vā anubrūyād ṛṣeḥ |
2.7.d: आद्य उत्तमे कामम् सूक्ते वा अनुब्रूयाद् ऋषेः ।
2.7.e: Or optionally he may recite the first and last hymn of (each) Rishi,

2.7.s: anuvākasya vā |
2.7.d: अनुवाकस्य वा ।
2.7.e: Or of (each) Anuvaka,

2.7.s: eka ekām sūkta ādāv iti |
2.7.d: एक एकाम् सूक्त आदाव् इति ।
2.7.e: (Or) one (verse) of the beginning of each hymn.

2.7.s: eṣā prabhṛtir iti kāmam sūkta ādāv ācārya iti |
2.7.d: एषा प्रभृतिर् इति कामम् सूक्त आदाव् आचार्य इति ।
2.7.e: The teacher may optionally say at the beginning of the hymn, 'This is the commencement.'

2.7.s: etad ṛṣi svādhyāye vyākhyātam |
2.7.d: एतद् ऋषि स्वाध्याये व्याख्यातम् ।
2.7.e: This has been (further) explained in (the treatise about) the Rishisvadhyaya.

2.7.s: samāpte kuśa taruṇān ādāya anaḍuhena mūle kuṇḍam kṛtvā yathā sūktam kuśeṣv apo niṣiñcati |
2.7.d: समाप्ते कुश तरुणान् आदाय अनडुहेन मूले कुण्डम् कृत्वा यथा सूक्तम् कुशेष्व् अपो निषिञ्चति ।
2.7.e: When (the lesson) is finished, he takes the young Kusa shoots, makes of cow-dung a pit at their roots, and sprinkles water on the Kusa (shoots) for each hymn.

2.7.s: ahaḥ śeṣam sthānam upavāsaś ca |
2.7.d: अहः शेषम् स्थानम् उपवासश् च ।
2.7.e: For the rest of the day standing and fasting.

2.8.s: apara ahṇe akṣata dhānā bhikṣitvā ājya āhuti dharmeṇa agnau pāṇinā juhuyāt sadasas aptim adbhutam iti pratyṛcam sūkta śeṣeṇa |
2.8.d: अपर अह्णे अक्षत धाना भिक्षित्वा आज्य आहुति धर्मेण अग्नौ पाणिना जुहुयात् सदसस् अप्तिम् अद्भुतम् इति प्रत्यृचम् सूक्त शेषेण ।
2.8.e: In the afternoon, having obtained by begging fried barley grains, he shall sacrifice them with his hand on the fire according to the rites of the Agya oblations with the text, 'The lord of the seat, the wonderful' (Rig-veda I, 18, 6 seq.), verse by verse, down to the end of the hymn,
Causing the teacher by (the gift of) food to pronounce auspicious wishes.

2.9.s: araṇye samit pāṇiḥ saṃdhyām āste nityam vāg yata uttara apara abhimukho anvaṣṭamadeśam ā nakṣatrāṇām darśanāt |
2.9.d: अरण्ये समित् पाणिः संध्याम् आस्ते नित्यम् वाग् यत उत्तर अपर अभिमुखो अन्वष्टमदेशम् आ नक्षत्राणाम् दर्शनात् ।
2.9.e: In the forest, with a piece of wood in his hand, seated, he performs the Sandhya (or twilight devotion) constantly, observing silence, turning his face north-west, to the region between the chief (west) point and the intermediate (north-western) point (of the horizon), until the stars appear,

2.9.s: atikrāntāyām mahā vyāhṛtīḥ sāvitrīm svastyayanāni ca japitvā |
2.9.d: अतिक्रान्तायाम् महा व्याहृतीः सावित्रीम् स्वस्त्ययनानि च जपित्वा ।
2.9.e: Murmuring, when (the twilight) has passed, the Mahavyahritis, the Savitri, and the auspicious hymns.

2.9.s: evam prātaḥ prān mukhas tiṣṭhann ā maṇḍala darśanāt |
2.9.d: एवम् प्रातः प्रान् मुखस् तिष्ठन्न् आ मण्डल दर्शनात् ।
2.9.e: In the same way in the morning, turning his face to the east, standing, until the disk of the sun appears. 10, 1 . When (the sun) has risen, the study (of the Veda) goes on.

2.10.s: agnim upasamādhāya parisamuhya paryukṣya dakṣiṇam jānv ācya |
2.10.d: अग्निम् उपसमाधाय परिसमुह्य पर्युक्ष्य दक्षिणम् जान्व् आच्य ।

2.10.s: agnaye samidham ahārṣam bṛhate jāta vedase | sa me śraddhām ca medhām ca jāta vedā prayacchatu svāhā | edho asy edhiṣīmahi samad asi tejo asi tejo mayi dhehi svāhā | samiddho mām samardhaya prajayā ca dhanena ca svāhā || eṣā te agne samit tayā vardhasva ca ā ca pyāyasva | vardhiṣīmahi ca vayam ā ca pyāsiṣīmahi svāhā iti |
2.10.d: अग्नये समिधम् अहार्षम् बृहते जात वेदसे । स मे श्रद्धाम् च मेधाम् च जात वेदा प्रयच्छतु स्वाहा । एधो अस्य् एधिषीमहि समद् असि तेजो असि तेजो मयि धेहि स्वाहा । समिद्धो माम् समर्धय प्रजया च धनेन च स्वाहा ॥ एषा ते अग्ने समित् तया वर्धस्व च आ च प्यायस्व । वर्धिषीमहि च वयम् आ च प्यासिषीमहि स्वाहा इति ।
2.10.e: (And puts fuel on the fire with the texts,) 'To Agni I have brought a piece of wood, to the great Gatavedas; may he, Gatavedas, give faith and insight to me. Svaha! 'Firewood art thou; may we prosper. Fuel art thou; splendour art thou; put splendour into me. Svaha! 'Being inflamed make me prosperous in offspring and wealth. Svaha! Thine is this fuel, Agni; thereby thou shalt grow and gain vigour. And may we grow and gain vigour. Svaha!'

2.10.s: agniḥ śraddhām ca medhām ca avinipātam smṛtim ca me | īlito jāta vedā ayam śunam naḥ prayachatv ityṇagnim upatiṣṭhate |
2.10.d: अग्निः श्रद्धाम् च मेधाम् च अविनिपातम् स्मृतिम् च मे । ईलितो जात वेदा अयम् शुनम् नः प्रयछत्व् इत्य्णग्निम् उपतिष्ठते ।

2.10.s: sauparṇa vrata bhāṣitam dṛṣṭam vṛddha sampradāya anuṣṭhitam tryāyuṣam pañcabhir mantraiḥ pratimantram lalāṭe hṛdaye dakṣiṇa skandhe vāme ca tataḥ pṛṣṭhe ca pañcasu bhasmanā tripuṇḍhram karoto |
2.10.d: सौपर्ण व्रत भाषितम् दृष्टम् वृद्ध सम्प्रदाय अनुष्ठितम् त्र्यायुषम् पञ्चभिर् मन्त्रैः प्रतिमन्त्रम् ललाटे हृदये दक्षिण स्कन्धे वामे च ततः पृष्ठे च पञ्चसु भस्मना त्रिपुण्ढ्रम् करोतो ।

2.10.s: sa eteṣām vedānām ekam dvau trīn sarvān vā adhīte ya evam hutvā agnim upatiṣṭhate |
2.10.d: स एतेषाम् वेदानाम् एकम् द्वौ त्रीन् सर्वान् वा अधीते य एवम् हुत्वा अग्निम् उपतिष्ठते ।
2.10.e: He who approaches the fire after having sacrificed thus, studies of these Vedas, one, two, three, or all.

2.11.e: Now (follows) the directing to the (special) observances.
The rules for it have been explained by the initiation.
He does not recite the Savitri.
Some say that the handing over of the staff forms the end (of this ceremony).
During the northern course of the sun, in the time of the increasing moon--

2.11.s: hotāram brahmacaryam upetya ācāryo amāṃsa āśī |
2.11.d: होतारम् ब्रह्मचर्यम् उपेत्य आचार्यो अमांस आशी ।
2.11.e: The teacher having abstained through one day and one night, from sexual intercourse and from eating flesh--
With the exclusion of the fourteenth day and of the eighth (of the half-month),
And of the first and last, according to some (teachers),

2.11.s: yām vā anyām bhapraśastām manyeta tasyām śukriye brahmacaryam ādiśet |
2.11.d: याम् वा अन्याम् भप्रशस्ताम् मन्येत तस्याम् शुक्रिये ब्रह्मचर्यम् आदिशेत् ।
2.11.e: Or on what day else the constellation seems lucky to him, on that day he shall direct (the student) to the duties of holiness according to the Sukriya rite.

2.11.s: trirātram brahmacaryam cared dvādaśa rātram saṃvatsaram vā yāvad vā gurur manyeta |
2.11.d: त्रिरात्रम् ब्रह्मचर्यम् चरेद् द्वादश रात्रम् संवत्सरम् वा यावद् वा गुरुर् मन्येत ।
2.11.e: Let him observe (those) duties through three days, or twelve days, or one year, or as long as the master may think fit.
The Sakvara (observance), however, (is to be kept) one year.

2.11.s: pūrṇe kāle carite brahmacarye śamyor bārhaspatya ante vede anūkte rahasyam śrāvayiṣyan kāla niyamam ca ādeśena pratīyeta |
2.11.d: पूर्णे काले चरिते ब्रह्मचर्ये शम्योर् बार्हस्पत्य अन्ते वेदे अनूक्ते रहस्यम् श्रावयिष्यन् काल नियमम् च आदेशेन प्रतीयेत ।
2.11.e: When the time has elapsed, when the duties have been observed, when the Veda has been studied down to the Samyu-Barhaspatya-(hymn), let (the teacher then), should he intend to instruct (the student) in the secret (part of the Veda), ascertain the time (through which the student has to observe the special rites) and the rules to be observed, from the (special) directions (that are handed down on this subject).

2.12.s: kṛta prātar āśasya apara ahṇe aparājitāyām diśi |
2.12.d: कृत प्रातर् आशस्य अपर अह्णे अपराजितायाम् दिशि ।
2.12.e: After (the student) has eaten something in the morning, in the afternoon, to the north-east--

2.12.s: hutvā ācāryo atha enam yāsv eva devatāsu parītto bhavati tāsv eva enam pṛchaty agnāv indra āditye viśveṣu ca deveṣu caritam te brahmacaryam |
2.12.d: हुत्वा आचार्यो अथ एनम् यास्व् एव देवतासु परीत्तो भवति तास्व् एव एनम् पृछत्य् अग्नाव् इन्द्र आदित्ये विश्वेषु च देवेषु चरितम् ते ब्रह्मचर्यम् ।
2.12.e: Having sacrificed, the teacher then asks him with regard to those deities to whom he has been given in charge (see above, chap. 3, 1), 'Hast thou fulfilled the duties of holiness before Agni, Indra, the Sun, and the Visve devas?'
If he answers, 'I have fulfilled them, sir!'--

2.12.s: paścād agneḥ purastād ācāryasya prān mukhe sthite ahatena vāsasā ācāryaḥ pradakṣiṇam mukham triḥ pariveṣṭya |
2.12.d: पश्चाद् अग्नेः पुरस्ताद् आचार्यस्य प्रान् मुखे स्थिते अहतेन वाससा आचार्यः प्रदक्षिणम् मुखम् त्रिः परिवेष्ट्य ।
2.12.e: The teacher three times envelops, from the left to the right, with a fresh garment the face (of the student) who is standing behind the fire, in front of the teacher, with his face to the east.

2.12.s: upariṣṭād daśāḥ kṛtvā yathā na sambhraśyeta |
2.12.d: उपरिष्टाद् दशाः कृत्वा यथा न सम्भ्रश्येत ।
2.12.e: He turns the skirt (of that garment) upwards so that it cannot slip down,

2.12.s: trirātram samid ādhānam bhikṣā caraṇam adhaḥ śayyām guru śuśrūṣām ca ākurvan vāg yato apramatto araṇye deva kule agni hotre vo apavasasva iti |
2.12.d: त्रिरात्रम् समिद् आधानम् भिक्षा चरणम् अधः शय्याम् गुरु शुश्रूषाम् च आकुर्वन् वाग् यतो अप्रमत्तो अरण्ये देव कुले अग्नि होत्रे वो अपवसस्व इति ।
2.12.e: (And says) 'Leaving off for three days the putting on of fuel, the going for alms, the sleeping on the ground, and the obedience to the teacher, fast in the forest, in a god's house or in a place where Agnihotra is performed, keeping silence, with earnest care.'

2.12.s: atra ha eke tān eva niyamāṃs tiṣṭhato rātryām eva upadiśanti |
2.12.d: अत्र ह एके तान् एव नियमांस् तिष्ठतो रात्र्याम् एव उपदिशन्ति ।
2.12.e: Here some (teachers) prescribe the same observances only for one night, during which he is to stand.
The teacher refrains from eating flesh and from sexual intercourse.

2.12.s: trirātre nirvṛtte rāryām vā grāmān niṣkrāman na etān īkṣeta anadhyāyān |
2.12.d: त्रिरात्रे निर्वृत्ते रार्याम् वा ग्रामान् निष्क्रामन् न एतान् ईक्षेत अनध्यायान् ।
2.12.e: When those three days or that night has elapsed, going out from the village he shall avoid to look at the following (persons or things) that form impediments for the study (of the Veda):

2.12.s: piśitāmam caṇḍālam sūtikām rajasvalām tedanim apahastakān śmaśānam sarvāṇi ca śava rūpāṇi yāny āsye na praviśeyuḥ svasya vāsān nirasan |
2.12.d: पिशितामम् चण्डालम् सूतिकाम् रजस्वलाम् तेदनिम् अपहस्तकान् श्मशानम् सर्वाणि च शव रूपाणि यान्य् आस्ये न प्रविशेयुः स्वस्य वासान् निरसन् ।
2.12.e: Raw flesh, a Kandala, a woman that has lately been confined, or that has her courses, blood, persons whose hands have been cut off, cemeteries, and all sorts of corpse-like (animals?) which enter (their dens?) with the mouth first (?), keeping them away from the place where he dwells.

2.12.s: prāg udīcīm diśam upaniṣkramya śucau deśe prān mukha ācārya upaviśaty |
2.12.d: प्राग् उदीचीम् दिशम् उपनिष्क्रम्य शुचौ देशे प्रान् मुख आचार्य उपविशत्य् ।
2.12.e: Going out (from the village) in a north-eastern direction the teacher sits down on a clean spot. turning his face to the east.

2.12.s: udita āditye anuvācana dharmeṇa vāg yatāya uṣṇīṣiṇe anvāha |
2.12.d: उदित आदित्ये अनुवाचन धर्मेण वाग् यताय उष्णीषिणे अन्वाह ।
2.12.e: When the sun has risen, he recites, in the way prescribed for the Veda-study, (the Aranyaka texts to the student) who is to keep silence and who wears a turban.
This rule is to be observed only for the Mahanamni verses.

2.12.s: atha uttareṣu prakaraṇeṣu svādhyāyam eva kurvata ācāryasya itaraḥ śṛṇoti |
2.12.d: अथ उत्तरेषु प्रकरणेषु स्वाध्यायम् एव कुर्वत आचार्यस्य इतरः शृणोति ।
2.12.e: At the sections however that follow (after the Mahanamnis) the other one hears while the teacher recites them for himself.
He gives (to the teacher) the turban, a vessel, a good cow.

2.12.s: tvam tam ity uccā divi iti ca praṇavena vā sarvam |
2.12.d: त्वम् तम् इत्य् उच्चा दिवि इति च प्रणवेन वा सर्वम् ।
2.12.e: (The teacher accepts the gifts) with the verses, [paragraph continues] 'Thou him' (Rig-veda I, 18, 5), and, 'High in the sky' (Rig-veda X, 107, 2), or (he accepts them) all with the Pranava (i.e. the syllable Om).

2.12.s: atra ha eke vaiśvadevam carum kurvate sarveṣu prakaraṇeṣu |
2.12.d: अत्र ह एके वैश्वदेवम् चरुम् कुर्वते सर्वेषु प्रकरणेषु ।
2.12.e: Here some prepare a mess of rice for the Visve devas at all sections (of the Aranyaka);
For the gods to whom he has been given in charge, according to Mandukeya.

2.13.e: Now (follow) the rules regarding the staff.

2.13.s: na antarā gamanam kuryād ātmano daṇḍasya |
2.13.d: न अन्तरा गमनम् कुर्याद् आत्मनो दण्डस्य ।
2.13.e: Let him not leave a passage between himself and the staff.

2.13.s: atha ced daṇḍa mekhala upavītānām anyatamam viśīryeta chidyeta vā tasya tat prāyaś cittam yad udvāhe rathasya |
2.13.d: अथ चेद् दण्ड मेखल उपवीतानाम् अन्यतमम् विशीर्येत छिद्येत वा तस्य तत् प्रायश् चित्तम् यद् उद्वाहे रथस्य ।
2.13.e: Now should any one of these things, viz. staff, girdle, or sacrificial cord, break or rend, the same penance (takes place) therefore which (has been prescribed) at the wedding with regard to the chariot.

2.13.s: mekhalā ced asaṃdheyā bhavaty anyām kṛtvā anumantrayate |
2.13.d: मेखला चेद् असंधेया भवत्य् अन्याम् कृत्वा अनुमन्त्रयते ।
2.13.e: If the girdle cannot be repaired, he makes another and speaks over it (the following verses):

2.13.s: medhya amedhya vibhāgajñe devi goptri sarasvati | mekhale askannam achinnam saṃtanuṣva vratam mama tvam agne vratabhṛt śucir agne devān iha āvaha | upa yajñam haviś ca naḥ vratāni bibhrad vratapā adābhyo bhavā no dūto ajaraḥ suvīraḥ | dadhad ratnāni sumṛlīko agne gopāya no jīvase jāta veda iti |
2.13.d: मेध्य अमेध्य विभागज्ञे देवि गोप्त्रि सरस्वति । मेखले अस्कन्नम् अछिन्नम् संतनुष्व व्रतम् मम त्वम् अग्ने व्रतभृत् शुचिर् अग्ने देवान् इह आवह । उप यज्ञम् हविश् च नः व्रतानि बिभ्रद् व्रतपा अदाभ्यो भवा नो दूतो अजरः सुवीरः । दधद् रत्नानि सुमृलीको अग्ने गोपाय नो जीवसे जात वेद इति ।
2.13.e: 'Thou who knowest the distinction of pure and impure, divine protectress Sarasvati, O girdle, prolong my vow unimpaired, unbroken. 'Thou, Agni, art the pure bearer of vows. Agni, carry hither the gods to our sacrifice and our oblation. 'Bearing the vows, the infallible protector of vows, be our messenger, undecaying and mighty. Giving treasures, merciful, Agni, protect us, that we may live, Gatavedas!
And he ties the sacrificial cord to the staff.

2.13.s: yajña upavītam daṇḍam ca mekhalām ajinam tathā | juhuyād apsu vrate pūrṇe vāruṇyā ṛcā rasena vā |
2.13.d: यज्ञ उपवीतम् दण्डम् च मेखलाम् अजिनम् तथा । जुहुयाद् अप्सु व्रते पूर्णे वारुण्या ऋचा रसेन वा ।
2.13.e: 'Let him sacrifice the sacrificial cord and the staff, the girdle and also the skin in water after the completion of his vow with a Varuna-verse or with the essence (of the Vedas, i.e. the syllable Om).

2.14.s: atha vaiśvadevaḥ |
2.14.d: अथ वैश्वदेवः ।
2.14.e: Now (follows) the Vaisvadeva (sacrifice).

2.14.s: vyākhyāto homa kalpaḥ |
2.14.d: व्याख्यातो होम कल्पः ।
2.14.e: The rite of the sacrifice has been explained.

2.14.s: vaiśvadevasya siddhasya sāyam prātar gṛhye agnau juhyāt |
2.14.d: वैश्वदेवस्य सिद्धस्य सायम् प्रातर् गृह्ये अग्नौ जुह्यात् ।
2.14.e: Let him pour oblations of prepared Vaisvadeva food in the evening and in the morning into the (sacred) domestic fire.

2.14.s: agnaye svāhā somāya svāhā indra agnibhyām svāhā viṣṇave svāhā bharadvāja dhanvantaraye svāhā viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ svāhā prajāpataye svāhā aditaye svāhā anumataye svāhā agnaye sviṣṭakṛte svāhā iti hutvā etāsām devatānām |
2.14.d: अग्नये स्वाहा सोमाय स्वाहा इन्द्र अग्निभ्याम् स्वाहा विष्णवे स्वाहा भरद्वाज धन्वन्तरये स्वाहा विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यः स्वाहा प्रजापतये स्वाहा अदितये स्वाहा अनुमतये स्वाहा अग्नये स्विष्टकृते स्वाहा इति हुत्वा एतासाम् देवतानाम् ।
2.14.e: 'To Agni svaha! To Soma svaha! To Indra and Agni svaha! To Vishnu svaha! To Bharadvaga Dhanvantari svaha! To the Visve devas svaha! To Pragapati svaha! To Aditi svaha! To Anumati svaha! To Agni Svishtakrit svaha!'--having thus offered the oblations belonging to those deities,

2.14.s: atha vāstu madhye balim hared etābhyaś ca eva devatābhyo namo brahmaṇe brāhmaṇebhyaś ca vāstoṣ pate prati jānīhy asmān iti vāstu madhye vāstoṣ pataye ca |
2.14.d: अथ वास्तु मध्ये बलिम् हरेद् एताभ्यश् च एव देवताभ्यो नमो ब्रह्मणे ब्राह्मणेभ्यश् च वास्तोष् पते प्रति जानीह्य् अस्मान् इति वास्तु मध्ये वास्तोष् पतये च ।
2.14.e: He then shall offer Balis (i.e. portions of food) in the centre of the floor to the same deities; (then another Bali with the words,) 'Adoration to Brahman and to the Brahmanas!' and (with the verse), 'Vastoshpati, accept us' (Rig-veda VII, 54, 1) in the centre of the floor to Vastoshpati.

2.14.s: atha diśām pradakṣiṇam yathā rūpam balim harati |
2.14.d: अथ दिशाम् प्रदक्षिणम् यथा रूपम् बलिम् हरति ।
2.14.e: He then distributes Balis, from the left to the right, through the different quarters (of the horizon, to the presiding deities) in due order (with the words),

2.14.s: nāma indrāya aindrebhyaś ca namo yamāya yāmyebhyaś ca namo varuṇāya vāruṇebhyaś ca namaḥ somāya saumyebhyaś ca namo bṛhaspataye bārhaspatyebhyaś ca |
2.14.d: नाम इन्द्राय ऐन्द्रेभ्यश् च नमो यमाय याम्येभ्यश् च नमो वरुणाय वारुणेभ्यश् च नमः सोमाय सौम्येभ्यश् च नमो बृहस्पतये बार्हस्पत्येभ्यश् च ।
2.14.e: 'Adoration to Indra and to those belonging to Indra! Adoration to Yama and to those belonging to Yama! Adoration to Varuna and to those belonging to Varuna! Adoration to Soma and to those belonging to Soma! Adoration to Brihaspati and to those belonging to Brihaspati!'

2.14.s: atha āditya maṇḍale namo aditaya ādityebhyaś ca namo nakṣatrebhya ṛtubhyo māsebhyo ardha māsebhyo ahorātrebhyaḥ saṃvatsarebhyaḥ |
2.14.d: अथ आदित्य मण्डले नमो अदितय आदित्येभ्यश् च नमो नक्षत्रेभ्य ऋतुभ्यो मासेभ्यो अर्ध मासेभ्यो अहोरात्रेभ्यः संवत्सरेभ्यः ।
2.14.e: Then (turned) towards the disk of the sun, 'Adoration to Aditi and to the Adityas! Adoration 5. 'He shall offer a Bali to those deities, i.e. to those ten deities to whom he has sacrificed, to Agni, &c. (see Sutra 4), addressing them with the word, "Adoration (to such and such a deity")--because in the other cases the word "adoration" (namah) has been prescribed for the Bali.' Narayana. to the Nakshatras, to seasons, to months, to half-months, to days and nights, to years!'

2.14.s: pūṣṇe pathikṛte dhātre vidhātre marudbhyaś ca iti dehalīṣu |
2.14.d: पूष्णे पथिकृते धात्रे विधात्रे मरुद्भ्यश् च इति देहलीषु ।
2.14.e: 'To Pushan, the path-maker; to Dhatar, to Vidhatar, and to the Maruts'--(thus) on the thresholds.

2.14.s: viṣṇave dṛṣadi |
2.14.d: विष्णवे दृषदि ।
2.14.e: To Vishnu on the grindstone.

2.14.s: vanaspataya ity ulūkhala |
2.14.d: वनस्पतय इत्य् उलूखल ।
2.14.e: 'To the tree'--(thus) in the mortar.

2.14.s: oṣadhībhya iti oṣadhīnām sthāne |
2.14.d: ओषधीभ्य इति ओषधीनाम् स्थाने ।
2.14.e: 'To the herbs'--(thus) where the herbs are kept.

2.14.s: parjanyāya adbhya iti maṇike |
2.14.d: पर्जन्याय अद्भ्य इति मणिके ।
2.14.e: 'To Parganya, to the waters'--(thus) near the water-pot.

2.14.s: namaḥ śriyau śayyāyām śirasi pādato bhadra kālyā |
2.14.d: नमः श्रियौ शय्यायाम् शिरसि पादतो भद्र काल्या ।
2.14.e: 'Adoration to Sri'--(thus) in the bed at the head, 'to Bhadrakali at the foot.

2.14.s: anugupte deśe namaḥ sarva anna bhūtaye |
2.14.d: अनुगुप्ते देशे नमः सर्व अन्न भूतये ।
2.14.e: In the privy, 'Adoration to Sarvannabhuti!'

2.14.s: atha antarikṣe naktam carebhya iti sāyam ahaś carebhya iti prātar ye devāsa iti ca |
2.14.d: अथ अन्तरिक्षे नक्तम् चरेभ्य इति सायम् अहश् चरेभ्य इति प्रातर् ये देवास इति च ।
2.14.e: Then (he throws a Bali) into the air, in the evening with the words, 'To the night-walkers,' in the morning with the words, 'To the day-walkers,' and with the Verse,' Which gods' (Rig-veda I, 139, 11).

2.14.s: avijñātābhyo devatābhya uttarato dhana pataye ca |
2.14.d: अविज्ञाताभ्यो देवताभ्य उत्तरतो धन पतये च ।

2.14.s: prācīna āvītī dakṣiṇataḥ śeṣam ninayati ye agni dagdhā iti |
2.14.d: प्राचीन आवीती दक्षिणतः शेषम् निनयति ये अग्नि दग्धा इति ।

2.14.s: deva pitṛ narebhyo dattvā śrotriyam bhojayed |
2.14.d: देव पितृ नरेभ्यो दत्त्वा श्रोत्रियम् भोजयेद् ।
2.14.e: When he has made his offerings to gods, fathers (i.e. Manes), and men, let him give food to a Srotriya (i.e. to a learned Brahmana).

2.14.s: brahma cāriṇe vā bhikṣām dadyād |
2.14.d: ब्रह्म चारिणे वा भिक्षाम् दद्याद् ।
2.14.e: Or let him give alms (of food) to a student.

2.14.s: anantaram sauvāsinīm garbhiṇīm kumārān sthavirāṃś ca bhojayet |
2.14.d: अनन्तरम् सौवासिनीम् गर्भिणीम् कुमारान् स्थविरांश् च भोजयेत् ।
2.14.e: Let him immediately afterwards offer food to a female under his protection, to a pregnant woman, to boys, and to old people.

2.14.s: śvabhyaḥ śvapacebhyaś ca vayobhyaś ca āvaped bhūvau |
2.14.d: श्वभ्यः श्वपचेभ्यश् च वयोभ्यश् च आवपेद् भूवौ ।
2.14.e: Let him throw (some food) on the ground for the dogs, for the dog-butchers, and for the birds.

2.14.s: iti na anavattam aśnīyāt |
2.14.d: इति न अनवत्तम् अश्नीयात् ।
2.14.e: Let him eat nothing without having cut off (and offered as a Bali) a portion thereof.

2.14.s: na ekaḥ |
2.14.d: न एकः ।
2.14.e: (Let him) not (eat) alone,

2.14.s: na pūrvam |
2.14.d: न पूर्वम् ।
2.14.e: Nor before (the others).

2.14.s: tad apy etad ṛco aktam mogham annam vindate apracetā iti |
2.14.d: तद् अप्य् एतद् ऋचो अक्तम् मोघम् अन्नम् विन्दते अप्रचेता इति ।
2.14.e: With regard thereto it has been said also in the Rik,' In vain the fool gains food' (Rig-veda X, 117, 6).

2.15.s: ṣaṇṇām ced arghyāṇām anyatama āgached go paśum ajam annam vā yat sāmānyatamam manyeta tat kuryāt |
2.15.d: षण्णाम् चेद् अर्घ्याणाम् अन्यतम आगछेद् गो पशुम् अजम् अन्नम् वा यत् सामान्यतमम् मन्येत तत् कुर्यात् ।
2.15.e: Should any one of the six persons (mentioned in the Srauta-sutra and in the Sutras 4-9) to whom the Arghya reception is due, visit (him), let him make (ready) a cow, a goat, or what (sort of food) he thinks most like (thereto).
Let the Argha not be without flesh.

2.15.s: adhiyajñam adhivivāham kuruta ity eva brūyāt |
2.15.d: अधियज्ञम् अधिविवाहम् कुरुत इत्य् एव ब्रूयात् ।
2.15.e: On the occasion of a sacrifice and of a wedding let (the guest) say, 'Make it (ready).'
The animal (offered) to the teacher is sacred to Agni;
If offered to an officiating priest, to Brihaspati;
If to the father-in-law, to Pragapati;
If to a king, to Indra;
If to a friend, to Mitra;
If to a Snataka, to Indra and Agni;

2.15.s: yady apy asakṛt saṃvatsarasya somena yajeta kṛta arghyā eva enam yājayeyur na akṛta arghyāḥ |
2.15.d: यद्य् अप्य् असकृत् संवत्सरस्य सोमेन यजेत कृत अर्घ्या एव एनम् याजयेयुर् न अकृत अर्घ्याः ।
2.15.e: Even if he performs more than one Soma sacrifice during a year, let only priests who have received (from him) the Arghya reception officiate for him, not such who have not received it.

2.16.s: madhu parke ca some ca pitṛ daivata krmaṇi | atra eva paśavo hiṃsyā na anyatra ity abravīn manuḥ |
2.16.d: मधु पर्के च सोमे च पितृ दैवत क्र्मणि । अत्र एव पशवो हिंस्या न अन्यत्र इत्य् अब्रवीन् मनुः ।
2.16.e: 'At the Madhuparka and at the Soma sacrifice, at the sacred rites for fathers (Manes) and gods only animals may be killed, not elsewhere: thus has Manu said.

2.16.s: ācāryaś ca pitā ca ubhau sakhā ca anatithir gṛhe | te yad vidadhyus tat kuryād iti dharmo vidhīyate |
2.16.d: आचार्यश् च पिता च उभौ सखा च अनतिथिर् गृहे । ते यद् विदध्युस् तत् कुर्याद् इति धर्मो विधीयते ।
2.16.e: 'Both his teacher and his father, and also a friend who does not stay in his house as a guest: whatever these dispose, that let him do; such is the established custom.

2.16.s: na eka grāmīṇam atithim viproṣya āgatam eva ca | upasthitam gṛhe vidyād bhāryā yatra agnayo api vā |
2.16.d: न एक ग्रामीणम् अतिथिम् विप्रोष्य आगतम् एव च । उपस्थितम् गृहे विद्याद् भार्या यत्र अग्नयो अपि वा ।
2.16.e: 'Let him not consider as a guest a person living in the same village, or one that comes in returning from a journey; (but let him consider as a guest only) one who has arrived at his house where the wife or the fires (of the host) are.

2.16.s: agni hotram bali vardāḥ kāle ca atithir āgataḥ | bālāś ca kula vṛddhāś ca nirdahanty apamānitāḥ |
2.16.d: अग्नि होत्रम् बलि वर्दाः काले च अतिथिर् आगतः । बालाश् च कुल वृद्धाश् च निर्दहन्त्य् अपमानिताः ।
2.16.e: '(The fire of) the Agnihotra, bulls, and a guest that has come in at the right time, children and persons of noble families: these burn up him who neglects them.

2.16.s: anaḍvān agni hotram ca brahma cārī ca te trayaḥ | aśnanta eva sidhyanti na eṣām siddhir anaśnatām |
2.16.d: अनड्वान् अग्नि होत्रम् च ब्रह्म चारी च ते त्रयः । अश्नन्त एव सिध्यन्ति न एषाम् सिद्धिर् अनश्नताम् ।
2.16.e: 'A bull, the Agnihotra, and a student, these three prosper only if they eat; there is no prosperity for them, if they do not eat.

2.16.s: devatāḥ puruṣam gṛhyā ahar ahar gṛha medhinam | bhāga artham upasarpanti tābhyo nirvaptum arhati |
2.16.d: देवताः पुरुषम् गृह्या अहर् अहर् गृह मेधिनम् । भाग अर्थम् उपसर्पन्ति ताभ्यो निर्वप्तुम् अर्हति ।
2.16.e: 'Day by day the domestic deities approach the man who performs the domestic rites, in order to receive their share; (that) let him pour out to them.

2.17.s: tṛṇāny apy uñchato nityam agni hotram ca juhvataḥ | sarvam sukṛtam ādatte brāhmaṇo anarcito vasan |
2.17.d: तृणान्य् अप्य् उञ्छतो नित्यम् अग्नि होत्रम् च जुह्वतः । सर्वम् सुकृतम् आदत्ते ब्राह्मणो अनर्चितो वसन् ।
2.17.e: 'Even if a man constantly gather grass and perform the Agnihotra, a Brahmana who stays (in his house) without receiving honour takes away all his good works.

2.17.s: ā uda pātrāt tu dātavyam ā kāṣṭhāj juhuyād api ā sūktād ā anuvākād vā brahma yajño vidhīyate |
2.17.d: आ उद पात्रात् तु दातव्यम् आ काष्ठाज् जुहुयाद् अपि आ सूक्ताद् आ अनुवाकाद् वा ब्रह्म यज्ञो विधीयते ।
2.17.e: 'One should give (even) if it were only a water-pot; one should sacrifice (even) if it were a piece of wood; (even) down to one hymn or to one Anuvaka the Brahmayagna is enjoined.

2.17.s: na upavāsaḥ pravāse syāt patnī dhārayate vratam | putro bhrātā athavā patnī śiṣyo vā asya balim haret |
2.17.d: न उपवासः प्रवासे स्यात् पत्नी धारयते व्रतम् । पुत्रो भ्राता अथवा पत्नी शिष्यो वा अस्य बलिम् हरेत् ।
2.17.e: 'When on a journey let him not fast; (during that time) the wife keeps the vow. Let his son, his brother, or his wife, or his pupil offer the Bali oblation.

2.17.s: vaiśvadevam imam ye tu sāyam prātaḥ prakurvate | te arthair āyuṣā kīrtyā prajābhiś ca samṛdhnuyur iti |
2.17.d: वैश्वदेवम् इमम् ये तु सायम् प्रातः प्रकुर्वते । ते अर्थैर् आयुषा कीर्त्या प्रजाभिश् च समृध्नुयुर् इति ।
2.17.e: 'Those who perform this Vaisvadeva sacrifice in the evening and in the morning, they will prosper in wealth and (long) life, in fame and offspring.'

2.18.e: A student who is going to set out on a journey, speaks thus to his teacher:

2.18.s: prāṇa apānayor ity upāṃśv om aham vatsyāmi bho iti uccaiḥ |
2.18.d: प्राण अपानयोर् इत्य् उपांश्व् ओम् अहम् वत्स्यामि भो इति उच्चैः ।
2.18.e: 'Of inhalation and exhalation'--(this he says) in a low voice; 'Om, I will dwell'--this aloud.

2.18.s: prāṇa apānā uruvyacas tvayā pra padye devāya tvā goptre pari dadāmi deva savitar eṣa te brahma cārī tam te pari dadāmi tam gopāyasva tam mā mṛdha ity upāṃśu |
2.18.d: प्राण अपाना उरुव्यचस् त्वया प्र पद्ये देवाय त्वा गोप्त्रे परि ददामि देव सवितर् एष ते ब्रह्म चारी तम् ते परि ददामि तम् गोपायस्व तम् मा मृध इत्य् उपांशु ।
2.18.e: (The teacher) in a low voice (replies), 'To inhalation and exhalation I, the wide-extended one, resort with thee. To the protecting god I give thee in charge. God Savitar; this student belongs to thee; I give him in charge to thee; protect him; do not forsake him.'

2.18.s: om svasti ity uccair ācāryaḥ svasti ity uccair ācāryaḥ |
2.18.d: ओम् स्वस्ति इत्य् उच्चैर् आचार्यः स्वस्ति इत्य् उच्चैर् आचार्यः ।
2.18.e: 'Om, hail!' the teacher aloud. 'Hail!' the teacher aloud. Here ends the Second Adhyaya.

3.1.e: A bath (shall be taken by the student) when he is going to return home (from his teacher).

3.1.s: anaḍduham ity uktam tasminn upaveśya keśa śmaśrūṇi vāpayati loma nakhāni ca |
3.1.d: अनड्दुहम् इत्य् उक्तम् तस्मिन्न् उपवेश्य केश श्मश्रूणि वापयति लोम नखानि च ।
3.1.e: 'A bull's hide'--this has been declared. On that hide he makes him sit down and have his hair and beard cut and the hair of the body and the nails.

3.1.s: vrīhi yavais tila sarṣapair apāmārgaiḥ sadā upṣpībhir ity udvāpya |
3.1.d: व्रीहि यवैस् तिल सर्षपैर् अपामार्गैः सदा उप्ष्पीभिर् इत्य् उद्वाप्य ।
3.1.e: Having had (the cut-off hair-ends, &c.) thrown away together with rice and barley, with sesamum-seed and mustard-seed, with Apamarga and Sadapushpi flowers,
Having sprinkled him (with water) with the Apohishthiya-hymn (Rig-veda X, 9),
Having dressed him with two garments with (the verse), 'The garments both of you' (Rig-veda I, 152, 1),

3.1.s: atha asmai niṣkam badhnāty āyuṣyam varcasyam |
3.1.d: अथ अस्मै निष्कम् बध्नात्य् आयुष्यम् वर्चस्यम् ।
3.1.e: He then puts on him a golden ornament (with the words), 'Giving life and vigour' (Vagasaneyi Samhita XXXIV, 50).
With (the verse), 'Mine, Agni, be vigour' (Rig-veda X, 128, 1), the veiling (of the head is done).
With (the verse), 'House by house the shining one' (Rig-veda I, 123, 4) (he takes) the parasol,
With (the verse), 'Rise up' (Rig-veda X, 18, 6), the shoes,

3.1.s: dīrghas te astv aṅkuśa iti vaiṇavam daṇḍam ādatte |
3.1.d: दीर्घस् ते अस्त्व् अङ्कुश इति वैणवम् दण्डम् आदत्ते ।
3.1.e: With (the verse), 'Long be thy hook' (Rig-veda VIII, 17, 10) he takes a bamboo staff.
Let him sit that day in solitude.

3.1.s: vanaspate vīḍvaṅgaḥ śāsa itthā iti ratham ārohed |
3.1.d: वनस्पते वीड्वङ्गः शास इत्था इति रथम् आरोहेद् ।
3.1.e: With (the verses), 'O tree! with strong limbs,' and, 'A ruler indeed' (Rig-veda VI, 47, 26; X, 152, 1) let him mount the chariot.

3.1.s: yatra enam gavā vā paśunā vā arhayeyus tat pūrvam upatiṣṭheta |
3.1.d: यत्र एनम् गवा वा पशुना वा अर्हयेयुस् तत् पूर्वम् उपतिष्ठेत ।
3.1.e: (Before returning home) let him first approach a place where they will perform Argha for him with a cow or a goat.

3.1.s: gobhyo vā samāvarteta phalavato vā vṛkṣād |
3.1.d: गोभ्यो वा समावर्तेत फलवतो वा वृक्षाद् ।
3.1.e: Or let him return (making his start) from cows or from a fruit-bearing tree.

3.1.s: indra śreṣṭhāni draviṇāni dhehi syonā pṛthivi bhava ity avarohati |
3.1.d: इन्द्र श्रेष्ठानि द्रविणानि धेहि स्योना पृथिवि भव इत्य् अवरोहति ।
3.1.e: With (the verses), 'Indra, give us best goods,' and, 'Be friendly, O earth' (Rig-veda II, 21, 6; I, 22, 15) he descends (from the chariot).
Let him eat that day his favourite food.

3.1.s: ācāryāya vastra yugam dadyād uṣṇīṣam maṇi kuṇḍalam daṇḍa upānaham chatram ca |
3.1.d: आचार्याय वस्त्र युगम् दद्याद् उष्णीषम् मणि कुण्डलम् दण्ड उपानहम् छत्रम् च ।
3.1.e: To his teacher he shall give (that) pair of garments, the turban, ear-rings and jewel, staff and shoes, and the parasol.

3.2.s: agāram kārayiṣyann iha anna adyāya viśaḥ pari gṛhṇāmi ity udumbara śākhayā triḥ parilikhya madhye sthaṇḍile juhoti |
3.2.d: अगारम् कारयिष्यन्न् इह अन्न अद्याय विशः परि गृह्णामि इत्य् उदुम्बर शाखया त्रिः परिलिख्य मध्ये स्थण्डिले जुहोति ।
3.2.e: If he wishes to have a house built, he draws with an Udumbara branch three times a line round (the building-ground) with (the words), 'Here I include the dwellings for the sake of food,' and sacrifices in (its) centre on an elevated spot,

3.2.s: ko asy kasya asi kāya te grāma kāmo juhoti svāhā asyām devānām asi bhāga dheyam itaḥ prajātāḥ pitaraḥ paretāḥ | virāl ajuhvad grāma kāmo na devānām kiṃcana antareṇa svāhā iti |
3.2.d: को अस्य् कस्य असि काय ते ग्राम कामो जुहोति स्वाहा अस्याम् देवानाम् असि भाग धेयम् इतः प्रजाताः पितरः परेताः । विराल् अजुह्वद् ग्राम कामो न देवानाम् किंचन अन्तरेण स्वाहा इति ।
3.2.e: (With the texts,) 'Who art thou? Whose art thou? To whom do I sacrifice thee, desirous of (dwelling in the) village? Svaha! 'Thou art the gods' share on this (earth). From here have sprung the fathers who have passed away. The ruler has sacrificed, desirous of (dwelling in the) village, not omitting anything that belongs to the gods. Svaha!'
Having had the pits for the posts dug,

3.2.s: imam vi minve amṛtasya śākhām madhor dhārām prataraṇīm vasūnām | enām śiśuḥ krandaty ā kumāra enām dhenuḥ krandatu nitya vatsa ity udumbara śākhām ghṛtena aktām dakṣiṇe dvārye garte nidadhāti |
3.2.d: इमम् वि मिन्वे अमृतस्य शाखाम् मधोर् धाराम् प्रतरणीम् वसूनाम् । एनाम् शिशुः क्रन्दत्य् आ कुमार एनाम् धेनुः क्रन्दतु नित्य वत्स इत्य् उदुम्बर शाखाम् घृतेन अक्ताम् दक्षिणे द्वार्ये गर्ते निदधाति ।
3.2.e: And with (the verse), 'This branch of the immortal one I erect, a stream of honey, promoting wealth. The child, the young one, cries to it; the cow shall low to it, the unceasingly fertile one'--he puts an Udumbara branch which has been besmeared with ghee into the pit for the right door-post.

3.2.s: imam uc chrayāmi bhuvanasya śākhām madhor dhārām prataraṇīm vasūnām | enām śiśuḥ krandaty ā kumāra enām dhenuḥ krandatu pāka vatsa ity uttarataḥ |
3.2.d: इमम् उच् छ्रयामि भुवनस्य शाखाम् मधोर् धाराम् प्रतरणीम् वसूनाम् । एनाम् शिशुः क्रन्दत्य् आ कुमार एनाम् धेनुः क्रन्दतु पाक वत्स इत्य् उत्तरतः ।
3.2.e: 'This branch of the world I establish, a stream of honey, promoting wealth. The child, the young one, cries to it; the cow shall low to it that has a young calf'--thus to the left.

3.2.s: evam dvayor dvayor dakṣiṇataḥ paścād uttarataś ca |
3.2.d: एवम् द्वयोर् द्वयोर् दक्षिणतः पश्चाद् उत्तरतश् च ।
3.2.e: In the same way at the two (pits) to the south, to the west, and to the north.

3.2.s: imām aham asya vṛkṣasya śākhām ghṛtam ukṣantīm amṛte minomi | enām śiśuḥ krandaty ā kumāra ā syandantām dhenavo nitya vatsa iti sthūṇā rājam ucchrayati |
3.2.d: इमाम् अहम् अस्य वृक्षस्य शाखाम् घृतम् उक्षन्तीम् अमृते मिनोमि । एनाम् शिशुः क्रन्दत्य् आ कुमार आ स्यन्दन्ताम् धेनवो नित्य वत्स इति स्थूणा राजम् उच्छ्रयति ।
3.2.e: With (the verse), 'This branch of this tree, that drops ghee, I erect in the immortal. The child, the young one, cries to it; cows shall flock to it, unceasingly fertile ones'--he erects the chief post.

3.2.s: enam kumāras taruṇa ā vatsa bhuvanas patri | enam parisrutaḥ kumbhyā ā dadhnaḥ kalaśair gaman |
3.2.d: एनम् कुमारस् तरुण आ वत्स भुवनस् पत्रि । एनम् परिस्रुतः कुम्भ्या आ दध्नः कलशैर् गमन् ।
3.2.e: 'May the young child come to it, may the calf . . . .; may they come to it with a cup of Parisrut, with pots of curds.

3.3.s: iha eva sthūṇe prati tiṣṭha dhruvā aśvāvatī gomatī sīlamāvatī | kṣeme tiṣṭha ghṛtam ukṣamāṇe iha eva tiṣṭha nimitā tilvilā sthājirāvatī | madhye poṣasya tṛmpatām mā tvā prāpann aghāyavaḥ upahūtā iha gāva upahūtā ajāvayaḥ | atho annasya kīlāla upahūto gṛheṣu naḥ | rathantare prati tiṣṭha vāmadevye śrayasva bṛhati stabhāya iti sthūṇā rājam abhimṛśati |
3.3.d: इह एव स्थूणे प्रति तिष्ठ ध्रुवा अश्वावती गोमती सीलमावती । क्षेमे तिष्ठ घृतम् उक्षमाणे इह एव तिष्ठ निमिता तिल्विला स्थाजिरावती । मध्ये पोषस्य तृम्पताम् मा त्वा प्रापन्न् अघायवः उपहूता इह गाव उपहूता अजावयः । अथो अन्नस्य कीलाल उपहूतो गृहेषु नः । रथन्तरे प्रति तिष्ठ वामदेव्ये श्रयस्व बृहति स्तभाय इति स्थूणा राजम् अभिमृशति ।
3.3.e: 'Stand here, O post, firm, rich in horses and cows, . . . .; stand safely, dropping ghee; stand here, fixed in the ground, prosperous, long-lasting(?), amid the prosperity of people who satiate themselves. May the malevolent ones not reach thee! 'Hither are called the cows; hither are called goats and sheep; and the sweet essence (?) of food is called hither to our house. 'Stand fast in the Rathantara; recline on the Vamadevya; establish thyself on the Brihat'--with (these texts) he touches the chief post.
When the house has been built conformably (to its proper dimensions), he touches the posts.

3.3.s: satyam ca śraddhā ca iti pūrve |
3.3.d: सत्यम् च श्रद्धा च इति पूर्वे ।
3.3.e: The two (posts) to the east with (the words), 'Truth and faith!'

3.3.s: yajñaś ca dakṣiṇā ca iti dakṣiṇe |
3.3.d: यज्ञश् च दक्षिणा च इति दक्षिणे ।
3.3.e: Those to the south with (the words), 'Sacrifice and gift!'

3.3.s: balam ca ojaś ca ity apare |
3.3.d: बलम् च ओजश् च इत्य् अपरे ।
3.3.e: Those to the west with (the words), 'Strength and power!'

3.3.s: brahma ca kṣatram ca ity uttare |
3.3.d: ब्रह्म च क्षत्रम् च इत्य् उत्तरे ।
3.3.e: Those to the north with (the words), 'The Brahman and the Kshatra!
'Fortune the pinnacle, law the chief post!
'Day and night the two door jambs!'

3.3.s: ukṣā samudra ity abhyaktam aśmānam stūpasya adhastān nikhanet |
3.3.d: उक्षा समुद्र इत्य् अभ्यक्तम् अश्मानम् स्तूपस्य अधस्तान् निखनेत् ।
3.3.e: With (the verse), 'A bull, an ocean' (Rig-veda V, 47, 3)' let him bury an anointed stone under the pinnacle.

3.4.s: agnim dadhāmi manasā śivena ayam astu saṃgamano vasūnām | mā no hiṃsī sthaviram mā kumāram śam no bhava dvipade śam catuṣpada iti gṛhyam agnim bāhyata upasamādhāya |
3.4.d: अग्निम् दधामि मनसा शिवेन अयम् अस्तु संगमनो वसूनाम् । मा नो हिंसी स्थविरम् मा कुमारम् शम् नो भव द्विपदे शम् चतुष्पद इति गृह्यम् अग्निम् बाह्यत उपसमाधाय ।
3.4.e: Having established the (sacred) domestic fire outside with (the words), 'I place (here) Agni with genial mind; may he be the assembler of goods. Do no harm to us, to the old nor to the young; be a saviour to us, to men and animals!'--

3.4.s: prāg agreṣu naveṣu kuśeṣu uda kumbham navam pratiṣṭhāpya |
3.4.d: प्राग् अग्रेषु नवेषु कुशेषु उद कुम्भम् नवम् प्रतिष्ठाप्य ।
3.4.e: Having put a new water-pot on fresh eastward-pointed Kusa-grass,

3.4.s: ariṣṭā asmākam vīrā mā parā seci no dhanam ity abhimantrya |
3.4.d: अरिष्टा अस्माकम् वीरा मा परा सेचि नो धनम् इत्य् अभिमन्त्र्य ।
3.4.e: And spoken over it (the words), 'Unhurt be our men, may our riches not be squandered!'--

3.4.s: rathantarasya stotriyeṇa punar ādāyam kakup kāram tisraḥ pūrva ahṇe juhoti |
3.4.d: रथन्तरस्य स्तोत्रियेण पुनर् आदायम् ककुप् कारम् तिस्रः पूर्व अह्णे जुहोति ।
3.4.e: He sacrifices three oblations in the forenoon with the Stotriya text of the Rathantara with repetition and Kakubh-forming;
(Three oblations with the Stotriya) of the Vamadevya at midday;
Of the Brihat in the afternoon;

3.4.s: mahā vyāhṛtayaś catasro vāstoṣ pata iti tisro amīvahā vāstoṣ pate vāstoṣ pate dhruvā sthūṇā sauviṣṭakṛtī daśamī sthālī pākasya rātrau |
3.4.d: महा व्याहृतयश् चतस्रो वास्तोष् पत इति तिस्रो अमीवहा वास्तोष् पते वास्तोष् पते ध्रुवा स्थूणा सौविष्टकृती दशमी स्थाली पाकस्य रात्रौ ।

3.4.s: jyeṣṭham putram ādāya jāyām ca sahadhānyaḥ prapadyeta |
3.4.d: ज्येष्ठम् पुत्रम् आदाय जायाम् च सहधान्यः प्रपद्येत ।

3.4.s: indrasya gṛhāḥ śivā vasumanto varūthinas tān aham pra padye saha jāyayā saha prajayā saha paśubhiḥ saha rāyas poṣeṇa saha yan me kiṃca asti tena |
3.4.d: इन्द्रस्य गृहाः शिवा वसुमन्तो वरूथिनस् तान् अहम् प्र पद्ये सह जायया सह प्रजया सह पशुभिः सह रायस् पोषेण सह यन् मे किंच अस्ति तेन ।

3.5.s: śagam śagmam śivam śivam kṣemāya vaḥ śāntyai prapadye abhayam no astu grāmo mā araṇyāya pari dadātu viśva mahāya mā pari dehi iti grāmān niṣkrāmanṇ |
3.5.d: शगम् शग्मम् शिवम् शिवम् क्षेमाय वः शान्त्यै प्रपद्ये अभयम् नो अस्तु ग्रामो मा अरण्याय परि ददातु विश्व महाय मा परि देहि इति ग्रामान् निष्क्रामन्ण् ।
3.5.e: 'To every able one, to every blissful one, to you I turn for the sake of safety, of peace. Free from danger may we be. May the village give me in charge to the forest. All! give me in charge to the great one,'--thus (he speaks) when leaving the village.

3.5.s: araṇyam mā grāmāya pari dadātu maha viśvāya mā pari dehi iti grāmam praviśann ariktaḥ |
3.5.d: अरण्यम् मा ग्रामाय परि ददातु मह विश्वाय मा परि देहि इति ग्रामम् प्रविशन्न् अरिक्तः ।
3.5.e: 'May the forest give me in charge to the village. Great one! give me in charge to the all'--thus (he speaks) when entering the village, not without (carrying) something (with himself, such as fuel, flowers, &c.)

3.5.s: gṛhān bhadran sumanasaḥ prapadye avīraghno vīrataraḥ suvīrān | irām vahanto ghṛtam ukṣamāṇā anyeṣv aham sumanāḥ sam viśeyam iti sadā pravacanīyaḥ |
3.5.d: गृहान् भद्रन् सुमनसः प्रपद्ये अवीरघ्नो वीरतरः सुवीरान् । इराम् वहन्तो घृतम् उक्षमाणा अन्येष्व् अहम् सुमनाः सम् विशेयम् इति सदा प्रवचनीयः ।
3.5.e: I enter the blessed, joyful house, which does not bring death to men; manly (I enter) that which is rich in men. Bringing refreshment, dropping ghee (we enter the house) in which I shall joyfully rest'--this verse is constantly to be pronounced (when he enters the house).

3.6.e: One who has not set up the (sacred Srauta) fires, when setting out on a journey, looks at his house.

3.6.s: imān me mitrāvaruṇau gṛhān gopāyatam yuvam | avinaṣṭān avibrutān pūṣā enān abhi rakṣatv ā asmākam punar āgamād |
3.6.d: इमान् मे मित्रावरुणौ गृहान् गोपायतम् युवम् । अविनष्टान् अविब्रुतान् पूषा एनान् अभि रक्षत्व् आ अस्माकम् पुनर् आगमाद् ।
3.6.e: (He murmurs the text,) 'Do ye both, Mitra and Varuna, protect this house for me; unscathed, undisturbed, may Pushan guard it till our return;'

3.6.s: api panthām aganmahi iti ca japati |
3.6.d: अपि पन्थाम् अगन्महि इति च जपति ।
3.6.e: And murmurs (the verse), 'Upon the path we have entered' (Rig-veda VI, 51, 16).

3.7.e: When he then returns from his journey, he looks at his house (and says),

3.7.s: gṛhā mā bibhīta mā vepadhvam ūrjam bibhrata emasi ūrjam bibhrad vaḥ sumanāḥ sumedhā gṛhān aimi manasā modamānaḥ yeṣām adhyeti pravasan yeṣu saumanaso bahuḥ | gṛhān upa hvayāmahe te no jānantu jānataḥ upahūtā iha gāva upahūtā ajāvayaḥ | atho annasya kīlāla upahūto gṛheṣu naḥ |
3.7.d: गृहा मा बिभीत मा वेपध्वम् ऊर्जम् बिभ्रत एमसि ऊर्जम् बिभ्रद् वः सुमनाः सुमेधा गृहान् ऐमि मनसा मोदमानः येषाम् अध्येति प्रवसन् येषु सौमनसो बहुः । गृहान् उप ह्वयामहे ते नो जानन्तु जानतः उपहूता इह गाव उपहूता अजावयः । अथो अन्नस्य कीलाल उपहूतो गृहेषु नः ।
3.7.e: 'House, do not fear, do not tremble; bringing strength we come back. Bringing strength, joyful and wise, I come back to thee, to the house, rejoicing in my mind. 'That of which the traveller thinks, that in which dwells much joy, that I call the house. May it know us as we know it. 'Hither are called the cows; hither are called goats and sheep; and the sweet essence (?) of food is called hither to our house.'

3.7.s: ayam no agnir bhagavān ayam no bhagavattaraḥ | asya upasadye mā riṣāma ayam śraiṣṭhye dadhātu na iti gṛhyam agnim upasthāya |
3.7.d: अयम् नो अग्निर् भगवान् अयम् नो भगवत्तरः । अस्य उपसद्ये मा रिषाम अयम् श्रैष्ठ्ये दधातु न इति गृह्यम् अग्निम् उपस्थाय ।
3.7.e: Having approached the (sacred) domestic fire with the verse, 'This Agni is glorious to us, this is highly glorious. Worshipping him (?) may we suffer no harm; may he bring us to supremity'--

3.7.s: virājo doho asi virājo doham aśīya mayi padyāyai virājo doha iti pādya pratigrahaṇaḥ |
3.7.d: विराजो दोहो असि विराजो दोहम् अशीय मयि पद्यायै विराजो दोह इति पाद्य प्रतिग्रहणः ।
3.7.e: When accepting the water for washing the feet he says, 'The milk of Virag art thou; may I obtain the milk of Virag; in me (may) the milk of Padya Virag (dwell)!'

3.8.s: anāhita agnir navam prāśiṣyan āgrayaṇa devatābhyaḥ sviṣṭakṛc caturthībhyaḥ svāhā kāreṇa gṛhye agnau juhuyāt |
3.8.d: अनाहित अग्निर् नवम् प्राशिष्यन् आग्रयण देवताभ्यः स्विष्टकृच् चतुर्थीभ्यः स्वाहा कारेण गृह्ये अग्नौ जुहुयात् ।
3.8.e: When one who has not set up the (sacred Srauta) fires, is going to partake of the first-fruits (of the harvest), let him sacrifice to the Agrayana deities with (Agni) Svishtakrit as the fourth, and with the word SVAHA, on his (sacred) domestic fire.

3.8.s: prājāpataye tvā graham gṛhṇāmi mahyam śriyai mahyam yaśase mahyam anna adyāya iti prāśana arthīyam abhimantrya |
3.8.d: प्राजापतये त्वा ग्रहम् गृह्णामि मह्यम् श्रियै मह्यम् यशसे मह्यम् अन्न अद्याय इति प्राशन अर्थीयम् अभिमन्त्र्य ।
3.8.e: Having recited over (the food) which he is going to eat (the formula), 'To Pragapati I draw thee, the proper portion, for luck to me, for glory to me, for food to me!'--

3.8.s: bhadrān naḥ śreyaḥ sam anaiṣṭa devās tvayā jvasena sam aśīmahi tvā | sa no mayobhūḥ pitav ā viśasva śam no bhava dvipade śam catuṣpada ity adbhir abhyutsiñcan triḥ prāśnāti |
3.8.d: भद्रान् नः श्रेयः सम् अनैष्ट देवास् त्वया ज्वसेन सम् अशीमहि त्वा । स नो मयोभूः पितव् आ विशस्व शम् नो भव द्विपदे शम् चतुष्पद इत्य् अद्भिर् अभ्युत्सिञ्चन् त्रिः प्राश्नाति ।
3.8.e: He thrice eats of it, sprinkling it with water, with (the verse), 'From the good you have led us to the better, ye gods! Through thee, the nourishment, may we obtain thee. Thus enter into us, O potion, bringing refreshment; be a saviour to us, to men and animals!'

3.8.s: amo asi prāṇa tad ṛtam bravīmy amo asi sarvān asi praviṣṭaḥ | sa me jarām rogam apanudya śarīrād amā ma edhi mā mṛdhā na indra iti hṛdaya deśam abhimṛśati |
3.8.d: अमो असि प्राण तद् ऋतम् ब्रवीम्य् अमो असि सर्वान् असि प्रविष्टः । स मे जराम् रोगम् अपनुद्य शरीराद् अमा म एधि मा मृधा न इन्द्र इति हृदय देशम् अभिमृशति ।
3.8.e: With (the verse), 'This art thou, breath; the truth I speak This art thou; from all directions thou hast entered (into all beings). Thou driving away old age and sickness from my body be at home with me. Do not forsake us, Indra!'--he touches the place of the heart;

3.8.s: nābhir asi mā bibhīthāḥ prāṇānām granthir asi mā visrasa iti nābhim |
3.8.d: नाभिर् असि मा बिभीथाः प्राणानाम् ग्रन्थिर् असि मा विस्रस इति नाभिम् ।
3.8.e: With (the words), 'The navel art thou; do not fear; the knot of the breathing powers art thou; do not loosen thyself,' (he touches) the navel;
With the verse, 'Bliss with our ears' (Rig-veda I, 89, 8), (lie touches) the limbs as stated (in that verse);
Worshipping the sun with the verse, 'Yonder eye' (Rig-veda VII, 66, 16).

3.9.s: pari vaḥ sainyād vadhād vy ā vṛñjantu ghoṣiṇyaḥ | samānas tasya gopater gāvo aṃśo na vo riṣat pūṣā gā anv etu na iti gāḥ praiṣṭhamānā anumantrayeta |
3.9.d: परि वः सैन्याद् वधाद् व्य् आ वृञ्जन्तु घोषिण्यः । समानस् तस्य गोपतेर् गावो अंशो न वो रिषत् पूषा गा अन्व् एतु न इति गाः प्रैष्ठमाना अनुमन्त्रयेत ।
3.9.e: 'May the noisy (goddesses) keep you away from slaughtering hosts. May the entire share, O cows, that belongs to this lord of cows, suffer no harm among you--(and) 'May Pushan go after our cows' (Rig-veda VI, 54, 5)--this he shall speak over the cows when they go away (to their pasture-grounds).
'May Pushan hold' (Rig-veda VI, 54, 10), when they run about.

3.9.s: yāsām ūdhaś catur bilam madhoḥ pūrṇam ghṛtasya ca | tā naḥ santu payasvatīr bahvīr goṣṭhe ghṛtācya iti ā gāvo agamann iti ca pratyāgatāsu |
3.9.d: यासाम् ऊधश् चतुर् बिलम् मधोः पूर्णम् घृतस्य च । ता नः सन्तु पयस्वतीर् बह्वीर् गोष्ठे घृताच्य इति आ गावो अगमन्न् इति च प्रत्यागतासु ।
3.9.e: 'May they whose udder with its four holes is full of sweet and ghee, be milk-givers to us; (may they be) many in our stable, rich in ghee'--and, 'The cows have come' (Rig-veda VI, 28), when they have come back.
The last (verse) when he puts them in (into the stable).

3.9.s: mayobhū r vāta iti sūktena goṣṭhe gatāḥ |
3.9.d: मयोभू र् वात इति सूक्तेन गोष्ठे गताः ।
3.9.e: The hymn, 'Refreshing wind' (Rig-veda X, 169), (he recites over the cows), when they are gone into the stable.

3.10.s: yā phālgunyā uttarā amāvāsyā sā revatyā sampadyate tasyām aṅka lakṣaṇāni kārayed |
3.10.d: या फाल्गुन्या उत्तरा अमावास्या सा रेवत्या सम्पद्यते तस्याम् अङ्क लक्षणानि कारयेद् ।
3.10.e: The new moon that follows after the Phalguna full moon, falls under (the Nakshatra) Revati: on that (new moon day) he shall have the marks made (on his cattle),

3.10.s: bhuvanam asi sahasra poṣam indrāya tvā śramo dadat | akṣatam asy ariṣṭam ilā annam gopāyanam yāvatīnām idam kariṣyāmi bhūyasīnām uttamām samām kriyāsam iti |
3.10.d: भुवनम् असि सहस्र पोषम् इन्द्राय त्वा श्रमो ददत् । अक्षतम् अस्य् अरिष्टम् इला अन्नम् गोपायनम् यावतीनाम् इदम् करिष्यामि भूयसीनाम् उत्तमाम् समाम् क्रियासम् इति ।
3.10.e: With (the words), 'Thou art the world, thousandfold prospering. To Indra may exertion (?) give thee. Inviolate art thou, unhurt, sap, food, protection. For as many (cows) I shall do this now, for more (than these) may I do it in the latest year.'

3.10.s: yā prathamā prajāyeta tasyāḥ pīyūṣam juhuyāt saṃvatsarīṇam paya usriyāyā ity etābhyām ṛgbhyām |
3.10.d: या प्रथमा प्रजायेत तस्याः पीयूषम् जुहुयात् संवत्सरीणम् पय उस्रियाया इत्य् एताभ्याम् ऋग्भ्याम् ।
3.10.e: Of that (cow) that calves first let him sacrifice the biestings with the two verses, 'Yearly the milk of the cow' (Rig-veda X, 87, 17. 18).

3.10.s: yadi yamau prajāyeta mahā vyāhṛtibhir hutvā yamasūm dadyāt |
3.10.d: यदि यमौ प्रजायेत महा व्याहृतिभिर् हुत्वा यमसूम् दद्यात् ।
3.10.e: If she brings forth twin-calves, let him sacrifice with the Mahavyahritis, and give the mother of the twins (to the Brahmanas).

3.11.e: Now (follows) the Vrishotsarga (i.e. setting a bull at liberty).
On the Karttika full moon day or on that day of the Asvayuga (month) that falls under (the Nakshatra) Revati--

3.11.s: gavām madhye susamiddham agnim kṛtvā ājya āhutīr juhoti |
3.11.d: गवाम् मध्ये सुसमिद्धम् अग्निम् कृत्वा आज्य आहुतीर् जुहोति ।
3.11.e: He sacrifices, after having kindled amid the cows a well-inflamed fire, Agya oblations (with the words),

3.11.s: iha ratir iha ramadhvam svāhā iha dhṛtir iha svadhṛtiḥ svāhā upa sṛjam dharuṇam mātre dharuṇo mātaram dhayan rāyas poṣam asmāsu dīdharat svāhā |
3.11.d: इह रतिर् इह रमध्वम् स्वाहा इह धृतिर् इह स्वधृतिः स्वाहा उप सृजम् धरुणम् मात्रे धरुणो मातरम् धयन् रायस् पोषम् अस्मासु दीधरत् स्वाहा ।
3.11.e: Here is delight; take delight here. Svaha! [paragraph continues] Here is still-standing; here is (your) own still-standing. Svaha! 'I have let the calf join its mother. May the calf, sucking its mother's breast, support increase of wealth among us. Svaha!'

3.11.s: pūṣā gā anv etu na iti pauṣṇasya juhoti |
3.11.d: पूषा गा अन्व् एतु न इति पौष्णस्य जुहोति ।
3.11.e: With the verse, 'May Pushan go after our cows' (Rig-veda VI, 54, 5) he sacrifices from (a mess of sacrificial food) belonging to Pushan.

3.11.s: eka varṇam dvi varṇam tri varṇam vā |
3.11.d: एक वर्णम् द्वि वर्णम् त्रि वर्णम् वा ।
3.11.e: (He takes) a one-coloured, two-coloured, or three-coloured (bull),
Or one that protects the herd,
Or that is protected by the herd,
Or it may also be red.

3.11.s: sarva aṅgair upeto yūthe varcasvitamaḥ syāt |
3.11.d: सर्व अङ्गैर् उपेतो यूथे वर्चस्वितमः स्यात् ।
3.11.e: It should have all its limbs complete, and be the finest (bull) in the herd.

3.11.s: yūthe mukhyāś catasro vatsataryas tāś ca alam kṛtya |
3.11.d: यूथे मुख्याश् चतस्रो वत्सतर्यस् ताश् च अलम् कृत्य ।
3.11.e: And the four best young cows of the herd, having adorned those too,

3.11.s: etam yuvānam patim vo dadāmi tena krīḍantīś carataḥ priyeṇa | mā vaśva atra januṣā saṃvidānā rāyas poṣeṇa sam iṣā madema svāhā iti |
3.11.d: एतम् युवानम् पतिम् वो ददामि तेन क्रीडन्तीश् चरतः प्रियेण । मा वश्व अत्र जनुषा संविदाना रायस् पोषेण सम् इषा मदेम स्वाहा इति ।
3.11.e: (He says,) 'This young (bull) I give you as your husband; sporting with him, your lover, walk about. Do not desert us (?), being joined (with us) from your birth. In increase of wealth, in food may we rejoice. Svaha!'

3.11.s: nabhyasthe anumantrayate mayobhūr ity anuvāka śeṣeṇa |
3.11.d: नभ्यस्थे अनुमन्त्रयते मयोभूर् इत्य् अनुवाक शेषेण ।
3.11.e: When (the bull) is in the midst (of the cows), he recites over (them), 'Refreshing,' &c. (Rig-veda X, 169, I seq.) down to the end of the Anuvaka.

3.11.s: sarvāsām payasi pāyasam śrapayitvā brāhmaṇān bhojayet |
3.11.d: सर्वासाम् पयसि पायसम् श्रपयित्वा ब्राह्मणान् भोजयेत् ।
3.11.e: With the milk of all of them he shall cook milk-rice and feed Brahmanas with it.

3.12.s: ūrdhvam āgrahāyaṇyās tisro aṣṭakā apara pakṣeṣu |
3.12.d: ऊर्ध्वम् आग्रहायण्यास् तिस्रो अष्टका अपर पक्षेषु ।
3.12.e: After the Agrahayani (or the full moon day of the month Margasirsha) (follow) the three Ashtakas in the second fortnight (of the Margasirsha and of the two following months).
At the first of these he sacrifices vegetables,

3.12.s: iyam eva sā yā prathamā vyuchad antar asyām carati praviṣṭā | vadhūr jajāna navakṛj janitrī traya enām mahimānaḥ sacantām svāhā iti |
3.12.d: इयम् एव सा या प्रथमा व्युछद् अन्तर् अस्याम् चरति प्रविष्टा । वधूर् जजान नवकृज् जनित्री त्रय एनाम् महिमानः सचन्ताम् स्वाहा इति ।
3.12.e: With (the verse), 'She who shone forth first is this (earth); she walks, having entered into this (earth). The wife has brought forth (children), the new-creating mother. May the three powers follow her. Svaha!'

3.12.s: yasyām vaivasvato yamaḥ sarve devāḥ samāhitāḥ | aṣṭakā sarvato mukhī sā me kāmān atītṛpat āhus te grāvāṇo dantān ūdhaḥ pavamānaḥ | māsāś ca ardha māsāś ca namas te sumanā mukhi svāhā iti |
3.12.d: यस्याम् वैवस्वतो यमः सर्वे देवाः समाहिताः । अष्टका सर्वतो मुखी सा मे कामान् अतीतृपत् आहुस् ते ग्रावाणो दन्तान् ऊधः पवमानः । मासाश् च अर्ध मासाश् च नमस् ते सुमना मुखि स्वाहा इति ।
3.12.e: With (the verses), 'She in whom Yama, the son of Vivasvat, and all gods are contained, the Ashtaka whose face is turned to all sides, she has satiated my desires. 'They call thy teeth "the pressing-stones;" thy udder is (Soma) Pavamana; . . . . are the months and half-months. Adoration to thee, O glad-faced one! Svaha!'

3.13.e: At the middle (Ashtaka) and in the middle of the rainy season,

3.13.s: mahā vyāhṛtayaś catasro ye tātṛṣur iti catasro anudrutya vapām juhuyād |
3.13.d: महा व्याहृतयश् चतस्रो ये तातृषुर् इति चतस्रो अनुद्रुत्य वपाम् जुहुयाद् ।
3.13.e: The four Mahavyahritis (and) the four (verses), They who have thirsted' (Rig-veda X, 15, 9 seq.): having quickly recited (these verses) he shall sacrifice the omentum;

3.13.s: vaha vapām jāta vedaḥ pitṛbhyo yatra enān vettha sukṛtasya loke | medasaḥ kulyā upa tān sravantu satyāḥ santu yajamānasya kāmāḥ svāhā iti vā |
3.13.d: वह वपाम् जात वेदः पितृभ्यो यत्र एनान् वेत्थ सुकृतस्य लोके । मेदसः कुल्या उप तान् स्रवन्तु सत्याः सन्तु यजमानस्य कामाः स्वाहा इति वा ।
3.13.e: Or (he shall do so) with the verse, 'Carry the omentum, Gatavedas, to the Manes, where thou knowest them in the world of virtue. May streams of fat flow to them; may the wishes of the sacrificer be fulfilled. Svaha!'

3.13.s: mahā vyāhṛtayaś catasro ye tātṛṣur iti catasro aṣṭa āhuti sthālī pāko avadāna miśraḥ |
3.13.d: महा व्याहृतयश् चतस्रो ये तातृषुर् इति चतस्रो अष्ट आहुति स्थाली पाको अवदान मिश्रः ।
3.13.e: (Then follow) the four Mahavyahritis (and) the four (verses), 'They who have thirsted' (see Sutra 2): (thus is offered) an eightfold oblation of cooked food, together with the cut-off portions.

3.13.s: antarhitā girayo antarhitā pṛthivī mahī me divā digbhiś ca sarvābhir anyam antaḥ pitur dadhe amuṣyai svāhā antarhitā ma ṛtavo ahorātrāś ca saṃdhijāḥ | māsāś ca ardha māsāś ca anyam antaḥ pitur dadhe amuṣyai svāhā yās tiṣṭhanti yāḥ sravanti yā dabhrāḥ parisasruṣīḥ | adbhiḥ sarvasya bhartṛbhir anyam antaḥ pitur dadhe amuṣyai svāhā yan me mātā pralulubhe vicaranty apati vratā | retas tan me pitā vṛṅktām mātur anyo ava padyata amuṣyai svāhā iti vā mahā vyāhṛtīnām sthāne catasro anyatra karaṇasya |
3.13.d: अन्तर्हिता गिरयो अन्तर्हिता पृथिवी मही मे दिवा दिग्भिश् च सर्वाभिर् अन्यम् अन्तः पितुर् दधे अमुष्यै स्वाहा अन्तर्हिता म ऋतवो अहोरात्राश् च संधिजाः । मासाश् च अर्ध मासाश् च अन्यम् अन्तः पितुर् दधे अमुष्यै स्वाहा यास् तिष्ठन्ति याः स्रवन्ति या दभ्राः परिसस्रुषीः । अद्भिः सर्वस्य भर्तृभिर् अन्यम् अन्तः पितुर् दधे अमुष्यै स्वाहा यन् मे माता प्रलुलुभे विचरन्त्य् अपति व्रता । रेतस् तन् मे पिता वृङ्क्ताम् मातुर् अन्यो अव पद्यत अमुष्यै स्वाहा इति वा महा व्याहृतीनाम् स्थाने चतस्रो अन्यत्र करणस्य ।
3.13.e: Or, 'Interposed are the mountains; interposed is the wide earth to me. With the sky and all the points of the horizon I interpose another one instead of the father. To N.N. svaha! 'Interposed to me are the seasons, and days and nights, the twilight's children. With the months and half-months I interpose another one instead of the father. To N.N. svaha! 'With the standing ones, with the streaming ones. with the small ones that flow about: with the waters, the supporters of all I interpose another one instead of the father. To N.N. svaha! 'Wherein my mother has done amiss, going astray, faithless to her husband, that sperm may my father take as his own; may another one fall off from the mother. To N.N. svaha!'--these four (verses) instead of the Mahavyahritis, if (the sacrificer) is an illegitimate child.

3.13.s: śvo anvaṣṭakyam piṇḍa pitṛ yajña āvṛtā |
3.13.d: श्वो अन्वष्टक्यम् पिण्ड पितृ यज्ञ आवृता ।
3.13.e: On the next day the Anvashtakya ceremony (i.e. ceremony following the Ashtaka) in accordance with the rite of the Pindapitriyagna.

3.14.e: On the last (Ashtaka) he sacrifices cakes,

3.14.s: ukthyaś ca atirātraś ca sadyahkrīś chandasā saha | apūpakṛd aṣṭake namas te sumanā mukhi svāhā iti |
3.14.d: उक्थ्यश् च अतिरात्रश् च सद्यह्क्रीश् छन्दसा सह । अपूपकृद् अष्टके नमस् ते सुमना मुखि स्वाहा इति ।
3.14.e: With the words, 'The Ukthya and the Atiratra. the Sadyahkri together with the metre--Ashtaka! [paragraph continues] Preparer of cakes! Adoration to thee, O glad-faced one. Svaha!

3.14.s: go paśur aja paśu sthālī pāko vā |
3.14.d: गो पशुर् अज पशु स्थाली पाको वा ।
3.14.e: A cow or a goat is the animal (to be sacrificed), or a mess of cooked food (should be offered).
Or he may optionally offer food to a cow.

3.14.s: api vā araṇye kakṣam apādahed eṣā me aṣṭakā iti |
3.14.d: अपि वा अरण्ये कक्षम् अपादहेद् एषा मे अष्टका इति ।
3.14.e: Or he may optionally burn down brushwood in the forest and say, 'This is my Ashtaka.'

3.14.s: na tv eva na kurvīta na tv eva na kurvīta |
3.14.d: न त्व् एव न कुर्वीत न त्व् एव न कुर्वीत ।
3.14.e: But let him not neglect to do (one of these things). But let him not neglect to do (one of these things). Here ends the Third Adhyaya.

4.1.e: Let him offer (Sraddha oblations) every month to the fathers.

4.1.s: brāhmaṇān vedavido ayugmāṃs tryavara ardhān pitṛvad upaveśya |
4.1.d: ब्राह्मणान् वेदविदो अयुग्मांस् त्र्यवर अर्धान् पितृवद् उपवेश्य ।
4.1.e: Having invited an uneven number of Brahmanas, versed in the Veda, at least three, to sit down as (representing) the fathers,
And having strewn sesamum into an uneven number of water-pots,

4.1.s: asāv etat ta ity anudiśya brāhmaṇānām pāṇiṣu ninayed |
4.1.d: असाव् एतत् त इत्य् अनुदिश्य ब्राह्मणानाम् पाणिषु निनयेद् ।

4.1.s: bhuñjāneṣu mahā vyāhṛtīḥ sāvitrīm madhuvatīyāḥ pitṛ devatyāḥ pāvamānīś ca japed |
4.1.d: भुञ्जानेषु महा व्याहृतीः सावित्रीम् मधुवतीयाः पितृ देवत्याः पावमानीश् च जपेद् ।

4.1.e: Before (their dinner he shall offer) the lumps, according to some (teachers).

4.1.s: piṇḍān paścimena tat patnīnām kiṃcid antardhāya |
4.1.d: पिण्डान् पश्चिमेन तत् पत्नीनाम् किंचिद् अन्तर्धाय ।
4.1.e: Behind (these he places the lumps) for their wives, putting something between (these and the preceding ones).
To the Brahmanas he shall announce the remnants.

4.1.s: agnau karaṇa ādi piṇḍa pitṛ yajñena kalpo vyākhyātaḥ |
4.1.d: अग्नौ करण आदि पिण्ड पितृ यज्ञेन कल्पो व्याख्यातः ।
4.1.e: The rites of the putting (of food) into the fire (see Sutra 6), &c. have been declared (in the Srauta-sutra) by the Pindapitriyagna.

4.2.e: Now (follows) the Ekoddishta (i.e. the Sraddha ceremony directed to a single dead person),

4.2.s: na āvāhanam na agnau karaṇam na atra viśve devāḥ svaditam iti tṛipta praśna upa tiṣṭhatām ity akṣayya sthāne |
4.2.d: न आवाहनम् न अग्नौ करणम् न अत्र विश्वे देवाः स्वदितम् इति तृइप्त प्रश्न उप तिष्ठताम् इत्य् अक्षय्य स्थाने ।
4.2.e: No inviting (takes place here), nor the putting (of food) into the fire, nor (do) the Visve devas (take part in this ceremony). 'Relished?'--thus are they to be asked whether they are satiated. 'May it approach (the fathers),' instead of 'imperishable.'
Thus through one year, when one has died.
And (then) omission of the fourth one.

4.3.e: Now (follows) the Sapindikarana (i.e. reception of a dead person into the community of Pinda-offerings with the other Manes).
When one year has elapsed, or three half-months,
Or on a day when something good happens,

4.3.s: catvāry uda pātrāṇi satila gandha udakāni kṛtvā |
4.3.d: चत्वार्य् उद पात्राणि सतिल गन्ध उदकानि कृत्वा ।
4.3.e: He fills four water-pots with sesamum, scents, and water,
Three for the fathers, one for the (newly) dead person,

4.3.s: preta pātram pitṛ pātreṣv āsiñcati ye samānā iti dvābhyām |
4.3.d: प्रेत पात्रम् पितृ पात्रेष्व् आसिञ्चति ये समाना इति द्वाभ्याम् ।
4.3.e: And pours the pot that belongs to the (newly) dead person out into the pots of the fathers with the two verses, 'They who commonly' (Vagasaneyi Samhita XIX, 45. 46).

4.4.e: Now (follows) the Abhyudayika (i.e. the Sraddha ceremony referring to good luck).
In the fortnight of the increasing moon, on an auspicious day,
After the sacrifice to the mothers has been performed,
And an even number of (Brahmanas) versed in the Veda have been invited to sit down;
The rite is performed from left to right.
The murmuring with the omission of the verses belonging to the Manes.
Barley is to be used instead of sesamum.
The lumps are mixed with curds, jujube fruits, fried grain.

4.4.s: nāndī mukhān pitṝn ā vāhayiṣya ity āvāhane |
4.4.d: नान्दी मुखान् पितॄन् आ वाहयिष्य इत्य् आवाहने ।
4.4.e: On inviting (the Manes, he should say), 'The Nandimukha (glad-faced?) Manes will I invite.'

4.4.s: nāndī mukhāḥ pitaraḥ prīyantām ity akṣayya sthāne |
4.4.d: नान्दी मुखाः पितरः प्रीयन्ताम् इत्य् अक्षय्य स्थाने ।
4.4.e: 'May the Nandimukha Manes be rejoiced,' instead of 'imperishable.'

4.4.s: nāndī mukhān pitṝn vācayiṣya iti vācane |
4.4.d: नान्दी मुखान् पितॄन् वाचयिष्य इति वाचने ।
4.4.e: 'The Nandimukha Manes will I make speak,' when he makes (the Brahmanas) speak.
'(Was it) well done?'--thus are they to be asked whether they are satiated.
The rest is the same (as in the other kinds of Sraddha rites), as far as it is not (by contrary rules).

4.5.e: Now (follows) the Upakarana (i.e. the ceremony by which the annual course of study is opened).

4.5.s: oṣadhīnām prādur bhāve hastena śravaṇena vā |
4.5.d: ओषधीनाम् प्रादुर् भावे हस्तेन श्रवणेन वा ।
4.5.e: When the herbs appear, under the Nakshatra Hasta or Sravana,

4.5.s: akṣata saktūnām dhānānām ca dadhi ghṛta miśrāṇām pratyṛcam vedena juhuyād iti ha eka āhuḥ |
4.5.d: अक्षत सक्तूनाम् धानानाम् च दधि घृत मिश्राणाम् प्रत्यृचम् वेदेन जुहुयाद् इति ह एक आहुः ।
4.5.e: Let him make oblations of the flour of fried barley and of grains, mixed with curds and ghee, with the (whole) Veda, verse by verse: thus say some (teachers).
Or with the first verses of the Suktas and Anuvakas.
With the first verses of the Adhyayas and of the sections belonging to the (different) Rishis, according to Mandukeya.
'I praise Agni the Purohita' (Rig-veda I, 1, 1), this one verse,

4.5.s: kuṣumbhakas tad abravīd āvadaṃs tvam śakune bhadram ā vada gṛṇānā jamadagninā dhāman te viśvam bhuvanam adhiśritam gantā no yajñam yajñiyāḥ suśami yo naḥ svo araṇaḥ prati cakṣva vi cakṣva ā agne yāhi marut sakhā yat te rājan śṛtam havir iti dvṛcāḥ |
4.5.d: कुषुम्भकस् तद् अब्रवीद् आवदंस् त्वम् शकुने भद्रम् आ वद गृणाना जमदग्निना धामन् ते विश्वम् भुवनम् अधिश्रितम् गन्ता नो यज्ञम् यज्ञियाः सुशमि यो नः स्वो अरणः प्रति चक्ष्व वि चक्ष्व आ अग्ने याहि मरुत् सखा यत् ते राजन् शृतम् हविर् इति द्वृचाः ।
4.5.e: 'The Kushumbhaka (mungoose?) has said it;' 'If thou criest, O bird, announce luck to us;' 'Sung by Gamadagni;' 'In thy abode the whole world rests;' [paragraph continues] 'Come to our sacrifice, O you that are worthy of sacrifice, with care;' 'Whosoever, be he ours, be he alien;' 'Look on, look about;' 'Come here, Agni, the Maruts' friend;' 'The oblation, O king, cooked for thee:' each time two verses,

4.5.s: tat śamyor ā vṛṇīmaha ity ekā |
4.5.d: तत् शम्योर् आ वृणीमह इत्य् एका ।
4.5.e: 'That blessing and bliss we choose'--this one verse (the first and last verse of each Mandala).

4.5.s: huta śeṣādd haviḥ prāśnanti dadhikrāvṇo akāriṣam ity etayā |
4.5.d: हुत शेषाद्द् हविः प्राश्नन्ति दधिक्राव्णो अकारिषम् इत्य् एतया ।
4.5.e: (Taking something) of the remnants of the sacrificed (food) they partake of that sacrificial food with this (verse), 'I praised Dadhikravan' (Rig-veda IV, 39, 6).

4.5.s: mahā vyāhṛtīḥ sāvitrīm veda ādi prabhṛtīni svastyayanāni ca japitvā |
4.5.d: महा व्याहृतीः सावित्रीम् वेद आदि प्रभृतीनि स्वस्त्ययनानि च जपित्वा ।
4.5.e: Murmur the Mahavyahritis, the Savitri, and the auspicious hymns commencing from the beginning of the Veda,
And cause the teacher to pronounce auspicious wishes.
Of this (ceremony) it is also said,

4.5.s: ayāta yāmatām pūjām sāratvam chandasām tathā | icchanta ṛṣayo apaśyann upākarma tapo balāt |
4.5.d: अयात यामताम् पूजाम् सारत्वम् छन्दसाम् तथा । इच्छन्त ऋषयो अपश्यन्न् उपाकर्म तपो बलात् ।
4.5.e: 'Desirous (of acquiring) for the hymns inexhaustible vigour, reverence, and also soundness, the Rishis, by the power of their austerities, have discovered the Upakarman.

4.5.s: tasmāt ṣaṭ karma nityena ātmano mantra siddhaye | upākartavyam ity āhuḥ karmaṇām siddhim ichatā |
4.5.d: तस्मात् षट् कर्म नित्येन आत्मनो मन्त्र सिद्धये । उपाकर्तव्यम् इत्य् आहुः कर्मणाम् सिद्धिम् इछता ।
4.5.e: 'Therefore a constant performer of the six kinds of works should, in order that his Mantras might be successful, perform the Upakarman--so they say--if he wishes for success of his (holy) works.

4.5.s: upākarmaṇi ca utsarge trirātram kṣapaṇam bhavet | aṣṭakāsu tv ahorātram ṛtv antyāsu ca rātriṣu |
4.5.d: उपाकर्मणि च उत्सर्गे त्रिरात्रम् क्षपणम् भवेत् । अष्टकासु त्व् अहोरात्रम् ऋत्व् अन्त्यासु च रात्रिषु ।
4.5.e: 'At the time of the Upakarman and of the Utsarga an interruption (of the Veda-study) shall take place for (three days and) three nights, likewise at the Ashtakas for one day and one night, and so on the last night of each season.'

4.6.e: On the first day of the bright fortnight of Magha,
In a place covered with herbs,

4.6.s: ud u tyam jātavedasam citram devānām namo mitrasya sūryo no divas pātv iti sauryāṇi japitvā |
4.6.d: उद् उ त्यम् जातवेदसम् चित्रम् देवानाम् नमो मित्रस्य सूर्यो नो दिवस् पात्व् इति सौर्याणि जपित्वा ।
4.6.e: Having murmured the hymns sacred to the Sun, 'Upwards that Gatavedas' (Rig-veda I, 50), 'The bright face of the gods' (I, 115), Adoration to Mitra's (eye)' (X, 37), 'From the sky (where he dwells) may Surya protect us' (X, 158),

4.6.s: śāsa itthā mahān asi iti pradakṣiṇam partyṛcam pratidiśam pratyasya loṣṭān |
4.6.d: शास इत्था महान् असि इति प्रदक्षिणम् पर्त्यृचम् प्रतिदिशम् प्रत्यस्य लोष्टान् ।
4.6.e: And having thrown clods of earth (on the ground) to the different quarters (of the horizon), from the left to the right, with the hymn, 'A ruler indeed' (Rig-veda X, 152), verse by verse,

4.6.s: ṛṣīṃś chandāṃsi devatāḥ śraddhā medhe ca tarpayitvā pratipuruṣam ca pitrīṃś |
4.6.d: ऋषींश् छन्दांसि देवताः श्रद्धा मेधे च तर्पयित्वा प्रतिपुरुषम् च पित्रींश् ।
4.6.e: And having satiated (with water) the Rishis, the metres, the deities, faith and insight, and the fathers man by man,
They interrupt (the study of) the hymns for six months and a half,
Or for five and a half.
But if they (wish to) recite them (nevertheless), let the recitation go on after a pause of one day and one night.

4.7.e: Now the interruption (of the Veda recitation):--
In the case of prodigies until the same time (next day),
And in the case of other miracles;
In the case of lightning, thunder, and rains (the recitation shall be interrupted) till the twilight has thrice passed;
At a Sraddha-dinner for one day;
If a death (of relations) or birth has happened, for ten days;
On the fourteenth days (of the fortnights), the new moon days, and the Ashtaka days,
And on misty days.
And when the teacher has died, for ten days;
When he has heard of it, for three days;
And (on the death) of those whose family-head he is.
On receiving (gifts) as at the Sraddha.
On (the death of) a fellow-student;
When he has followed (the funeral of) a dead person,
And when he has laid down the lumps of flour to the fathers.
At night;
During twilight;
On the full and change of the moon;
After sunset;
In the neighbourhood of a Sudra;
When the sound of a Saman is heard;
On a burial ground;
In a wilderness which belongs to the village;
In a village where a corpse is;
On seeing forbidden sights;
On hearing what is forbidden;
On smelling a foul smell;
If a high wind blows;
If a cloud emits (heavy) rain;
On a carriage road;
And while the sound of a lute is heard;
While being on a chariot;
(In the neighbourhood) of a dog as (in that) of a Sudra;
Having climbed up a tree;
Having descended into a pit;
(Immersed) in water;
While anybody cries;
While suffering bodily pain;
While he is naked;
Whilst impure with the remnants of food
On a bridge;
On the occasion of the shaving of the hair and the beard until the bath;
While being rubbed;
While bathing;
When having sexual intercourse;
While being anointed;

4.7.s: preta parśini sūtika udakyayoś ca śūdravat |
4.7.d: प्रेत पर्शिनि सूतिक उदक्ययोश् च शूद्रवत् ।
4.7.e: (In the neighbourhood) of a man who has to touch corpses (a corpse-bearer, &c.), of a woman that has recently been confined, or that has her courses, as (in the neighbourhood) of a Sudra;
With veiled hands;
In an army;
In presence of a Brahmana who has not had his meal, and of cows (that have eaten nothing);
When (these impediments) have passed, let them (continue to) recite (the Veda).

4.7.s: eteṣām yadi kiṃcid akāma utpāto bhavet prāṇān āyamya ādityam īkṣitvā adhīyīta |
4.7.d: एतेषाम् यदि किंचिद् अकाम उत्पातो भवेत् प्राणान् आयम्य आदित्यम् ईक्षित्वा अधीयीत ।
4.7.e: Should any of these cases arise against his will, let him (continue to) recite after having held his breath and looked at the sun.

4.7.s: vidyut stanayitnu varṣa varjam kalpe varṣavad ardha ṣaṣṭheṣu |
4.7.d: विद्युत् स्तनयित्नु वर्ष वर्जम् कल्पे वर्षवद् अर्ध षष्ठेषु ।
4.7.e: (The same rules hold good,) except (those regarding) lightning, thunder, and rain, for (the study of) the Kalpa. During the five months and a half (they have to behave) as while it rains.
Thereof it is also said,

4.7.s: annam āpo mūla phalam yac ca anyat śrāddhikam bhavet | pratigṛhya apy anadhyāyaḥ pāṇy āsyo brāhmaṇaḥ smṛta iti |
4.7.d: अन्नम् आपो मूल फलम् यच् च अन्यत् श्राद्धिकम् भवेत् । प्रतिगृह्य अप्य् अनध्यायः पाण्य् आस्यो ब्राह्मणः स्मृत इति ।
4.7.e: 'Food, water, roots and fruits, and whatsoever else Sraddha-food there may be: even when he has (only) accepted thereof, the study should be interrupted; the Brahmana's hand is his mouth; so it is taught.'

4.8.e: And to (students) who have been duly initiated he shall set forth (the Veda);

4.8.s: prān vā udan vā āsīna ācāryo daṣiṇata udan mukha itaraḥ |
4.8.d: प्रान् वा उदन् वा आसीन आचार्यो दषिणत उदन् मुख इतरः ।
4.8.e: The teacher sitting to the east or to the north, the other one to the south, with his face turned to the north.
Or two (students shall be so seated).
But more (than two) as there is room (for them).

4.8.s: na ucchrita āsana upaviṣṭo guru samīpe |
4.8.d: न उच्छ्रित आसन उपविष्टो गुरु समीपे ।
4.8.e: He should not sit on a high seat in presence of a Guru,
Nor on the same seat (with him),
Nor stretching his arms under his knees,
Nor holding his feet like an axe.

4.8.s: adhīhi bho ity uktvā ācārya om kāram pracodayet |
4.8.d: अधीहि भो इत्य् उक्त्वा आचार्य ओम् कारम् प्रचोदयेत् ।
4.8.e: After (the student) has said, Recite, sir!' the teacher shall cause him to pronounce the syllable OM.
When he has recited, he embraces (his teacher's feet),

4.8.s: viratāḥ sma bho ity uktvā yathā artham |
4.8.d: विरताः स्म भो इत्य् उक्त्वा यथा अर्थम् ।
4.8.e: Says, 'We have finished, sir!' and (goes away) according to his business.
(He shall say,) 'Leave! Pause meanwhile!' according to some (teachers).
Let no one step between (a teacher and students) who study.
Let no one change his place during the recitation.

4.8.s: yadi ced doṣaḥ syāt trirātram upoṣya ahorātram vā sāvitrīm abhyāvartayed yāvat śaknuyād brāhmaṇebhyaḥ kiṃcid dadyād ahorātram uparamya prādhyayanam |
4.8.d: यदि चेद् दोषः स्यात् त्रिरात्रम् उपोष्य अहोरात्रम् वा सावित्रीम् अभ्यावर्तयेद् यावत् शक्नुयाद् ब्राह्मणेभ्यः किंचिद् दद्याद् अहोरात्रम् उपरम्य प्राध्ययनम् ।
4.8.e: Should any fault be committed, let him fast three days, or one day and one night, repeat the Savitri as long as he can, and give something to the Brahmanas; then after an interruption of one day and one night the study should go on.

4.9.e: And having submerged himself at the time prescribed for the bath, he satiates the deities:

4.9.s: agnis tṛpyatu vāyus tṛpyatu sūryas tṛpyatu viṣṇus tṛpyatu prajāpatis tṛpyatu virūpa akṣas tṛpyatu sahasra akṣas tṛpyatu somaḥ brahmā vedāḥ devāḥ ṛṣayaḥ sarvāṇi ca chandāṃsi om kāraḥ vaṣaṭ kārha mahā vyāhṛtayaḥ sāvitrī yajñāḥ dyāvā pṛthivī nakṣatrāṇi antarikṣam ahorātrāṇi saṃkhyāḥ saṃdhyāḥ samudrāḥ nadyaḥ girayaḥ kṣetra oṣadhi vanaspati gandharva apsarasaḥ nāgāḥ bhūtāny evam antāni tṛpyantu śrutim tarpayāmi smṛtim tarpayāmi dhṛtim tarpayāmi ratim tarpayāmi gatim tarpayāmi matim tarpayāmi śraddhā medhe dhāraṇām ca go brāhmaṇam sthāvara jaṅgamāni sarva bhūtāni tarpyantv iti yajña upavītī |
