4.9.d: अग्निस् तृप्यतु वायुस् तृप्यतु सूर्यस् तृप्यतु विष्णुस् तृप्यतु प्रजापतिस् तृप्यतु विरूप अक्षस् तृप्यतु सहस्र अक्षस् तृप्यतु सोमः ब्रह्मा वेदाः देवाः ऋषयः सर्वाणि च छन्दांसि ओम् कारः वषट् कार्ह महा व्याहृतयः सावित्री यज्ञाः द्यावा पृथिवी नक्षत्राणि अन्तरिक्षम् अहोरात्राणि संख्याः संध्याः समुद्राः नद्यः गिरयः क्षेत्र ओषधि वनस्पति गन्धर्व अप्सरसः नागाः भूतान्य् एवम् अन्तानि तृप्यन्तु श्रुतिम् तर्पयामि स्मृतिम् तर्पयामि धृतिम् तर्पयामि रतिम् तर्पयामि गतिम् तर्पयामि मतिम् तर्पयामि श्रद्धा मेधे धारणाम् च गो ब्राह्मणम् स्थावर जङ्गमानि सर्व भूतानि तर्प्यन्त्व् इति यज्ञ उपवीती ।
4.9.e: 'Agni may satiate himself; Vayu may satiate himself; Surya may satiate himself; Vishnu may satiate himself; Pragapati may satiate himself; Virupaksha may satiate himself; Sahasraksha may satiate himself; Soma, Brahman, the Vedas, the gods, the Rishis, and all the metres, the word Om, the word VASHAT, the Mahavyahritis, the Savitri, the sacrifices, heaven and earth, the Nakshatras, the air, days and nights, the numbers, the twilights, the oceans, the rivers, the mountains, fields, herbs, trees, Gandharvas and Apsaras, the serpents, the birds, the Siddhas, the Sadhyas, the Vipras, the Yakshas, the Rakshas, the beings that have these (Rakshas, &c.) at their end, may satiate themselves. 'I satiate the Sruti; I satiate the Smriti; I satiate the firmness; I satiate the delight; I satiate the success; I satiate the thought; I satiate belief and insight, and the memory, cows and Brahmanas, movable and immovable things. All beings may satiate themselves!'--so far with the sacrificial cord suspended over the left shoulder.

4.10.e: Now with the sacrificial cord suspended over the right shoulder,
Looking in the direction that belongs to the Manes (i.e. the south):

4.10.s: śatarcinaḥ mādhyamāḥ gṛtsamadaḥ viśvāmitraḥ jamadagniḥ vāmadevaḥ atriḥ bharadvājaḥ vasiṣṭhaḥ pragāthāḥ pavamānāḥ kṣudra sūkta mahā sūktāḥ sumantuḥ jaimini vaiśampāyana paila sūtra bhāṣya gārgya babhru bābhravya maṇḍu māṇḍavyāḥ gārgi vācaknavī vaḍavā prātitheyī sulabhā maitreyī kaholam kauṣītakim mahā kauṣītakim suyajñam śāṅkhāyanam āśvalāyanam aitareyam mahā aitareyam bhāradvājam jātūkarṇyam paiṅgyam mahā paiṅgyam bāṣkalam gārgyam śakalya māṇḍūkeyam mahā damatram audavāhim mahā audavāhim sauyāmim śaunakim śāpa pūṇim gatamim ye ca anye ācāryās te sarve tṛpyantv iti |
4.10.d: शतर्चिनः माध्यमाः गृत्समदः विश्वामित्रः जमदग्निः वामदेवः अत्रिः भरद्वाजः वसिष्ठः प्रगाथाः पवमानाः क्षुद्र सूक्त महा सूक्ताः सुमन्तुः जैमिनि वैशम्पायन पैल सूत्र भाष्य गार्ग्य बभ्रु बाभ्रव्य मण्डु माण्डव्याः गार्गि वाचक्नवी वडवा प्रातिथेयी सुलभा मैत्रेयी कहोलम् कौषीतकिम् महा कौषीतकिम् सुयज्ञम् शाङ्खायनम् आश्वलायनम् ऐतरेयम् महा ऐतरेयम् भारद्वाजम् जातूकर्ण्यम् पैङ्ग्यम् महा पैङ्ग्यम् बाष्कलम् गार्ग्यम् शकल्य माण्डूकेयम् महा दमत्रम् औदवाहिम् महा औदवाहिम् सौयामिम् शौनकिम् शाप पूणिम् गतमिम् ये च अन्ये आचार्यास् ते सर्वे तृप्यन्त्व् इति ।
4.10.e: 'The (Rishis) of the hundred (Rikas), the (Rishis) of the middle (Mandalas), Gritsamada, Visvamitra, Gamadagni, Vamadeva, Atri, Bharadvaga, Vasishtha, the Pragathas, the (Rishis) of the Pavamana hymns, the (Rishis) of the short hymns and of the long hymns, Sumantu, Gaimini, Vaisampayana, Paila, the Sutras, the Bhashyas, Gargya, Babhru, Babhravya, Mandu, Mandavya, Gargi Vakaknavi, [paragraph continues] Vadava Pratitheyi, Sulabha Maitreyi (may satiate themselves). '(I satiate) Kahola Kaushitaki, Mahakaushitaki, Suyagna Sankhayana, Asvalayana, Aitareya, Mahaitareya, Bharadvaga, Gatukarnya, Paingya, Mahapangya, Bashkala, Gargya, Sakalya, Mandukeya, Mahadamatra, Audavahi, Mahaudavahi, Sauyami, Saunaki, Sakapuni, Gautami; and whatsoever other teachers there are, may they all satiate themselves.
'The ancestry of the father may satiate itself.
'The ancestry of the mother may satiate itself.'

4.11.s: na nagnām striyam īkṣeta anyatara maithunāt |
4.11.d: न नग्नाम् स्त्रियम् ईक्षेत अन्यतर मैथुनात् ।
4.11.e: Let him not look at a naked woman, except during sexual intercourse,
Nor (look) at the sun while it rises or sets,
At a person that has to touch dead bodies.
Let him not talk with a woman who has recently been confined or who has her courses,
Let him not eat food from which its strength is taken away.
Let him not do his work with implements wasted by use.
Let him not eat together (with his wife),

4.11.s: pitṛ devatā atithi bhṛtyānām śeṣam bhuñjīta |
4.11.d: पितृ देवता अतिथि भृत्यानाम् शेषम् भुञ्जीत ।
4.11.e: Remnants of (food belonging to the) Manes, gods, guests, and servants he may eat.

4.11.s: uñchaśilam ayācita rpatigrahaḥ sādhubhyo yācito vā yājanam vṛttiḥ |
4.11.d: उञ्छशिलम् अयाचित र्पतिग्रहः साधुभ्यो याचितो वा याजनम् वृत्तिः ।
4.11.e: Gleaning ears of corn, receiving alms unasked for, or for which he has asked the good, performing sacrifices for others, are the means of livelihood;
(Of these) each preceding one is the more respectable.
Let him not abandon his teacher,

4.12.e: Every day he shall respectfully salute his teacher,
And his Gurus,
A Srotriya when meeting him,
When he returns from a journey, (also) one who is not a Srotriya.

4.12.s: asāv aham bho ity ātmano nāma ādiśya vyatyasya pāṇī |
4.12.d: असाव् अहम् भो इत्य् आत्मनो नाम आदिश्य व्यत्यस्य पाणी ।
4.12.e: In the words, 'I am N.N., sir!' pronouncing his own name, crossing his hands (so as to seize with his right hand the right foot, and with his left hand the left of the other person).

4.12.s: asāv ity asya pāṇī saṃgṛhya āśiṣam āśāste |
4.12.d: असाव् इत्य् अस्य पाणी संगृह्य आशिषम् आशास्ते ।
4.12.e: (The person who has been thus saluted, in reply addressing him with his name,) 'N.N.!' and seizing his hands, pronounces a wish to him.
Let him not go to a sacrifice without being chosen (thereto).
And let him beware of (doing) wrong.
Let him not go to assemblies of people.
If he has come upon (such assemblies), let him not point out (anything evil) against (anybody).

4.12.s: anākrośako apiśunaḥ kulam kulo na atihetiḥ syāt |
4.12.d: अनाक्रोशको अपिशुनः कुलम् कुलो न अतिहेतिः स्यात् ।
4.12.e: He shall not be a reviler, nor slanderous, nor a wanderer from house to house, nor a prattler.
He shall not walk alone,
Nor naked,
Nor with veiled hands.
Gods'-houses (he shall walk round) keeping the right side turned to them.
Let him not run.
Let him not spit.
Let him not scratch himself.
Let him not look on urine and excrements.
Let him sit with veiled head,
Not on the bare (ground),

4.12.s: yady eka vastro yajña upavītam karṇe kṛtvā |
4.12.d: यद्य् एक वस्त्रो यज्ञ उपवीतम् कर्णे कृत्वा ।
4.12.e: If he has only one garment, suspending his sacrificial cord on his ear,
Not turning his face to the sun,
Nor his rump,

4.12.s: ahar udan mukho naktam dakṣiṇā mukhaḥ |
4.12.d: अहर् उदन् मुखो नक्तम् दक्षिणा मुखः ।
4.12.e: In the day-time with his face to the north, at night to the south.

4.12.s: na ca apsu śleṣma na ca samīpe |
4.12.d: न च अप्सु श्लेष्म न च समीपे ।
4.12.e: He shall not (eject) phlegm into water, nor in the neighbourhood (of water).
He shall not climb up a tree.
He shall not look down into a well.
He shall not go to an execution-place,
And in no case to a cemetery.
Let him bathe day by day with his clothes on.
When he has bathed, let him put on another garment before he is dry.

4.13.e: Under (the Nakshatra) Rohini he shall have the ploughing done.

4.13.s: purastāt karmaṇām prācyām kṣetra maryādāyām dyāvā pṛthivī balim hared |
4.13.d: पुरस्तात् कर्मणाम् प्राच्याम् क्षेत्र मर्यादायाम् द्यावा पृथिवी बलिम् हरेद् ।
4.13.e: Before it is done, he shall offer at the eastern boundary of his field a Bali to Heaven and Earth.

4.13.s: dyāvā pṛthivīyayā ṛcā namo dyāvā pṛthivībhyām iti ca upasthānam |
4.13.d: द्यावा पृथिवीयया ऋचा नमो द्यावा पृथिवीभ्याम् इति च उपस्थानम् ।
4.13.e: With a verse sacred to Heaven and Earth and with the words, 'Adoration to Heaven and Earth!' (he performs his) worship (to Heaven and Earth).

4.13.s: prathama prayoge sīrasya brāhmaṇaḥ sīram spṛśet śunam naḥ phālā iti etām anubruvan |
4.13.d: प्रथम प्रयोगे सीरस्य ब्राह्मणः सीरम् स्पृशेत् शुनम् नः फाला इति एताम् अनुब्रुवन् ।
4.13.e: When the plough is being put into motion first, let a Brahmana touch the plough reciting this (verse), 'For luck may us the plough-shares' (Rig-veda IV, 57, 8).

4.13.s: kṣetrasya patinā iti pradakṣiṇam patyṛcam pratidiśam upasthānam |
4.13.d: क्षेत्रस्य पतिना इति प्रदक्षिणम् पत्यृचम् प्रतिदिशम् उपस्थानम् ।
4.13.e: 'Through the lord of the field'--with (this hymn) (Rig-veda IV, 57), verse by verse, to the different directions (of the sky), from left to right, worship is done.

4.14.e: When going to cross water, he performs the Svastyayana (ceremony for lucky progress).

4.14.s: udaka añjalīṃs trīn apsu juhoti samudrāya vaiṇave namo varuṇāya dharma pataye namo namaḥ sarvābhyo nadībhyaḥ |
4.14.d: उदक अञ्जलींस् त्रीन् अप्सु जुहोति समुद्राय वैणवे नमो वरुणाय धर्म पतये नमो नमः सर्वाभ्यो नदीभ्यः ।
4.14.e: He sacrifices thrice with his joined hands full of water into the waters, with the words, 'Adoration to the Sea, the child of the reed! Adoration to Varuna, the lord of righteousness! Adoration to all rivers!'--

4.14.s: sarvāsām pitre viśva karmaṇe dattam havir juṣatām iti japitvā |
4.14.d: सर्वासाम् पित्रे विश्व कर्मणे दत्तम् हविर् जुषताम् इति जपित्वा ।
4.14.e: Murmuring, 'May Visvakarman, the father of them all, relish the food offered.'
Against the stream for flowing (waters); up into the air for standing ones.

4.14.s: taraṃś ced bhayam śaṅked vāsiṣṭham sūktam japet samudra jyeṣṭhā ity etat plavam |
4.14.d: तरंश् चेद् भयम् शङ्केद् वासिष्ठम् सूक्तम् जपेत् समुद्र ज्येष्ठा इत्य् एतत् प्लवम् ।
4.14.e: Should he while crossing apprehend any danger, let him murmur the hymn of Vasishtha, 'The eldest of which is the sea' (Rig-veda VII, 49); this (will serve to him as) a boat.

4.15.s: śravaṇam śraviṣṭhīyāyām paurṇamāsyām akṣata saktūnām sthālī pākasya vā juhoti |
4.15.d: श्रवणम् श्रविष्ठीयायाम् पौर्णमास्याम् अक्षत सक्तूनाम् स्थाली पाकस्य वा जुहोति ।
4.15.e: The Sravana (oblation) he offers on the full moon day that falls under (the Nakshatra) Sravishthas, of the flour of fried barley, or of cooked food,

4.15.s: viṣṇave svāhā śravaṇāya svāhā śrāvaṇyai paurṇamāsyai svāhā varṣābhyaḥ svāhā iti |
4.15.d: विष्णवे स्वाहा श्रवणाय स्वाहा श्रावण्यै पौर्णमास्यै स्वाहा वर्षाभ्यः स्वाहा इति ।
4.15.e: With (the words), 'To Vishnu svaha! To (the Nakshatra) Sravana svaha! To the full moon of Sravana svaha! To the rainy season svaha!'

4.15.s: gṛhyam agnim bāhyata upasamādhāya lājān akṣata saktūṃś ca sarpiṣā samninīya juhoti |
4.15.d: गृह्यम् अग्निम् बाह्यत उपसमाधाय लाजान् अक्षत सक्तूंश् च सर्पिषा सम्निनीय जुहोति ।
4.15.e: Having established the (sacred) domestic fire outside, and having mixed together fried grain and the flour of fried barley with butter, he sacrifices--

4.15.s: divyānām sarpāṇām adhipataye svāhā divyebhyaḥ sarpebhyaḥ svāhā iti |
4.15.d: दिव्यानाम् सर्पाणाम् अधिपतये स्वाहा दिव्येभ्यः सर्पेभ्यः स्वाहा इति ।
4.15.e: With (the words), 'To the Lord of the celestial Serpents svaha! To the celestial Serpents svaha!'

4.15.s: uttareṇa agnim prāg agreṣu naveṣu kuśeṣu uda kumbham navam pratiṣṭhāpya |
4.15.d: उत्तरेण अग्निम् प्राग् अग्रेषु नवेषु कुशेषु उद कुम्भम् नवम् प्रतिष्ठाप्य ।
4.15.e: Having placed to the north of the fire a new water-pot on eastward-pointed, fresh Kusa grass,

4.15.s: divyānām sarpāṇām adhipatir ava neniktām divyāḥ sarpā ava nenijatām ity apo ninayati |
4.15.d: दिव्यानाम् सर्पाणाम् अधिपतिर् अव नेनिक्ताम् दिव्याः सर्पा अव नेनिजताम् इत्य् अपो निनयति ।
4.15.e: With (the words), 'May the Lord of the celestial Serpents wash himself! May the celestial Serpents wash themselves!'--he pours water into it.

4.15.s: divyānām sarpāṇām adhipatiḥ pra likhatām divyāḥ sarpāḥ pra likhantām iti phaṇena ceṣṭayati |
4.15.d: दिव्यानाम् सर्पाणाम् अधिपतिः प्र लिखताम् दिव्याः सर्पाः प्र लिखन्ताम् इति फणेन चेष्टयति ।
4.15.e: With (the words), 'May the Lord of the celestial Serpents comb himself! May the celestial Serpents comb themselves!'--he makes movements with a comb.

4.15.s: divyānām sarpāṇām adhipatiḥ pra limpatām divyāḥ sarpāḥ pra limpantām iti varṇakasya mātrā ninayati |
4.15.d: दिव्यानाम् सर्पाणाम् अधिपतिः प्र लिम्पताम् दिव्याः सर्पाः प्र लिम्पन्ताम् इति वर्णकस्य मात्रा निनयति ।
4.15.e: With (the words), 'May the Lord of the celestial Serpents paint himself! May the celestial Serpents paint themselves!'--he pours out portions of paint.

4.15.s: divyānām sarpāṇām adhipatir ā badhnītām divyāḥ sarpā ā badhnatām iti sumanasa upaharati |
4.15.d: दिव्यानाम् सर्पाणाम् अधिपतिर् आ बध्नीताम् दिव्याः सर्पा आ बध्नताम् इति सुमनस उपहरति ।
4.15.e: With (the words), 'May the Lord of the celestial Serpents tie (this) to (himself)! May the celestial Serpents tie (this) to themselves!'--he offers flowers.

4.15.s: divyānām sarpāṇām adhipatir ā chādayatām divyāḥ sarpā ā chādayantām iti sūtra tantum upaharati |
4.15.d: दिव्यानाम् सर्पाणाम् अधिपतिर् आ छादयताम् दिव्याः सर्पा आ छादयन्ताम् इति सूत्र तन्तुम् उपहरति ।
4.15.e: With (the words), 'May the Lord of the celestial Serpents clothe himself! May the celestial Serpents clothe themselves!'--he offers a thread.

4.15.s: divyānām sarpāṇām adhipati āṅktām divyāḥ sarpā āñjatām iti kuśa taruṇena upaghātam āñjanasya karoti |
4.15.d: दिव्यानाम् सर्पाणाम् अधिपति आङ्क्ताम् दिव्याः सर्पा आञ्जताम् इति कुश तरुणेन उपघातम् आञ्जनस्य करोति ।
4.15.e: With (the words), 'May the Lord of the celestial Serpents anoint (his eyelashes)! May the celestial Serpents anoint (their eyelashes)!'--he spirts out (small portions of collyrium) with a young Kusa shoot.

4.15.s: divyānām sarpāṇām adhipatir īkṣatām divyāḥ sarpā īkṣantām ity āfarśena ākṣayati |
4.15.d: दिव्यानाम् सर्पाणाम् अधिपतिर् ईक्षताम् दिव्याः सर्पा ईक्षन्ताम् इत्य् आfअर्शेन आक्षयति ।
4.15.e: With (the words), 'May the Lori of the celestial Serpents look (at himself)! May the celestial Serpents look (at themselves)!'--he makes them look in a mirror.

4.15.s: divyānām sarpāṇām adhipata eṣa te balir divyāḥ sarpā eṣa vo balir iti balim upaharati |
4.15.d: दिव्यानाम् सर्पाणाम् अधिपत एष ते बलिर् दिव्याः सर्पा एष वो बलिर् इति बलिम् उपहरति ।
4.15.e: With (the words), 'Lord of the celestial Serpents, this is thy Bali! Celestial Serpents, this is your Bali!'--he makes a Bali-offering.

4.15.s: evam āntarikṣāṇām |
4.15.d: एवम् आन्तरिक्षाणाम् ।
4.15.e: In the same way for the aerial (Serpents).

4.15.s: diśyānām |
4.15.d: दिश्यानाम् ।
4.15.e: For those dwelling in the directions (of the horizon).

4.15.s: pārthivānām iti |
4.15.d: पार्थिवानाम् इति ।
4.15.e: For the terrestrial ones.

4.15.s: tris trir uccaistarām uccaistarām pūrvam |
4.15.d: त्रिस् त्रिर् उच्चैस्तराम् उच्चैस्तराम् पूर्वम् ।
4.15.e: (He repeats these Mantras) thrice each time, the first (part) with higher voice each time,

4.15.s: nīcaistarām nīcaistarām uttaram |
4.15.d: नीचैस्तराम् नीचैस्तराम् उत्तरम् ।
4.15.e: The second (part) with lower voice each time.

4.15.s: evam ahar ahar akṣata saktūnām darveṇa upaghātam ā pratyavarohaṇād rātrau vāg yataḥ sa udakam balim haret |
4.15.d: एवम् अहर् अहर् अक्षत सक्तूनाम् दर्वेण उपघातम् आ प्रत्यवरोहणाद् रात्रौ वाग् यतः स उदकम् बलिम् हरेत् ।
4.15.e: In this way he shall offer day by day with the spoon, in small portions, a Bali of the flour of fried barley with water, down to the Pratyavarohana (or the ceremony of the 'redescent'), at night, keeping silence.

4.15.s: vāg yatā ca enam upasādayed |
4.15.d: वाग् यता च एनम् उपसादयेद् ।
4.15.e: And (his wife) shall put (it) down silently.

4.15.s: ya upakramaḥ sa utsargaḥ |
4.15.d: य उपक्रमः स उत्सर्गः ।
4.15.e: The close of the ceremony is the same as the beginning.

4.15.s: sutrāmāṇam iti śayyām ārohet |
4.15.d: सुत्रामाणम् इति शय्याम् आरोहेत् ।
4.15.e: With (the verse), 'The good protectress' (Rig-veda X, 63, 10), let him ascend the (high) couch.

4.16.e: On the full moon day of Asvayuga a milk-rice oblation to Indra.

4.16.s: aśvibhyām svāhā aśvayugbhyām svāhā āśvayujyai paurṇamāsyai svāhā śarade svāhā paśupataye svāhā piṅgalāya svāhā ity ājyasya hutvā |
4.16.d: अश्विभ्याम् स्वाहा अश्वयुग्भ्याम् स्वाहा आश्वयुज्यै पौर्णमास्यै स्वाहा शरदे स्वाहा पशुपतये स्वाहा पिङ्गलाय स्वाहा इत्य् आज्यस्य हुत्वा ।
4.16.e: Having sacrificed Agya with (the words), 'To the two Asvins svaha! To the two Asvayug svaha! To the full moon of Asvayuga svaha! To the autumn svaha! To Pasupati svaha! To the tawny one svaha!'--

4.16.s: atha pṛṣātakasya ā gāvo agmann ity etena sūktena pratyṛcam juhuyāt |
4.16.d: अथ पृषातकस्य आ गावो अग्मन्न् इत्य् एतेन सूक्तेन प्रत्यृचम् जुहुयात् ।
4.16.e: He shall sacrifice a mixture of curds and butter with this hymn, 'The cows came hither' (Rig-veda VI, 28), verse by verse.
That night they let the calves join their mothers.

4.17.e: On the Agrahayani full moon day he shall redescend,
(Or) under (the Nakshatra) Rohini, or under the Proshthapadas.

4.17.s: prātaḥ śamī palāśa madhūka iṣīkā apāmārgāṇām śirīśa udumbara kuśa taruṇa badarīṇām ca pūrṇa muṣṭim ādāya śītā loṣṭam ca |
4.17.d: प्रातः शमी पलाश मधूक इषीका अपामार्गाणाम् शिरीश उदुम्बर कुश तरुण बदरीणाम् च पूर्ण मुष्टिम् आदाय शीता लोष्टम् च ।
4.17.e: In the morning, having taken a handfull of Sami leaves, Madhuka flowers, reeds, Apamarga plants, and of Sirisha, Udumbara, Kusa shoots, and jujube fruits, and an earth-clod (taken) out of a furrow,
Having put (all that) into a water-pot,

4.17.s: mahā vyāhṛtīḥ sāvitrīm ca uddrutya upa naḥ śośucad agham ity etena sūktena tasmin nimajjya nimajjya pradakṣiṇam śaraṇyebhyaḥ pāpmānam apahatya uttarato ninayet |
4.17.d: महा व्याहृतीः सावित्रीम् च उद्द्रुत्य उप नः शोशुचद् अघम् इत्य् एतेन सूक्तेन तस्मिन् निमज्ज्य निमज्ज्य प्रदक्षिणम् शरण्येभ्यः पाप्मानम् अपहत्य उत्तरतो निनयेत् ।
4.17.e: And, after he has quickly repeated the Mahavyahritis and the Savitri, having repeatedly immersed (it) therein with this hymn, 'May he burn away from us pain' (Rig-veda I, 97), he shall drive away the evil from the persons standing under his protection, from left to right, and pour out (the water) to the north.
A Madhuparka is the fee for the sacrifice.

4.18.s: grīṣmo hemanta uta vā vasantaḥ śarad varṣāḥ sukṛtam no astu | teṣām ṛtūnām śata śāradānām nivāta eṣām abhaya syāma svāhā apa śveta padā jahi pūrveṇa ca apareṇa ca | sapta ca vāruṇīr imāḥ sarvāś ca rāja bāndhavaiḥ svāhā śvetāya vaidārvāya svāhā vidārvāya svāhā takṣakāya vaiśāleyāya svāhā viśālāya svāhā ity ājyasya hutvā |
4.18.d: ग्रीष्मो हेमन्त उत वा वसन्तः शरद् वर्षाः सुकृतम् नो अस्तु । तेषाम् ऋतूनाम् शत शारदानाम् निवात एषाम् अभय स्याम स्वाहा अप श्वेत पदा जहि पूर्वेण च अपरेण च । सप्त च वारुणीर् इमाः सर्वाश् च राज बान्धवैः स्वाहा श्वेताय वैदार्वाय स्वाहा विदार्वाय स्वाहा तक्षकाय वैशालेयाय स्वाहा विशालाय स्वाहा इत्य् आज्यस्य हुत्वा ।
4.18.e: 'May summer, winter and spring, autumn and rainy season be well-ordered to us. May we be under the safe protection of these seasons, and may they last (to us) through a hundred years. Svaha! Beat away, O white one, with thy foot, with the forefoot and with the hind-foot, these seven daughters of Varuna and all that belong to the king's tribe. Svaha! 'To the white one, the son of Vidarva svaha! To Vidarva svaha! To Takshaka Vaisaleya svaha! To Visala svaha!'--with (these words) he sacrifices (oblations) of Agya.

4.18.s: suhemantaḥ suvasantaḥ sugrīṣmaḥ prati dhīyatām | suvarṣāḥ santu no varṣāḥ śaradaḥ śam bhavantu na iti |
4.18.d: सुहेमन्तः सुवसन्तः सुग्रीष्मः प्रति धीयताम् । सुवर्षाः सन्तु नो वर्षाः शरदः शम् भवन्तु न इति ।
4.18.e: 'May a good winter, a good spring, a good summer be bestowed (on us). May the rains be to us happy rains; may the autumns be blessed to us.'

4.18.s: śam no mitra iti palāśa śākhayā vimṛjya |
4.18.d: शम् नो मित्र इति पलाश शाखया विमृज्य ।
4.18.e: With (the verse), 'Blessing on us, Mitra' (Rig-veda I, 90, 9), he sweeps (the floor) with a Palasa branch,
Sprinkles (it with water) with (the verse), 'From the sea the wave' (Rig-veda IV, 58, 1),

4.18.s: syonā pṛthivi bhava iti srastaram āstīrya |
4.18.d: स्योना पृथिवि भव इति स्रस्तरम् आस्तीर्य ।
4.18.e: And spreads out a layer (of straw) with (the verse), 'Be soft, O earth' (Rig-veda I, 22, 15).
They then lie down on their sides, the eldest one to the right hand--

4.18.s: prati brahman prati tiṣṭhāmi kṣatra iti dakṣiṇaiḥ |
4.18.d: प्रति ब्रह्मन् प्रति तिष्ठामि क्षत्र इति दक्षिणैः ।
4.18.e: With (the words), 'In the Brahman I establish myself, in the Kshatra,' on (their) right (sides);

4.18.s: praty aśveṣu prati tiṣṭhāmi goṣv iti savyaiḥ |
4.18.d: प्रत्य् अश्वेषु प्रति तिष्ठामि गोष्व् इति सव्यैः ।
4.18.e: With (the words), 'Among the horses I establish myself, among the cows,' on (their) left (sides);

4.18.s: prati paśuṣu prati tiṣṭhāmi puṣtāv iti dakṣiṇaiḥ |
4.18.d: प्रति पशुषु प्रति तिष्ठामि पुष्ताव् इति दक्षिणैः ।
4.18.e: With (the words), 'Among the cattle I establish myself, in prosperity,' on (their) right (sides);

4.18.s: prati prajāyām prati tiṣṭhāmy anna iti savyaiḥ |
4.18.d: प्रति प्रजायाम् प्रति तिष्ठाम्य् अन्न इति सव्यैः ।
4.18.e: With (the words), 'Among offspring I establish myself, in food,' on (their) left (sides).
With (the verse), 'Arise, the living' (Rig-veda I, 113, 16), they arise.
During that night they lie on that layer.

4.19.e: On the full moon day of Kaitra,

4.19.s: karkandhu parṇāni mithunānām ca yathā upapādam piṣṭasya kṛtvā |
4.19.d: कर्कन्धु पर्णानि मिथुनानाम् च यथा उपपादम् पिष्टस्य कृत्वा ।
4.19.e: (Taking) jujube leaves, and making of meal (images) of couples of animals as it happens.
A figure with prominent navel to Indra and Agni.

4.19.s: lokato nakṣatrāṇy anvākṛtayaś ca lokato nakṣatrāṇy anvākṛtayaś ca |
4.19.d: लोकतो नक्षत्राण्य् अन्वाकृतयश् च लोकतो नक्षत्राण्य् अन्वाकृतयश् च ।
4.19.e: According to custom the Nakshatras and (their?) images (?). According to custom the Nakshatras and (their?) images (?). Here ends the Fourth Adhyaya.

5.1.s: atha pravatsyann ātmann araṇyoḥ samidhi vā agnim samārohayati |
5.1.d: अथ प्रवत्स्यन्न् आत्मन्न् अरण्योः समिधि वा अग्निम् समारोहयति ।
5.1.e: Now when he intends to set out on a journey, he makes (his sacred) fire enter into himself, (or) into the two kindling sticks, or into (an ordinary) log of wood,

5.1.s: ehi me prāṇān ā roha iti sakṛt sakṛn mantreṇa dvir-dvis tūṣṇīm |
5.1.d: एहि मे प्राणान् आ रोह इति सकृत् सकृन् मन्त्रेण द्विर्-द्विस् तूष्णीम् ।
5.1.e: Once with (the text), 'Come, enter into my Pranas,' twice silently.

5.1.s: ayam te yonir iti vā araṇī pratitapati |
5.1.d: अयम् ते योनिर् इति वा अरणी प्रतितपति ।
5.1.e: Or with (the verse), 'This is thy womb' (Rig-veda III, 29, to) he warms the two kindling sticks,
And before sunset the kindling (by attrition),
And at the time of the Vaisvadeva sacrifice.

5.1.s: upalipta uddhata avokṣite laukikam agnim āhṛtya upāvaroha ity upāvarohaṇam |
5.1.d: उपलिप्त उद्धत अवोक्षिते लौकिकम् अग्निम् आहृत्य उपावरोह इत्य् उपावरोहणम् ।
5.1.e: Having carried a common fire to a place that has been smeared (with cowdung), which is elevated, and which has been sprinkled (with water), he makes (the sacred fire) redescend (from its receptacle, with the formula), 'Redescend!'

5.1.s: anugate agnau sarva prāyaś citta āhutī hutvā pāhi no agna edhase svāhā pāhi no viśva vedase svāhā yajñam pāhi vibhāvaso svāhā sarvam pāhi śata krato svāhā iti |
5.1.d: अनुगते अग्नौ सर्व प्रायश् चित्त आहुती हुत्वा पाहि नो अग्न एधसे स्वाहा पाहि नो विश्व वेदसे स्वाहा यज्ञम् पाहि विभावसो स्वाहा सर्वम् पाहि शत क्रतो स्वाहा इति ।
5.1.e: If the fire goes out, he sacrifices the two Sarvaprayaskitta oblations (oblations for general expiation) and (other oblations) with (the formulas), 'Protect us, Agni, that we may prosper. Svaha! Protect us that we may obtain all wealth. Svaha! The sacrifice protect, O resplendent one! Svaha! Protect everything, O hundredfold wise one. Svaha!'

5.1.s: vrata hānā upoṣya ājyasya hutvā tvam agne vratapā iti |
5.1.d: व्रत हाना उपोष्य आज्यस्य हुत्वा त्वम् अग्ने व्रतपा इति ।
5.1.e: In the case of a breach of his vow let him fast and sacrifice (an oblation) of Agya with (the verse), 'Thou, Agni, art the lord of the vow' (Rig-veda VIII, 11, 1).

5.2.e: Now about (the consecration of) ponds, wells, and tanks.
In the bright fortnight, or on an auspicious Tithi,

5.2.s: tvam no agna iti dvābhyām ava te heḷa imam me varuna ud uttamam varuṇa imām dhiyam śikṣamāṇsya |
5.2.d: त्वम् नो अग्न इति द्वाभ्याम् अव ते हेऌअ इमम् मे वरुन उद् उत्तमम् वरुण इमाम् धियम् शिक्षमाण्स्य ।
5.2.e: He shall sacrifice with the two (verses), 'Thou hast us, Agni' (Rig-veda IV, 1, 4. 5), (and with the verses), 'We propitiate thy wrath' (I, 24, 14), 'This my prayer, Varuna' (I, 25, 19), 'Loosen the highest, Varuna' (I, 24, 15), 'This prayer of the man who exercises himself' (VIII, 42, 3),

5.2.s: gṛhyo apagṛhyo mayobhūr ākharo nikharo nihsaro nikāmaḥ sapatna dūṣaṇa iti vāruṇyā dik prabhṛti pradakṣiṇam juhuyāt |
5.2.d: गृह्यो अपगृह्यो मयोभूर् आखरो निखरो निह्सरो निकामः सपत्न दूषण इति वारुण्या दिक् प्रभृति प्रदक्षिणम् जुहुयात् ।

5.2.s: madhye payasā juhoti viśvataś cakṣur idam viṣṇur iti |
5.2.d: मध्ये पयसा जुहोति विश्वतश् चक्षुर् इदम् विष्णुर् इति ।

5.2.s: yat kim ca idam iti majjayitvā |
5.2.d: यत् किम् च इदम् इति मज्जयित्वा ।
5.2.e: Plunging (into the water) with (the verse), 'Whatever here' (Rig-veda VII, 89, 5).
A cow and a pair of clothes is the fee for the sacrifice.

5.3.e: Now at (the consecration of) a garden: having established the (sacred) fire (in that garden),
(And) having prepared a mess of cooked food,

5.3.s: viṣṇave svāhā indra agnibhyām svāhā viśva karmaṇe svāhā iti yān vo nara iti pratyṛcam juhuyād |
5.3.d: विष्णवे स्वाहा इन्द्र अग्निभ्याम् स्वाहा विश्व कर्मणे स्वाहा इति यान् वो नर इति प्रत्यृचम् जुहुयाद् ।
5.3.e: He shall sacrifice with (the formulas), 'To [paragraph continues] Vishnu svaha! To Indra and Agni svaha! To Visvakarman svaha!' (and with the verses), 'Whom the men' (Rig-veda III, 8, 6 seq.), verse by verse.

5.3.s: vanas pate śata valśa ity abhimantrya |
5.3.d: वनस् पते शत वल्श इत्य् अभिमन्त्र्य ।
5.3.e: He recites over (the garden), 'O tree with thy hundred branches' (Rig-veda III, 8, 11).
The fee for the sacrifice is gold.

5.4.s: yadi pārvaṇas tv akṛto anyataras tataś caruḥ |
5.4.d: यदि पार्वणस् त्व् अकृतो अन्यतरस् ततश् चरुः ।
5.4.e: Now if a half-monthly sacrifice has not been performed, one or the other of them, then a mess of rice (is to be offered as an expiation),

5.4.s: agnaye vaiśvānarāya svāhā agnaye tantumate svāhā iti |
5.4.d: अग्नये वैश्वानराय स्वाहा अग्नये तन्तुमते स्वाहा इति ।
5.4.e: With (the words), 'To Agni Vaisvanara svaha! To Agni Tantumat svaha!'
In the case of an intermission of the (morning or evening) oblations--
(He shall make expiatory oblations), in the evening with (the formula), 'Enlightener of the darkness, adoration! Svaha!'

5.4.s: prātaḥ prātar vastar namaḥ svāhā iti |
5.4.d: प्रातः प्रातर् वस्तर् नमः स्वाहा इति ।
5.4.e: In the morning with (the formula), 'Enlightener of the morning, adoration! Svaha!'

5.4.s: yāvanto homās tāvatīr hutvā pūrvavadd homaḥ |
5.4.d: यावन्तो होमास् तावतीर् हुत्वा पूर्ववद्द् होमः ।
5.4.e: After he has sacrificed as many oblations as there had been sacrifices (left out), the sacrifice (itself goes on) as (stated) above.

5.5.e: If a dove or an owl sits down (on his house),
Let him sacrifice with (the hymn), 'O gods, the dove' (Rig-veda X, 165), verse by verse.

5.5.s: duhsvapna darśane ca ariṣṭa darśane ca |
5.5.d: दुह्स्वप्न दर्शने च अरिष्ट दर्शने च ।
5.5.e: If he has seen a bad dream or an occurrence boding misfortune,
Or when the cawing of a crow is heard in (the dead of) night,
And in the case of other prodigies,
Let him cook rice-grains with milk,
With the milk of a cow that has a calf of the same colour (with her own),
But in no case of a black (cow),
And let him sacrifice with the night-hymn (Rig-veda X, 127), verse by verse.
Having eaten the remnants of those oblations with the Mahavyahritis,
And having recited over his ears (the verse), 'Blessing with our ears' (Rig-veda I, 89, 8),

5.5.s: śatam in nu śarado anti devā ity ātmānam abhimantrya |
5.5.d: शतम् इन् नु शरदो अन्ति देवा इत्य् आत्मानम् अभिमन्त्र्य ।
5.5.e: And over himself (the verse), 'May a hundred autumns be before us, ye gods' (ibid. 9),
He shall give something to the Brahmanas.

5.6.e: When a disease has befallen him,

5.6.s: imā rudrāya tavase kapardina iti pratyṛcam gāvedhukam carum juhuyāt |
5.6.d: इमा रुद्राय तवसे कपर्दिन इति प्रत्यृचम् गावेधुकम् चरुम् जुहुयात् ।
5.6.e: Let him offer boiled rice-grains with Gavedhuka-grass with (the hymn), 'These (prayers) to Rudra, the strong one, with braided hair' (Rig-veda I, 114), verse by verse.

5.7.e: If (his wife) gives birth to a child, without the Simantonnayana having been performed,
(Or if) the Gatakarman has not been performed (for the child),

5.7.s: tato atīte daśāha utsaṅge mātuḥ kumārakam sthāpayitvā |
5.7.d: ततो अतीते दशाह उत्सङ्गे मातुः कुमारकम् स्थापयित्वा ।
5.7.e: He places, when ten days have elapsed since (the delivery), the little child in the mother's lap,
And after he has sacrificed with the Mahavyahritis, the sacrifice (that had been omitted, is performed) as (stated) above.

5.8.e: If a post puts forth shoots,

5.8.s: sthālī pākam śrapayitvā ayā viṣṭhā janayan karvarāṇi piśaṅga rūpaḥ subharo vayodhā iti dvābhyām carum juhuyāt |
5.8.d: स्थाली पाकम् श्रपयित्वा अया विष्ठा जनयन् कर्वराणि पिशङ्ग रूपः सुभरो वयोधा इति द्वाभ्याम् चरुम् जुहुयात् ।
5.8.e: Let him prepare a mess of cooked food and offer the boiled rice with the two (verses), 'In that way bringing forth deeds' (Srauta-sutra III, 17, 1), 'Of tawny shape, weighty, a giver of vigour' (Rig-veda II, 3, 9). A

5.8.s: yadi praṇītā carur ājya sthāly anyad api mṛnmayam bhinnam sravet |
5.8.d: यदि प्रणीता चरुर् आज्य स्थाल्य् अन्यद् अपि मृन्मयम् भिन्नम् स्रवेत् ।
5.8.e: Should the pot for the Pranita water, the Agya- pot, any other earthen (vessel) be damaged and leak,

5.8.s: sarva prāyaś citta āhutī hutvā ya ṛte cid iti tṛcena bhinnam anumantrayate |
5.8.d: सर्व प्रायश् चित्त आहुती हुत्वा य ऋते चिद् इति तृचेन भिन्नम् अनुमन्त्रयते ।
5.8.e: He sacrifices the two Sarvaprayaskitta oblations and recites the three verses, 'He who without' (Rig-veda VIII, I, 12 seq.), over the broken (vessel).
Should the two (Kusa blades which are used as) strainers be spoiled before the completion of the sacrifice,

5.8.s: sarva prāyaś cittam hutvā apsv agna iti punar utpādayet |
5.8.d: सर्व प्रायश् चित्तम् हुत्वा अप्स्व् अग्न इति पुनर् उत्पादयेत् ।
5.8.e: Let him sacrifice the Sarvaprayaskitta and make new ones with (the verse), 'In the water, Agni' (Rig-veda VIII, 43, 9).

5.9.s: catvāry uda pātrāṇi pūrayitvā samanasaḥ pitaro yama rājye |
5.9.d: चत्वार्य् उद पात्राणि पूरयित्वा समनसः पितरो यम राज्ये ।

5.9.s: teṣām lokaḥ svadhā namo yajño deveṣu kalpatām ye samānāḥ samanaso jīvā jīveṣu māmakāḥ |
5.9.d: तेषाम् लोकः स्वधा नमो यज्ञो देवेषु कल्पताम् ये समानाः समनसो जीवा जीवेषु मामकाः ।

5.9.s: teṣām śrīr mayi kalpatām asmin loke śatam samāḥ samāno mantra iti dvābhyām ādyam piṇḍam triṣu vibhajet |
5.9.d: तेषाम् श्रीर् मयि कल्पताम् अस्मिन् लोके शतम् समाः समानो मन्त्र इति द्वाभ्याम् आद्यम् पिण्डम् त्रिषु विभजेत् ।

5.9.e: In the same way the vessels with Argha water.

5.9.s: evam mātur bhrātur bhāryāyāḥ pūrvamāriṇyā ebhiḥ piṇḍaiḥ prakṣipya |
5.9.d: एवम् मातुर् भ्रातुर् भार्यायाः पूर्वमारिण्या एभिः पिण्डैः प्रक्षिप्य ।
5.9.e: In the same way for the mother, for a brother, and for a wife that has died before (her husband), adding (the lump belonging to that person) to those (other) lumps.

5.10.e: If the bees make honey in his house,

5.10.s: upoṣyau audumbarīḥ samidho aṣṭa śatam dadhi madhu ghṛta aktā mā nas toka iti dvābhyām juhuyāt |
5.10.d: उपोष्यौ औदुम्बरीः समिधो अष्ट शतम् दधि मधु घृत अक्ता मा नस् तोक इति द्वाभ्याम् जुहुयात् ।
5.10.e: Let him fast and sacrifice a hundred and eight pieces of Udumbara wood, which are besmeared with curds, honey, and ghee, with the two (verses), 'No (harm) to us in our offspring' (Rig-veda I, 114, 8. 9).

5.10.s: śam no indra agnī iti ca sūktam japet sarveṣu ca karmasu pratiśruta ādiṣu |
5.10.d: शम् नो इन्द्र अग्नी इति च सूक्तम् जपेत् सर्वेषु च कर्मसु प्रतिश्रुत आदिषु ।
5.10.e: And let him murmur the hymn, 'For welfare may Indra and Agni' (Rig-veda VII, 35); and (the same hymn should be used) at all (ceremonies), such as that of the sacrifice after assent has been declared (see above, I, 7, 1).

5.10.s: prādeśa mātrīḥ pālāśīḥ samidhaḥ saptadaśa hutvā paścāt sruva grahaṇam |
5.10.d: प्रादेश मात्रीः पालाशीः समिधः सप्तदश हुत्वा पश्चात् स्रुव ग्रहणम् ।
5.10.e: After he has sacrificed seventeen one span long pieces of Palasa wood, he then seizes the Sruva.
Fifteen at the full and new moon sacrifices.

5.10.s: madhya āvarṣe aṣṭake tisro vā bhavanti pitṛ yajñavadd homaḥ |
5.10.d: मध्य आवर्षे अष्टके तिस्रो वा भवन्ति पितृ यज्ञवद्द् होमः ।
5.10.e: At the Ashtaka ceremony in the middle of the rainy season there may optionally be three (pieces of wood); the sacrifice as at the Pitriyagna.

5.11.s: yadi gṛhe valmīka sambhūtir gṛha utsargaḥ |
5.11.d: यदि गृहे वल्मीक सम्भूतिर् गृह उत्सर्गः ।
5.11.e: If an anthill arises in his house, the house should be abandoned.

5.11.s: atha trirātram upoṣya mahā śāntim kuryāt mahā śāntim kuryāt |
5.11.d: अथ त्रिरात्रम् उपोष्य महा शान्तिम् कुर्यात् महा शान्तिम् कुर्यात् ।
5.11.e: Then, after having fasted three nights (and days), he should perform the great expiation. Here ends the Fifth Adhyaya.

6.1.s: atha ato brahmāṇam brahmarṣim brahma yonim indram prajāpatim vasiṣṭham vāmadevam kaholam kauṣītakim mahā kauṣītakim suyajñam śāṅkhāyanam āśvalāyanam aitareyam mahā aitareyam kātyāyanam śāṭyāyanam śākalyam babhrum bābhravyam maṇḍum māṇḍavyam sarvān eva pūrva ācāryān namasya svādhyāya āraṇyakasya niyamān udāhariṣyāmaḥ |
6.1.d: अथ अतो ब्रह्माणम् ब्रह्मर्षिम् ब्रह्म योनिम् इन्द्रम् प्रजापतिम् वसिष्ठम् वामदेवम् कहोलम् कौषीतकिम् महा कौषीतकिम् सुयज्ञम् शाङ्खायनम् आश्वलायनम् ऐतरेयम् महा ऐतरेयम् कात्यायनम् शाट्यायनम् शाकल्यम् बभ्रुम् बाभ्रव्यम् मण्डुम् माण्डव्यम् सर्वान् एव पूर्व आचार्यान् नमस्य स्वाध्याय आरण्यकस्य नियमान् उदाहरिष्यामः ।
6.1.e: Now, after having paid reverence to Brahman, to the Brahmarishi, to (those who descend from) Brahman's womb, to Indra, Pragapati, Vasishtha, Vamadeva, Kahola Kaushitaki, Mahakaushitaki, Suyagna Sankhayana, Asvalayana, Aitareya, Mahaitareya, Katyayana, Satyayana, Sakalya, Babhru, Babhravya, Mandu, Mandavya, and to all the teachers of the past, we will henceforth explain the rules for the Aranyaka as forming the subject of Svadhyaya (private recitation of a text).

6.1.s: ahorātram brahmacaryam upetya ācāryo amāṃsa āśī |
6.1.d: अहोरात्रम् ब्रह्मचर्यम् उपेत्य आचार्यो अमांस आशी ।
6.1.e: The teacher abstains through one day and one night from sexual intercourse and from eating flesh.

6.1.s: āma piśitam caṇḍālam sūtikām rajasvalām tedany apahastaka darśanāny anadhyāyakāni |
6.1.d: आम पिशितम् चण्डालम् सूतिकाम् रजस्वलाम् तेदन्य् अपहस्तक दर्शनान्य् अनध्यायकानि ।
6.1.e: Raw flesh, a Kandala, a woman that has lately been confined, or that has her courses, seeing blood or persons whose hands have been cut off: (these persons and things he shall know form) impediments for the study.
Those which enter (their dens?) with the mouth first (?).
When he has vomited, or when his beard has been shaved,
When he has eaten flesh or partaken of a Sraddha or birth dinner,
During the days that immediately follow on (days of) study in the village,
Three nights (and days), if (he has been) put out of order,
(Or has been violently) seized by others,
And during the second half of the days that precede (?) the Parvan days,

6.1.s: agni vidyut stanayitnu varṣā mahā abhra prādurbhāvāc ca |
6.1.d: अग्नि विद्युत् स्तनयित्नु वर्षा महा अभ्र प्रादुर्भावाच् च ।
6.1.e: And if fire-flames, lightning, thunder, (heavy) rains, and great clouds appear,

6.1.s: vāte ca śarkara ākarṣiṇi yāvat kālam |
6.1.d: वाते च शर्कर आकर्षिणि यावत् कालम् ।
6.1.e: And if a storm (blows) that carries away pebbles, as long as that lasts. 2, 1. During four months after the full moon of Ashadha let him not study. 2 . Especially the Sakvari verses (are concerned by what has been declared). Such are the rules.

6.2.s: ūrdhvam āṣāḍhyāś caturo māsān na adhīyīta |
6.2.d: ऊर्ध्वम् आषाढ्याश् चतुरो मासान् न अधीयीत ।

6.2.s: prāg jyotiṣam aparājitāyām diśi puṇyam upagamya deśam |
6.2.d: प्राग् ज्योतिषम् अपराजितायाम् दिशि पुण्यम् उपगम्य देशम् ।

6.2.s: maṇḍala praveśaś ca añjana gandhim ity etayā ṛcā |
6.2.d: मण्डल प्रवेशश् च अञ्जन गन्धिम् इत्य् एतया ऋचा ।

6.2.s: maṇḍalam tu prāg dvāram udag dvāram vā ajanāgrīyam asampramāṇam asambādham |
6.2.d: मण्डलम् तु प्राग् द्वारम् उदग् द्वारम् वा अजनाग्रीयम् असम्प्रमाणम् असम्बाधम् ।

6.2.e: The final expiation (should extend) to the Vamadevya.
And the invitation to resume the recitation (is done in the following way)
After they have sipped water that stands outside the circle,
Let them resume the recitation, having performed the expiation.

6.2.s: śānti pātra upaghāte prokṣaṇam prāyaś cittiḥ |
6.2.d: शान्ति पात्र उपघाते प्रोक्षणम् प्रायश् चित्तिः ।
6.2.e: If the vessel used in the expiation is damaged, sprinkling (with water forms) the expiatory act (to be performed for it).

6.2.s: prokṣaṇam tu hiraṇyavatā pāṇinā darbha piñjūlavatā vā |
6.2.d: प्रोक्षणम् तु हिरण्यवता पाणिना दर्भ पिञ्जूलवता वा ।
6.2.e: (That) sprinkling, however, (one should perform) holding gold or a bunch of Darbha grass in his hand.
So far what pertains to the general rules.

6.3.e: Now after they have entered the circle--

6.3.s: prān mukha ācārya upaviśaty udan mukhā dakṣiṇata itare yathā pradhānam |
6.3.d: प्रान् मुख आचार्य उपविशत्य् उदन् मुखा दक्षिणत इतरे यथा प्रधानम् ।
6.3.e: The teacher sits down with his face to the east, the others, according to their rank, (sit down) towards the south, with their faces to the north.
If that is impossible, with their faces to all directions.
Let them expect the rising of the sun,
And when they behold it in its splendour,

6.3.s: adhīhi bho iti dakṣiṇair dakṣiṇam savyaiḥ savyam dakṣiṇa uttaraiḥ pāṇibhir upasaṃgṛhya pādāv ācāryasya nirṇiktau |
6.3.d: अधीहि भो इति दक्षिणैर् दक्षिणम् सव्यैः सव्यम् दक्षिण उत्तरैः पाणिभिर् उपसंगृह्य पादाव् आचार्यस्य निर्णिक्तौ ।
6.3.e: Let them with (the words), 'Recite, sir!' seize with their hands, holding the right hand uppermost, the feet of the teacher, which have been washed, with the right (hand) the right (foot), with the left the left,

6.3.s: atha ādhāya śānti pātre dūrvā kāṇḍavatīṣv apsv apinvamānaiḥ pāṇibhiḥ prādhīyīran |
6.3.d: अथ आधाय शान्ति पात्रे दूर्वा काण्डवतीष्व् अप्स्व् अपिन्वमानैः पाणिभिः प्राधीयीरन् ।
6.3.e: And having then put (the hands) into the vessel used for the expiation, into water in which pieces of Durva stalks are, let them begin their study, when their hands have ceased to drip.

6.3.s: eṣa vidhirṇyadi tu glāyerann eka eṣām aśūnyam śānti bhājanam kuryād |
6.3.d: एष विधिर्ण्यदि तु ग्लायेरन्न् एक एषाम् अशून्यम् शान्ति भाजनम् कुर्याद् ।
6.3.e: This is the rite. But when they are tired, let one of them bring it about that the vessel used for the expiation be not empty.
And all (should do so) at the beginning and the end of (each) Adhyaya.
(All) that is done continuously, without interruption.

6.3.s: om kāro mahā vyāhṛtayaḥ sāvitrī rathantaram bṛhad vāmadevyam punar ādāyam kakup kāram iti bṛhad rathantare |
6.3.d: ओम् कारो महा व्याहृतयः सावित्री रथन्तरम् बृहद् वामदेव्यम् पुनर् आदायम् ककुप् कारम् इति बृहद् रथन्तरे ।
6.3.e: The syllable OM, the Mahavyahritis, the Savitri, the Rathantara, the Brihat, the Vamadevya; Brihat and Rathantara with repetition and Kakubh-forming.
These (holy words and verses) are (thus) made to attain (the number of) ten.

6.3.s: daśa daśiṇī virāḍ ity etad brāhmaṇam |
6.3.d: दश दशिणी विराड् इत्य् एतद् ब्राह्मणम् ।
6.3.e: 'Of decades consists the Virag'--thus says the Brahmana.

6.4.s: adabdham mana iṣiram cakṣuḥ sūryo jyotiṣām śreṣṭho dīkṣe mā mā hiṃsīr iti savitārma īkṣante |
6.4.d: अदब्धम् मन इषिरम् चक्षुः सूर्यो ज्योतिषाम् श्रेष्ठो दीक्षे मा मा हिंसीर् इति सवितार्म ईक्षन्ते ।
6.4.e: 'Unerring mind, vigorous eye (is) the sun, the noblest of the stars. Inauguration, do no harm to me!'--with (these words) they look at Savitri (I.e. the sun).

6.4.s: yuvam surāmam ity ekā svasti naḥ pathyāsv iti ca tisra iti mahā vratasya |
6.4.d: युवम् सुरामम् इत्य् एका स्वस्ति नः पथ्यास्व् इति च तिस्र इति महा व्रतस्य ।
6.4.e: One (verse), 'You both the gladdening one' (Rig-veda X, 131, 4), and the three (verses), 'Blessing to us on the paths' (Rig-veda X, 63, 15-17) (are to be repeated before the recitation) of the Mahavrata (chapter).
But (at that) of the Sakvari (verses) before (the formula mentioned in the first Sara):

6.4.s: praty asmai pipīṣate yo rayivo rayitamas tyam u vo aprahaṇam iti trayas tṛcāḥ asmā asmā id andhasa ity evā hy asi vīrayur ity abhitaḥ śakvarīṇām |
6.4.d: प्रत्य् अस्मै पिपीषते यो रयिवो रयितमस् त्यम् उ वो अप्रहणम् इति त्रयस् तृचाः अस्मा अस्मा इद् अन्धस इत्य् एवा ह्य् असि वीरयुर् इत्य् अभितः शक्वरीणाम् ।
6.4.e: The three Trikas, 'To him, the thirsty one' (Rig-veda VI, 42, 1-3), 'The wealthiest (Soma), O wealthy one' (VI, 44, 1-3), 'Him who does no harm to you' (VI, 44, 4-6), (the verse), 'To him, to him the sap of the herb' (VI, 42, 4), (and the verse), "Verily thou art a hero' (VIII, 81, 28)--thus for the Sakvari (verses) before and afterwards.
The same (recitation) as for the Mahavrata.

6.4.s: saṃhitānām tu pūrvam ṛtam vadiṣyāmi satyam vadiṣyāmi iti viśeṣaḥ |
6.4.d: संहितानाम् तु पूर्वम् ऋतम् वदिष्यामि सत्यम् वदिष्यामि इति विशेषः ।
6.4.e: For the Samhitas, however, before (the text given in the first Sutra the formula has to be recited), 'I shall speak right, I shall speak truth (&c.)'--this is the difference (in the case of the Samhitas).

6.4.s: atha manthasya tat savitur vṛṇīmahe tat savitur vareṇyam iti pūrve ca |
6.4.d: अथ मन्थस्य तत् सवितुर् वृणीमहे तत् सवितुर् वरेण्यम् इति पूर्वे च ।

6.4.s: adabdham mana ity ādhikārikāḥ śāntayas tataḥ |
6.4.d: अदब्धम् मन इत्य् आधिकारिकाः शान्तयस् ततः ।

6.4.s: ud itaḥ śukriyam dadha ity ādityam īkṣante |
6.4.d: उद् इतः शुक्रियम् दध इत्य् आदित्यम् ईक्षन्ते ।

6.5.s: tam aham ātmani ity ātmānam abhinihitam trir hitam |
6.5.d: तम् अहम् आत्मनि इत्य् आत्मानम् अभिनिहितम् त्रिर् हितम् ।

6.5.s: upa mā śrīr juṣatām upa yaśo anu mā śrīr juṣatām anu yaśaḥ |
6.5.d: उप मा श्रीर् जुषताम् उप यशो अनु मा श्रीर् जुषताम् अनु यशः ।

6.5.s: sa indraḥ sagaṇaḥ sabalaḥ sayaśaḥ savīrya ut tiṣṭhāṇi ity uttiṣṭhati |
6.5.d: स इन्द्रः सगणः सबलः सयशः सवीर्य उत् तिष्ठाणि इत्य् उत्तिष्ठति ।

6.5.s: śrīr mā ut tiṣṭhantu yaśo mā ut tiṣṭhatv ity utthāya |
6.5.d: श्रीर् मा उत् तिष्ठन्तु यशो मा उत् तिष्ठत्व् इत्य् उत्थाय ।

6.5.s: idam aham dviṣantam bhrātṛvyam pāpmānam alakṣmīm ca apa dhunomi iti vastra antam avadhūya |
6.5.d: इदम् अहम् द्विषन्तम् भ्रातृव्यम् पाप्मानम् अलक्ष्मीम् च अप धुनोमि इति वस्त्र अन्तम् अवधूय ।

6.5.s: apa prāca it sūktam indraś ca mṛlayāti na iti dve yata indra bhayāmaha ity ekā śāsa itthā mahān asi iti prācīm svastidā iti dakṣiṇām dakṣiṇāvṛto virakṣa iti pratīcīm vi na indra ity udīcīm savya āvṛto apa indra iti dakṣiṇa āvṛto divam udīkṣante |
6.5.d: अप प्राच इत् सूक्तम् इन्द्रश् च मृलयाति न इति द्वे यत इन्द्र भयामह इत्य् एका शास इत्था महान् असि इति प्राचीम् स्वस्तिदा इति दक्षिणाम् दक्षिणावृतो विरक्ष इति प्रतीचीम् वि न इन्द्र इत्य् उदीचीम् सव्य आवृतो अप इन्द्र इति दक्षिण आवृतो दिवम् उदीक्षन्ते ।

6.6.s: savitā paścātāt tac cakṣur ity ādityam upasthāya |
6.6.d: सविता पश्चातात् तच् चक्षुर् इत्य् आदित्यम् उपस्थाय ।
6.6.e: Having worshipped the Sun with (the verses), 'Savitri from the west,' 'This eye' (Rig-veda X, 36, 14; VII, 66, 16),
They turn away, come back, sit down.

6.6.s: yathā apaḥ śāntā iti śānti pātrād apa ādāya |
6.6.d: यथा अपः शान्ता इति शान्ति पात्राद् अप आदाय ।
6.6.e: With (the words), 'As the water is appeased'--they draw water out of the vessel used for the expiation,
Pour it out on the ground,
Spread (some) of that (water over the ground) with (the words), 'As the earth (is appeased),'--

6.6.s: evam mayi śāmyatv iti dakṣiṇe aṃse nilimpati |
6.6.d: एवम् मयि शाम्यत्व् इति दक्षिणे अंसे निलिम्पति ।
6.6.e: He (then) smears it on his right shoulder with (the words), 'Thus may peace dwell in me.'
In the same way a second time.
In the same way a third time.

6.6.s: kāṇḍāt kāṇḍāt sam bhavasi kāṇḍāt kāṇḍāt pra rohasi śivā naḥ śāle bhava iti dūrvā kāṇḍam ādāya mūrdhani kṛtvā |
6.6.d: काण्डात् काण्डात् सम् भवसि काण्डात् काण्डात् प्र रोहसि शिवा नः शाले भव इति दूर्वा काण्डम् आदाय मूर्धनि कृत्वा ।
6.6.e: 'Piece by piece thou art produced; piece by piece thou risest up; bring welfare to us, O house!'--with (this text they) take pieces of Durva stalks (out of the vessel of water), put them on their heads,

6.6.s: agnis tṛpyatu vāyus tṛpyatu sūryas tṛpyatu viṣṇus tṛpyatu prajāpatis tṛpyatu virūpa akśas tṛpyatu sahasra akṣas tṛpyatu sarva bhūtāni tṛpyantv iti |
6.6.d: अग्निस् तृप्यतु वायुस् तृप्यतु सूर्यस् तृप्यतु विष्णुस् तृप्यतु प्रजापतिस् तृप्यतु विरूप अक्शस् तृप्यतु सहस्र अक्षस् तृप्यतु सर्व भूतानि तृप्यन्त्व् इति ।
6.6.e: (And make water-offerings with the formulas), 'May Agni satiate himself; may Vayu satiate himself; may Surya satiate himself; may Vishnu satiate himself; may Pragapati satiate himself; may Virupaksha satiate himself; may Sahasraksha satiate himself; may all beings satiate themselves.'

6.6.s: sumantu jaimini vaiśampāyana paila ādy ācāryāḥ |
6.6.d: सुमन्तु जैमिनि वैशम्पायन पैल आद्य् आचार्याः ।
6.6.e: (Then) Sumantu, Gaimini, Vaisampayana, Paila, and the other teachers (receive their offerings).
(Then) every one (worships in the same way) his fathers.
With (the text), 'To the sea you' (Sraut. IV, 11, 11) they pour out the water,
And separate according to their pleasure.

6.6.s: yathā āgama prajñā śruti smṛti vibhavād anukrāntamānād avivāda pratiṣṭhād abhayam śam bhave no astu namo astu devarṣi pitṛ manuṣyebhyaḥ śivam āyur vapur anāmayam śāntim ariṣṭim akṣitim ojas tejo yaśo balam brahma varcasam kīrtim āyuḥ prajām paśūn namo namas kṛtā vardhayantu duṣṭutād durupayuktān nyūna adhikāś ca sarvasmāt svasti devarṣibhyaś ca brahma satyam ca pātu mām iti brahma satya ca pātu mām iti |
6.6.d: यथा आगम प्रज्ञा श्रुति स्मृति विभवाद् अनुक्रान्तमानाद् अविवाद प्रतिष्ठाद् अभयम् शम् भवे नो अस्तु नमो अस्तु देवर्षि पितृ मनुष्येभ्यः शिवम् आयुर् वपुर् अनामयम् शान्तिम् अरिष्टिम् अक्षितिम् ओजस् तेजो यशो बलम् ब्रह्म वर्चसम् कीर्तिम् आयुः प्रजाम् पशून् नमो नमस् कृता वर्धयन्तु दुष्टुताद् दुरुपयुक्तान् न्यून अधिकाश् च सर्वस्मात् स्वस्ति देवर्षिभ्यश् च ब्रह्म सत्यम् च पातु माम् इति ब्रह्म सत्य च पातु माम् इति ।
6.6.e: (The final benedictory formula runs thus), 'Through the power of wisdom, of Sruti and Smriti, as handed down by tradition, through (that power) which has its measure in (the Vedic texts) that have been gone through(?), and which is possessed of undisputed firmness, may peace be with us in welfare. Adoration be to gods, Rishis, Manes, and men! May they whom we have adored, make happy life, beauty, health, peace, incolumity, imperishableness, vigour, splendour, glory, power, holy lustre, renown, age, offspring, cattle, adoration, increase. From wrongly spoken, wrongly used (prayer), from everything that is deficient or excessive, for the good of gods and Rishis, may the Brahman and Truth protect me; may the Brahman and Truth protect me!'
